4:92: God Almighty says: It is not permissible for a believer to kill his believing brother in any way, and as it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Masoud: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God is not permissible to be shed except in one of three cases: a life for a life, a married man who commits adultery, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community.” Then if one of these three occurs, then no one among the people has the right to kill him, and that is only up to the Imam or his deputies. And his saying: Except by mistake, they said: It is an isolated exception, like the poet’s saying: The eggs did not travel far and did not step on the ground except to tie a cold deportation There are many evidences for this. There is disagreement about the reason for the revelation of this verse. Mujahid and more than one person said: It was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah, the brother of Abu Jahl on his mother’s side, Asma bint Makhrama. He killed a man who was torturing him with his brother for Islam, and he was Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Ghamidi. Ayyash harbored evil against him, so that man converted to Islam and emigrated, and Ayyash did not know. When the day of the conquest came, he saw him and thought that he was of his religion, so he attacked him and killed him. Then God revealed this verse. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: It was revealed about Abu Darda’ because he killed a man who had said the word of faith when he raised his sword against him, so he struck him and said his word. When that was mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: He only said it seeking refuge. So he said to him: Did you split his heart open? This story is in Sahih, and it is not from Abu Darda’. And his saying: And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave and the blood money to be paid to his family These are two obligations in killing by mistake, one of them is expiation for the great sin committed even if it was by mistake, and one of its conditions is that it be the freeing of a believing slave, so a disbelieving slave is not sufficient. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Al-Hasan Al-Basri that they said: A minor does not suffice unless he intends to believe. And it was narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, who said: In a letter, then the freeing of a believing slave is not sufficient for a boy. Ibn Jarir chose that if he was born to Muslim parents, it is sufficient, otherwise it is not. And what the majority are upon is that whenever he is a Muslim, his freeing is valid for expiation, whether he is a minor or an adult. Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Razzaq informed us, Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of a man from the Ansar: That he came with a black slave girl and said: O Messenger of God, I have to free a believing slave, so if I am… You see this believing woman whom I freed, so the Messenger of God said to her: Do you bear witness that there is no god but God? She said: Yes. He said: Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? She said: Yes. He said: Do you believe in resurrection after death? She said: Yes. He said: Free her. This is a sound chain of transmission, and the ignorance of the companion does not harm it. In the Muwatta of Malik, the Musnad of Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud, and An-Nasa’i, on the authority of Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Al-Hakam: When he brought that black slave girl, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Where is God? She said: In the sky. He said: Who am I? She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Free her, for she is a believer. His saying: And a blood money to be paid to his family is the second obligation between the killer and the family of the murdered person, as compensation for what they have lost of their dead. This blood money is only due in fifths, as narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunan from the hadith of Al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, on the authority of Zayd ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Khafs ibn Malik, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding the blood money for accidental killing: twenty young female camels, twenty young male camels, twenty one-year-old female camels, twenty two-year-old female camels, and twenty three-year-old female camels. The wording of An-Nasa’i is: Al-Tirmidhi: We do not know it as being raised except from this source, and it has been narrated from Abdullah as a narration from Ali and a group, and it has been said: It must be divided into fourths, and this blood money is on the agnates, not from his wealth. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: I do not know of anyone who disagreed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the blood money is on the agnates, and this is more than one hadith of the elite. What he referred to, may God have mercy on him, has been proven in more than one hadith, including what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Two women from Hudhayl fought, and one of them threw a stone at the other, killing her and what was in her womb. They disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ruled that the blood money for her fetus is the blood money of a male or female slave, and he ruled that the blood money for the woman is on her agnates. This requires that the ruling on pure intentional error is the obligation of blood money, but in this case the blood money must be divided into thirds due to the suspicion of intentional murder. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid bin Al-Walid to Banu Juthaymah and called them to Islam, but they did not know how to do so. They said, We have converted to Islam. So they began to say, We have converted to Islam. So Khalid began to kill them. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he raised his hands and said, O God, I disavow before You what Khalid did. He sent Ali to pay the blood money for their dead and for whatever he had destroyed of their property, even the saliva of a dog. From this hadith it is understood that the mistake of the imam or his deputy is in the public treasury. And his saying: unless they give in charity means that the blood money must be paid to his family unless they give it in charity, in which case it is not obligatory. And his saying: But if he is from a people who are enemies to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave means that if the one killed is a believer but his relatives are from the infidels who are at war, then there is no blood money for them, and the killer must free a believing slave and nothing else. And his saying: But if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty the verse means that if the relatives of the one killed are people of protection or a truce, then they are entitled to the blood money of their victim, and if he is a believer, then the full blood money is due, and likewise if he is a disbeliever also according to a group of scholars. And it was said: Half of the blood money of the Muslim is due for the disbeliever, and it was said: a third of it, as is detailed in the Book of Rulings. And the killer must also free a believing slave. But whoever cannot find [a slave], then he must fast for two consecutive months means that he does not break his fast between them, but rather he should continue their fasting until the end of them. If he breaks his fast without an excuse such as sickness, menstruation, or childbirth, he should start over. And they differed regarding travel, whether it should be interrupted or not, based on Two sayings, and his saying: Repentance from God, and God is Knowing and Wise meaning this is the repentance of the murderer by mistake if he does not find a manumission, he fasts two consecutive months, and they differed about the one who is unable to fast, is it obligatory for him to feed sixty poor people as in the expiation for zihar, according to two sayings, one of them: Yes, as is stated in the expiation for zihar, and it was not mentioned here, because this is a place of threat, intimidation and warning, so it is not appropriate to mention feeding in it because of what is in it of facilitation and permission, and the second saying is that it is not switched to food, because if it was obligatory, he would not have delayed explaining it from the time of need and God is Knowing and Wise its interpretation has been presented more than once, Then, when the Almighty explained the ruling on accidental killing, He proceeded to explain the ruling on premeditated killing, saying: And whoever kills a believer intentionally verse. This is a severe threat and a definite warning to whoever commits this great sin, which is linked to associating partners with God in more than one verse in the Book of God, where the Almighty says in Surat al-Furqan 25:And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right verse. And the Almighty said: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him” verse. And the verses and hadiths prohibiting killing are very many, including what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first thing that will be judged between people on the Day of Resurrection will be blood. And in another hadith narrated by Abu Dawud on the authority of Amr ibn al-Walid ibn Abdah al-Masri on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The believer will continue to be righteous as long as he does not shed unlawful blood. But if he sheds unlawful blood, he will be saved.” And in another hadith The destruction of the world is easier in the sight of God than the killing of a Muslim man, and in another hadith, “Whoever helps in killing a Muslim, even with half a word, will come on the Day of Resurrection with it written between his eYa-Sin 36:Despairing of the mercy of God.” Ibn Abbas believed that there is no repentance for the one who intentionally kills a believer. Al-Bukhari said: Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Al-Nu’man told us, he said: I heard Ibn Jubayr say: The people of Kufa differed about it, so I traveled to Ibn Abbas and asked him about it, and he said: This verse was revealed, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, it is the last to be revealed, and nothing abrogated it. This is how he also narrated it, as did Muslim and Al-Nasa’i through various chains of transmission on the authority of Shu’bah. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hanbal on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mughirah ibn Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, and he said: Nothing abrogated it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Awn told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the statement of God, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, the verse, he said: Nothing abrogated it. And he said about this verse, And those who do not invoke with God another deity, to the end of it, he said: It was revealed about the polytheists. Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Mansur, Sa’id ibn Jubayr told me or al-Hakam told me on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, he said: If a man knows Islam and the laws of Islam, then he kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell and there is no repentance for him. So I mentioned that to Mujahid and he said: Except for the one who regrets. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Yahya al-Jaber on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said: We were with Ibn Abbas after he had lost his sight, when a man came to him and called out: O Abdullah ibn Abbas, what do you think of a man who intentionally killed a believer? He said: His recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and God is angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment. He said: What if he repents and does righteous deeds, then is guided? Ibn Abbas said: May his mother be bereaved of him, how can he repent and be guided? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “May his mother be bereaved of him, he who intentionally kills a believer will come on the Day of Resurrection taking him by his right hand or his left, his jugular veins gushing out from before the Throne of the Most Merciful. He will hold his killer with his left hand and with his other hand his head, saying: ‘O Lord, ask this man why he killed me.’” By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Abdullah, this verse was revealed and no verse abrogated it until your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, and no proof was revealed after it. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, I heard Yahya ibn al-Mujbir narrating on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to him and said: ‘What do you think of a man who intentionally kills another man?’ He said: ‘His recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever,’ the verse. He said: ‘It was revealed among the last to be revealed, and nothing abrogated it until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, and no revelation was revealed after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that said: ‘What do you think if he repents, believes, does righteous deeds, then is guided?’ He said: How can he repent, when I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “May his mother be bereaved of a man who kills a man intentionally. He will come on the Day of Resurrection seizing his killer by his right or his left hand - or seizing his head by his right or his left hand - his veins gushing with blood from the direction of the Throne, saying: O Lord, ask your servant why he killed me.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ammar al-Dahni, Yahya al-Jaber, and Thabit al-Thamali, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. This has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas through many chains of narration, and among those who held that there is no repentance for him from the Salaf are Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Hurayrah, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, Ubayd ibn Umair, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim. There are many hadiths on this topic, including what Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh al-Hafiz narrated in his Tafsir: Dulaj told us. Ibn Ahmad, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Saeed Al-Bushanji H narrated to us, and Abdullah ibn Jaafar narrated to us, and Ibrahim ibn Fahd narrated to us, they said: Ubaid ibn Ubaidah narrated to us, Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Amr ibn Shurahbil, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The one who was killed will come clinging to his killer on the Day of Resurrection, holding his head with his other hand, and he will say: ‘O Lord, ask this one why he killed me?’ He will say: ‘I killed him so that honor would be for You.’ He will say: ‘Then it is mine.’ He said: And another will come clinging to his killer and say: ‘O Lord, ask this one why he killed me.’ He will say: ‘I killed him so that honor would be for so-and-so.’ He will say: ‘Then he has no share in his sin.’ He said: ‘Then he will fall into the Fire for seventy autumns.’” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Al-Mustamir Al-Awfi, on the authority of Amr ibn Asim, on the authority of Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Safwan bin Isa told us, Thawr bin Yazid told us on the authority of Abu Awn, on the authority of Abu Idris, who said: I heard Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God may forgive every sin except for a man who dies as a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer intentionally. And this is how al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Muthanna, on the authority of Safwan bin Isa, and Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Ja’far told us, Samuyah told us, Abdul A’la bin Musahhir told us, Sadaqah bin Khalid told us, Khalid bin Dahqan told us, Ibn Abi Zakariya told us, he said: I heard Umm al-Darda’ say: I heard Abu al-Darda’ say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God may forgive every sin except for a man who dies as a polytheist, or a man who kills a believer intentionally. This is very strange from this aspect, and the preserved hadith of Muawiyah mentioned above, and God knows best. Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Baqiyyah bin al-Waleed on the authority of Nafi’ bin Yazid: Ibn Jubayr told me. Al-Ansari narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever kills a believer intentionally has disbelieved in God Almighty. This is also a strange hadith, as its chain of transmission has been greatly criticized. Imam Ahmad said: An-Nadr narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Aaliyah came to me and a friend of mine, and he said to us: Come, for you are younger than me and more knowledgeable of hadith than me. So he went with us to Bishr ibn Asim, and Abu al-Aaliyah said to him: Tell these people your hadith. So he said: Uqbah ibn Malik al-Laythi narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a raiding party that raided a people, and a man went with the people, and a man from the raiding party followed him, brandishing his sword. The one who went with the man said: I am a Muslim, but he did not consider what he said. So he struck him and killed him. The hadith reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said a harsh word about it, and the killer was informed. While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon, the killer said: By God, he did not say what he said except… Seeking refuge from being killed, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him and from the people before him and began his sermon, then he said again: O Messenger of God, he did not say what he said except to seek refuge from being killed, so he turned away from him and from the people before him and began his sermon, then he did not wait until he said the third time: By God, O Messenger of God, he did not say what he said except to seek refuge from being killed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to him and you could see the displeasure on his face, and he said: God has refused to do with whoever kills a believer three times. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, and what the majority of the predecessors and successors of the Ummah are upon is that the killer has repentance between him and God, the Almighty, the Majestic, so if he repents and returns, and is humble and submissive and does a righteous deed, God will replace his bad deeds with good deeds, and compensate the one who was killed for his injustice and satisfy him for his injustice, God the Almighty said: “And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right or commit unlawful sexual intercourse - and whoever should do that will meet a penalty. * Doubled for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated.” * Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work” verse. This is a report that cannot be abrogated and applied to the polytheists. Applying this verse to the believers is contrary to what appears, and applying it to them requires evidence. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God’ (al-Baqarah 2:17). This is general for all sins, including disbelief, polytheism, doubt, hypocrisy, murder, immorality, and others. Whoever repents of any of these, God will accept his repentance. God the Almighty said: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. This verse is general for all sins except polytheism. It is mentioned in this noble surah after and before this verse to strengthen hope. God knows best. It is proven in the two Sahihs that there is a story about the Israelite who killed a hundred people, then asked a scholar if there was any repentance for him. He said: Who will stand between you and repentance? Then he directed him to a country where God could be worshipped, so he migrated to it and died on the way, and the angels of mercy took him, as we have mentioned more than once. If this was the case with the Children of Israel, then it is even more appropriate for repentance to be accepted in this nation, because God removed the burdens and shackles that were upon them and sent our Prophet with the tolerant Hanafi school of thought. As for the noble verse, which is the Almighty’s saying: And whoever kills a believer intentionally Al-Baqarah 2:176, Abu Hurairah and a group of the Salaf said: This is his recompense if He punishes him. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with his chain of transmission, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jami’ al-Attar, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn Maymun al-Anbari, on the authority of Hajjaj al-Aswad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but it is not authentic. The meaning of this wording is that this is his recompense if he is punished. This is also the case with every threat for a sin, but it may also be opposed by righteous deeds that prevent that recompense from reaching him, according to the two opinions of the proponents of balancing and nullification. This is the best way to proceed in the matter of the threat, and God knows best what is correct, and with regard to the estimation of the killer entering Hell. As for the opinion of Ibn Abbas and those who agreed with him, that there is no repentance for him, or according to the opinion of the majority, where he has no righteous deeds that will save him, he will not remain in it forever. Rather, eternity is a long stay. The hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have been transmitted: Whoever has in his heart the smallest weight of an atom of evil will be taken out of Hell. As for the hadith of Muawiyah, Every sin, God may forgive it, except for a man who dies as a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer intentionally, then may is for hope. If hope is not present in these two cases, this does not negate the occurrence of one of them, which is murder, based on the evidence we have mentioned. As for the one who dies as a disbeliever, the text is that God will not forgive him at all. As for the one who was killed demanding the killer on the Day of Resurrection, this is a right of the rights of human beings, and it is not dropped by repentance, but it must be returned to them. There is no difference between the one who was killed, the one from whom it was stolen, the one from whom it was usurped, the one who was slandered, and all the rights of human beings. The consensus is that they are not dropped by repentance, but they must be returned to them if the repentance is valid. If that is not possible, then it is necessary to demand it on the Day of Resurrection. However, the occurrence of the demand does not necessarily lead to the occurrence of retribution, since the killer may have good deeds that are directed to the one who was killed, or some of them, then he is given a reward that will admit him to Paradise, or God will compensate the one who was killed with whatever He wishes from His grace of palaces in Paradise and its delights, and raise his status in it and the like, and God knows best. Then the killer Intentional killing has rulings in this world and in the Hereafter. As for in this world, the guardians of the murdered person have authority over him. God Almighty said: And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority (al-Ahkam 2:10). Then they have the choice between killing, or pardoning, or taking a heavy blood money in three parts: thirty one-year-old camels, thirty two-year-old camels, and forty two-year-old camels, as is stated in the Book of Rulings. The imams differed as to whether he must pay the expiation of freeing a slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, or feeding, according to one of the two opinions, as mentioned previously in the expiation for mistake. According to two opinions, al-Shafi’i and his companions and a group of scholars say yes, he must, because if he must pay the expiation for mistake, then it is more appropriate for him to pay the expiation for intentional killing. They excluded this in the expiation for a false oath and excused themselves by making up the prayer that was intentionally neglected, as they agreed upon in the case of mistake. His companions, Imam Ahmad and others said: Intentional killing is more serious than to be expiated, so there is no expiation for it, and so is the false oath. They have no way to differentiate between these two scenarios and the prayer. Abandoned intentionally, they say that it is obligatory to make up for it if it is abandoned intentionally. Those who hold that expiation is obligatory for premeditated murder have provided evidence for what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said: A’rim ibn al-Fadl told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of al-Gharif ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’, who said: A group of Banu Salim came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: A friend of ours has made an obligation. He said: Let him free a slave, and God will ransom a limb of his from the Fire for every limb of his. Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq told us, Damrah ibn Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of al-Gharif al-Daylami, who said: We came to Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ al-Laythi and said to him: Tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: We came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a friend of ours who had made an obligation, and he said: Free a slave on his behalf, and God will ransom a limb of his from the Fire for every limb of his. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, and the wording of Abu Dawud from al-Gharif al-Daylami is: He said: We came to Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ and said to him: Tell us a hadith in which there is no addition or subtraction. He became angry and said: One of you may read while his Qur’an is hanging in his house, and he adds and subtracts. We said: We only wanted a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: We came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a companion of ours who had committed murder, meaning Hell. He said: Free him and God will free for every limb of his a limb from Hell.
4:93: God Almighty says: It is not permissible for a believer to kill his believing brother in any way, and as it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Masoud: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God is not permissible to be shed except in one of three cases: a life for a life, a married man who commits adultery, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community.” Then if one of these three occurs, then no one among the people has the right to kill him, and that is only up to the Imam or his deputies. And his saying: Except by mistake, they said: It is an isolated exception, like the poet’s saying: The eggs did not travel far and did not step on the ground except to tie a cold deportation There are many evidences for this. There is disagreement about the reason for the revelation of this verse. Mujahid and more than one person said: It was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah, the brother of Abu Jahl on his mother’s side, Asma bint Makhrama. He killed a man who was torturing him with his brother for Islam, and he was Al-Harith bin Yazid Al-Ghamidi. Ayyash harbored evil against him, so that man converted to Islam and emigrated, and Ayyash did not know. When the day of the conquest came, he saw him and thought that he was of his religion, so he attacked him and killed him. Then God revealed this verse. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: It was revealed about Abu Darda’ because he killed a man who had said the word of faith when he raised his sword against him, so he struck him and said his word. When that was mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: He only said it seeking refuge. So he said to him: Did you split his heart open? This story is in Sahih, and it is not from Abu Darda’. And his saying: And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave and the blood money to be paid to his family These are two obligations in killing by mistake, one of them is expiation for the great sin committed even if it was by mistake, and one of its conditions is that it be the freeing of a believing slave, so a disbelieving slave is not sufficient. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Al-Hasan Al-Basri that they said: A minor does not suffice unless he intends to believe. And it was narrated on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, who said: In a letter, then the freeing of a believing slave is not sufficient for a boy. Ibn Jarir chose that if he was born to Muslim parents, it is sufficient, otherwise it is not. And what the majority are upon is that whenever he is a Muslim, his freeing is valid for expiation, whether he is a minor or an adult. Imam Ahmad said: Abd Al-Razzaq informed us, Muammar informed us on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of a man from the Ansar: That he came with a black slave girl and said: O Messenger of God, I have to free a believing slave, so if I am… You see this believing woman whom I freed, so the Messenger of God said to her: Do you bear witness that there is no god but God? She said: Yes. He said: Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? She said: Yes. He said: Do you believe in resurrection after death? She said: Yes. He said: Free her. This is a sound chain of transmission, and the ignorance of the companion does not harm it. In the Muwatta of Malik, the Musnad of Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Sahih Muslim, Sunan Abi Dawud, and An-Nasa’i, on the authority of Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Al-Hakam: When he brought that black slave girl, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Where is God? She said: In the sky. He said: Who am I? She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Free her, for she is a believer. His saying: And a blood money to be paid to his family is the second obligation between the killer and the family of the murdered person, as compensation for what they have lost of their dead. This blood money is only due in fifths, as narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunan from the hadith of Al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, on the authority of Zayd ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Khafs ibn Malik, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding the blood money for accidental killing: twenty young female camels, twenty young male camels, twenty one-year-old female camels, twenty two-year-old female camels, and twenty three-year-old female camels. The wording of An-Nasa’i is: Al-Tirmidhi: We do not know it as being raised except from this source, and it has been narrated from Abdullah as a narration from Ali and a group, and it has been said: It must be divided into fourths, and this blood money is on the agnates, not from his wealth. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: I do not know of anyone who disagreed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the blood money is on the agnates, and this is more than one hadith of the elite. What he referred to, may God have mercy on him, has been proven in more than one hadith, including what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: Two women from Hudhayl fought, and one of them threw a stone at the other, killing her and what was in her womb. They disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ruled that the blood money for her fetus is the blood money of a male or female slave, and he ruled that the blood money for the woman is on her agnates. This requires that the ruling on pure intentional error is the obligation of blood money, but in this case the blood money must be divided into thirds due to the suspicion of intentional murder. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid bin Al-Walid to Banu Juthaymah and called them to Islam, but they did not know how to do so. They said, We have converted to Islam. So they began to say, We have converted to Islam. So Khalid began to kill them. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he raised his hands and said, O God, I disavow before You what Khalid did. He sent Ali to pay the blood money for their dead and for whatever he had destroyed of their property, even the saliva of a dog. From this hadith it is understood that the mistake of the imam or his deputy is in the public treasury. And his saying: unless they give in charity means that the blood money must be paid to his family unless they give it in charity, in which case it is not obligatory. And his saying: But if he is from a people who are enemies to you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave means that if the one killed is a believer but his relatives are from the infidels who are at war, then there is no blood money for them, and the killer must free a believing slave and nothing else. And his saying: But if he is from a people between you and whom there is a treaty the verse means that if the relatives of the one killed are people of protection or a truce, then they are entitled to the blood money of their victim, and if he is a believer, then the full blood money is due, and likewise if he is a disbeliever also according to a group of scholars. And it was said: Half of the blood money of the Muslim is due for the disbeliever, and it was said: a third of it, as is detailed in the Book of Rulings. And the killer must also free a believing slave. But whoever cannot find [a slave], then he must fast for two consecutive months means that he does not break his fast between them, but rather he should continue their fasting until the end of them. If he breaks his fast without an excuse such as sickness, menstruation, or childbirth, he should start over. And they differed regarding travel, whether it should be interrupted or not, based on Two sayings, and his saying: Repentance from God, and God is Knowing and Wise meaning this is the repentance of the murderer by mistake if he does not find a manumission, he fasts two consecutive months, and they differed about the one who is unable to fast, is it obligatory for him to feed sixty poor people as in the expiation for zihar, according to two sayings, one of them: Yes, as is stated in the expiation for zihar, and it was not mentioned here, because this is a place of threat, intimidation and warning, so it is not appropriate to mention feeding in it because of what is in it of facilitation and permission, and the second saying is that it is not switched to food, because if it was obligatory, he would not have delayed explaining it from the time of need and God is Knowing and Wise its interpretation has been presented more than once, Then, when the Almighty explained the ruling on accidental killing, He proceeded to explain the ruling on premeditated killing, saying: And whoever kills a believer intentionally verse. This is a severe threat and a definite warning to whoever commits this great sin, which is linked to associating partners with God in more than one verse in the Book of God, where the Almighty says in Surat al-Furqan 25:And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right verse. And the Almighty said: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you - that you not associate anything with Him” verse. And the verses and hadiths prohibiting killing are very many, including what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first thing that will be judged between people on the Day of Resurrection will be blood. And in another hadith narrated by Abu Dawud on the authority of Amr ibn al-Walid ibn Abdah al-Masri on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The believer will continue to be righteous as long as he does not shed unlawful blood. But if he sheds unlawful blood, he will be saved.” And in another hadith The destruction of the world is easier in the sight of God than the killing of a Muslim man, and in another hadith, “Whoever helps in killing a Muslim, even with half a word, will come on the Day of Resurrection with it written between his eYa-Sin 36:Despairing of the mercy of God.” Ibn Abbas believed that there is no repentance for the one who intentionally kills a believer. Al-Bukhari said: Adam told us, Shu’bah told us, Al-Mughirah ibn Al-Nu’man told us, he said: I heard Ibn Jubayr say: The people of Kufa differed about it, so I traveled to Ibn Abbas and asked him about it, and he said: This verse was revealed, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, it is the last to be revealed, and nothing abrogated it. This is how he also narrated it, as did Muslim and Al-Nasa’i through various chains of transmission on the authority of Shu’bah. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hanbal on the authority of Ibn Mahdi, on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mughirah ibn Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, and he said: Nothing abrogated it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Awn told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the statement of God, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, the verse, he said: Nothing abrogated it. And he said about this verse, And those who do not invoke with God another deity, to the end of it, he said: It was revealed about the polytheists. Ibn Jarir also said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Mansur, Sa’id ibn Jubayr told me or al-Hakam told me on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, he said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, he said: If a man knows Islam and the laws of Islam, then he kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell and there is no repentance for him. So I mentioned that to Mujahid and he said: Except for the one who regrets. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Jarir narrated on the authority of Yahya al-Jaber on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, who said: We were with Ibn Abbas after he had lost his sight, when a man came to him and called out: O Abdullah ibn Abbas, what do you think of a man who intentionally killed a believer? He said: His recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and God is angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment. He said: What if he repents and does righteous deeds, then is guided? Ibn Abbas said: May his mother be bereaved of him, how can he repent and be guided? By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “May his mother be bereaved of him, he who intentionally kills a believer will come on the Day of Resurrection taking him by his right hand or his left, his jugular veins gushing out from before the Throne of the Most Merciful. He will hold his killer with his left hand and with his other hand his head, saying: ‘O Lord, ask this man why he killed me.’” By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Abdullah, this verse was revealed and no verse abrogated it until your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, and no proof was revealed after it. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, I heard Yahya ibn al-Mujbir narrating on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a man came to him and said: ‘What do you think of a man who intentionally kills another man?’ He said: ‘His recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever,’ the verse. He said: ‘It was revealed among the last to be revealed, and nothing abrogated it until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, and no revelation was revealed after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that said: ‘What do you think if he repents, believes, does righteous deeds, then is guided?’ He said: How can he repent, when I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “May his mother be bereaved of a man who kills a man intentionally. He will come on the Day of Resurrection seizing his killer by his right or his left hand - or seizing his head by his right or his left hand - his veins gushing with blood from the direction of the Throne, saying: O Lord, ask your servant why he killed me.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ammar al-Dahni, Yahya al-Jaber, and Thabit al-Thamali, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. This has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas through many chains of narration, and among those who held that there is no repentance for him from the Salaf are Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Hurayrah, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, Ubayd ibn Umair, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim. There are many hadiths on this topic, including what Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh al-Hafiz narrated in his Tafsir: Dulaj told us. Ibn Ahmad, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Saeed Al-Bushanji H narrated to us, and Abdullah ibn Jaafar narrated to us, and Ibrahim ibn Fahd narrated to us, they said: Ubaid ibn Ubaidah narrated to us, Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Amr ibn Shurahbil, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The one who was killed will come clinging to his killer on the Day of Resurrection, holding his head with his other hand, and he will say: ‘O Lord, ask this one why he killed me?’ He will say: ‘I killed him so that honor would be for You.’ He will say: ‘Then it is mine.’ He said: And another will come clinging to his killer and say: ‘O Lord, ask this one why he killed me.’ He will say: ‘I killed him so that honor would be for so-and-so.’ He will say: ‘Then he has no share in his sin.’ He said: ‘Then he will fall into the Fire for seventy autumns.’” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Al-Mustamir Al-Awfi, on the authority of Amr ibn Asim, on the authority of Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman, on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Safwan bin Isa told us, Thawr bin Yazid told us on the authority of Abu Awn, on the authority of Abu Idris, who said: I heard Muawiyah, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God may forgive every sin except for a man who dies as a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer intentionally. And this is how al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Muthanna, on the authority of Safwan bin Isa, and Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Ja’far told us, Samuyah told us, Abdul A’la bin Musahhir told us, Sadaqah bin Khalid told us, Khalid bin Dahqan told us, Ibn Abi Zakariya told us, he said: I heard Umm al-Darda’ say: I heard Abu al-Darda’ say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God may forgive every sin except for a man who dies as a polytheist, or a man who kills a believer intentionally. This is very strange from this aspect, and the preserved hadith of Muawiyah mentioned above, and God knows best. Then Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Baqiyyah bin al-Waleed on the authority of Nafi’ bin Yazid: Ibn Jubayr told me. Al-Ansari narrated from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever kills a believer intentionally has disbelieved in God Almighty. This is also a strange hadith, as its chain of transmission has been greatly criticized. Imam Ahmad said: An-Nadr narrated to us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, Humayd narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Aaliyah came to me and a friend of mine, and he said to us: Come, for you are younger than me and more knowledgeable of hadith than me. So he went with us to Bishr ibn Asim, and Abu al-Aaliyah said to him: Tell these people your hadith. So he said: Uqbah ibn Malik al-Laythi narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a raiding party that raided a people, and a man went with the people, and a man from the raiding party followed him, brandishing his sword. The one who went with the man said: I am a Muslim, but he did not consider what he said. So he struck him and killed him. The hadith reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said a harsh word about it, and the killer was informed. While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon, the killer said: By God, he did not say what he said except… Seeking refuge from being killed, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him and from the people before him and began his sermon, then he said again: O Messenger of God, he did not say what he said except to seek refuge from being killed, so he turned away from him and from the people before him and began his sermon, then he did not wait until he said the third time: By God, O Messenger of God, he did not say what he said except to seek refuge from being killed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to him and you could see the displeasure on his face, and he said: God has refused to do with whoever kills a believer three times. Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sulayman ibn al-Mughira, and what the majority of the predecessors and successors of the Ummah are upon is that the killer has repentance between him and God, the Almighty, the Majestic, so if he repents and returns, and is humble and submissive and does a righteous deed, God will replace his bad deeds with good deeds, and compensate the one who was killed for his injustice and satisfy him for his injustice, God the Almighty said: “And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right or commit unlawful sexual intercourse - and whoever should do that will meet a penalty. * Doubled for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated.” * Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work” verse. This is a report that cannot be abrogated and applied to the polytheists. Applying this verse to the believers is contrary to what appears, and applying it to them requires evidence. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God’ (al-Baqarah 2:17). This is general for all sins, including disbelief, polytheism, doubt, hypocrisy, murder, immorality, and others. Whoever repents of any of these, God will accept his repentance. God the Almighty said: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. This verse is general for all sins except polytheism. It is mentioned in this noble surah after and before this verse to strengthen hope. God knows best. It is proven in the two Sahihs that there is a story about the Israelite who killed a hundred people, then asked a scholar if there was any repentance for him. He said: Who will stand between you and repentance? Then he directed him to a country where God could be worshipped, so he migrated to it and died on the way, and the angels of mercy took him, as we have mentioned more than once. If this was the case with the Children of Israel, then it is even more appropriate for repentance to be accepted in this nation, because God removed the burdens and shackles that were upon them and sent our Prophet with the tolerant Hanafi school of thought. As for the noble verse, which is the Almighty’s saying: And whoever kills a believer intentionally Al-Baqarah 2:176, Abu Hurairah and a group of the Salaf said: This is his recompense if He punishes him. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it with his chain of transmission, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jami’ al-Attar, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn Maymun al-Anbari, on the authority of Hajjaj al-Aswad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, but it is not authentic. The meaning of this wording is that this is his recompense if he is punished. This is also the case with every threat for a sin, but it may also be opposed by righteous deeds that prevent that recompense from reaching him, according to the two opinions of the proponents of balancing and nullification. This is the best way to proceed in the matter of the threat, and God knows best what is correct, and with regard to the estimation of the killer entering Hell. As for the opinion of Ibn Abbas and those who agreed with him, that there is no repentance for him, or according to the opinion of the majority, where he has no righteous deeds that will save him, he will not remain in it forever. Rather, eternity is a long stay. The hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have been transmitted: Whoever has in his heart the smallest weight of an atom of evil will be taken out of Hell. As for the hadith of Muawiyah, Every sin, God may forgive it, except for a man who dies as a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer intentionally, then may is for hope. If hope is not present in these two cases, this does not negate the occurrence of one of them, which is murder, based on the evidence we have mentioned. As for the one who dies as a disbeliever, the text is that God will not forgive him at all. As for the one who was killed demanding the killer on the Day of Resurrection, this is a right of the rights of human beings, and it is not dropped by repentance, but it must be returned to them. There is no difference between the one who was killed, the one from whom it was stolen, the one from whom it was usurped, the one who was slandered, and all the rights of human beings. The consensus is that they are not dropped by repentance, but they must be returned to them if the repentance is valid. If that is not possible, then it is necessary to demand it on the Day of Resurrection. However, the occurrence of the demand does not necessarily lead to the occurrence of retribution, since the killer may have good deeds that are directed to the one who was killed, or some of them, then he is given a reward that will admit him to Paradise, or God will compensate the one who was killed with whatever He wishes from His grace of palaces in Paradise and its delights, and raise his status in it and the like, and God knows best. Then the killer Intentional killing has rulings in this world and in the Hereafter. As for in this world, the guardians of the murdered person have authority over him. God Almighty said: And whoever is killed unjustly, We have given his heir authority (al-Ahkam 2:10). Then they have the choice between killing, or pardoning, or taking a heavy blood money in three parts: thirty one-year-old camels, thirty two-year-old camels, and forty two-year-old camels, as is stated in the Book of Rulings. The imams differed as to whether he must pay the expiation of freeing a slave, or fasting for two consecutive months, or feeding, according to one of the two opinions, as mentioned previously in the expiation for mistake. According to two opinions, al-Shafi’i and his companions and a group of scholars say yes, he must, because if he must pay the expiation for mistake, then it is more appropriate for him to pay the expiation for intentional killing. They excluded this in the expiation for a false oath and excused themselves by making up the prayer that was intentionally neglected, as they agreed upon in the case of mistake. His companions, Imam Ahmad and others said: Intentional killing is more serious than to be expiated, so there is no expiation for it, and so is the false oath. They have no way to differentiate between these two scenarios and the prayer. Abandoned intentionally, they say that it is obligatory to make up for it if it is abandoned intentionally. Those who hold that expiation is obligatory for premeditated murder have provided evidence for what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said: A’rim ibn al-Fadl told us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of al-Gharif ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’, who said: A group of Banu Salim came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: A friend of ours has made an obligation. He said: Let him free a slave, and God will ransom a limb of his from the Fire for every limb of his. Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq told us, Damrah ibn Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, on the authority of al-Gharif al-Daylami, who said: We came to Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ al-Laythi and said to him: Tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: We came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a friend of ours who had made an obligation, and he said: Free a slave on his behalf, and God will ransom a limb of his from the Fire for every limb of his. Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla, and the wording of Abu Dawud from al-Gharif al-Daylami is: He said: We came to Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’ and said to him: Tell us a hadith in which there is no addition or subtraction. He became angry and said: One of you may read while his Qur’an is hanging in his house, and he adds and subtracts. We said: We only wanted a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: We came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a companion of ours who had committed murder, meaning Hell. He said: Free him and God will free for every limb of his a limb from Hell.
4:94: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Abi Bakr, Khalaf bin Al-Waleed, and Hussein bin Muhammad told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from Banu Salim passed by a group of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, tending his sheep, and he greeted them. They said: He does not greet us except to seek refuge from us. So they went to him and killed him, and they brought his sheep to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then this verse was revealed: O you who believe, to the end of it. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Abd bin Hamid, on the authority of Abd Al-Aziz bin Abi Razmah, on the authority of Isra’il, on his authority. Then he said: This is a good and authentic hadith. There is another hadith on the subject on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid. Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Musa on the authority of Isra’il, on his authority. Then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Musa and Abd Al-Rahim bin Sulayman, both on the authority of Isra’il, on his authority. He said in some of his books other than Tafsir, and he narrated it on the authority of Abdul Rahman only, and this is a report with us that is authentic in its chain of transmission, and it may have to be weak according to the doctrine of others for reasons including: that it is not known for it to be from Samak except from this source, and from them that Ikrimah in his narration with them is questionable, and from them that the one about whom this verse was revealed is disputed with them, so some of them said: It was revealed about Muhallim bin Jaththama, and some of them said: Usamah bin Zaid, and other things were said, I said: This is a strange statement and it is rejected from aspects: First, it is proven from Samak and more than one of the great imams narrated it from him, second, Ikrimah is cited as evidence in the Sahih, third, it is narrated from other than this source from Ibn Abbas, as Al-Bukhari said: Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us from Amr bin Dinar, from Ata’, from Ibn Abbas, “And do not say to one who gives you peace, ‘You are not a believer. ’” He said: Ibn Abbas said that a man was with his spoils and the Muslims caught up with him, so he said: Peace be upon you, so they killed him and took his spoils, so God revealed in that, “And do not say to one who gives you peace, ‘You are not a believer. ’” Ibn Abbas said: That is the worldly show Al-Ghanimah, and Ibn Abbas read as-Salam, and Saeed bin Mansour said: Mansour told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Muslims caught up with a man in his spoils, and he said: Peace be upon you, so they killed him and took his spoils, so the verse was revealed: “And do not say to one who gives you peace, ‘You are not a believer’”. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, and in the biography: That his brother Fazar migrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the command of his father to convert them and their people to Islam, so a company of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met him in the dead of night, and he had told them that he was a Muslim, but they did not accept it from him, so they killed him. His father said: So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave me another thousand dinars as blood money and sent me on, so the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God verse. As for the story of Muhallim bin Jaththama, Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yaqub told us: My father told me on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, Yazid bin Abdullah bin Qusayt told us on the authority of Al-Qaqa’ bin Abdullah bin Abi Hadrad, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent us to Idam, so I went out with a group of Muslims among them Abu Qatada Al-Harith bin Rib’i and Muhallim bin Jaththama bin Qais. We went out until we were in the valley of Idam, and Amir bin Al-Adbat Al-Ashja’i passed by us on his camel, with him his provisions and a bowl of milk. When he passed by us, he greeted us, so we held back from him, and Muhallim bin Jaththama attacked him and killed him, for something that had happened between them, and he took his camel and provisions. When we came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we told him the report, this verse was revealed concerning us: “O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate and do not say to one who offers you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’ seeking the goods of worldly life. But with God are many spoils.” Thus were you before, but God has conferred favor upon you. So be certain that God is All-Aware of what you do. It was transmitted exclusively by Ahmad. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Muhallim ibn Juthamah as an expedition, and Aamer ibn al-Adbat met them and greeted them with the greeting of Islam. There was a grudge between them in the pre-Islamic era, so Muhallim shot him with an arrow and killed him. The report reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Uyaynah and al-Aqra’ spoke about it. Al-Aqra’ said: O Messenger of God, go today and be deceived tomorrow. Uyaynah said: No, by God, until his women taste the grief that my women taste. Muhallim came wearing two cloaks and sat in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask forgiveness for him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God not forgive you. He stood up while wiping his tears with his two cloaks. Not even seven days had passed before he died and they buried him, but the earth rejected him. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so he said: The earth accepts those who are worse than your companion, but God wanted to admonish you. Then They threw him between two mountain cliffs and threw stones at him, so the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate. Al-Bukhari said: Habib bin Abi Umrah said on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Miqdad: If a believing man conceals his faith with a group of disbelievers and you kill him, then you used to conceal your faith in Mecca before. This is how Al-Bukhari mentioned it in a shortened, suspended form. It was narrated in a long, connected form. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Hammad bin Ali Al-Baghdadi told us, Jaafar bin Salamah told us, Abu Bakr bin Ali bin Muqaddam told us, Habib bin Abi Umrah told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a detachment in which was Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad. When they reached the people, they found that they had dispersed, and a man with a lot of money remained who had not moved. He said: I bear witness that there is no god but God. Al-Miqdad attacked him and killed him. One of his companions said to him: Did you kill a man who bears witness that there is no god but God? By God, I will mention that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said: O Messenger of God, a man testified that there is no god but God, and Al-Miqdad killed him. He said: “Call Al-Miqdad to me, O Al-Miqdad: You killed a man who said there is no god but God, so how will you say there is no god but God tomorrow?” He said: So God revealed: “O you who believe! When you go forth in the cause of God, investigate and do not say to one who offers you peace, ‘You are not a believer,’ seeking the goods of worldly life. But with God are many spoils. Thus were you before, but God was gracious to you. So investigate.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Miqdad: “There was a believing man who concealed his faith with a people of unbelievers, then he showed his faith and you killed him. And thus were you concealing your faith in Mecca before.” And His statement: But with God are many spoils means better than what you desired for the goods of worldly life that led you to kill someone who offered you peace and showed you faith, but you ignored him and accused him of flattery and dissimulation in order to seek the goods of worldly life. But what is with God of lawful provision is better for you than the wealth of this man. And his saying: Thus were you before, then God has bestowed His favor upon you means that you were before this state like this one who concealed his faith and hid it from his people, as mentioned in the hadith attributed to the Prophet earlier, and as God the Almighty said: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land verse. This is the view of Saeed bin Jubair, as narrated by Ath-Thawri on the authority of Habib bin Abi Umrah on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his saying: Thus were you before concealing your faith from the polytheists. And Abd al-Razzaq narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Abdullah bin Katheer informed me on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair regarding his saying: Thus were you before concealing your faith as this shepherd concealed his faith. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said, and he mentioned on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: His saying: Thus were you before you were not believers, then God has bestowed His favor upon you means He repented to you, so Usama swore that he would not kill a man who said: There is no god but God after that man, and what he encountered from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding him. His saying: Then verify is an emphasis on what came before, and his saying: Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Aware Saeed bin Jubair said: This is a threat and a warning.
4:95: Al-Bukhari said: Hafs bin Umar told us, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara', who said: When the verse, Not equal are those believers who sit at home was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Zaid and wrote it down. Then Ibn Umm Maktum came and complained about his injury, so God revealed, Except those who are disabled. Muhammad bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara', who said: When the verse, Not equal are those believers who sit at home was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Call so-and-so. So he came to him with an inkwell, a tablet, and a shoulder blade. He said: Write, Not equal are those believers who sit at home except those who are disabled and those who strive in the cause of God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Ibn Umm Maktum behind, and he said: O Messenger of God, I am blind. So the verse, Not equal are those believers who sit at home except those who are disabled and those who strive in the cause of God was revealed in its place. Al-Bukhari also said: Ismail bin Abdullah told us, Ibrahim bin Saad told me, on the authority of Salih bin Kaysan, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Sahl bin Saad told me. Al-Sa’idi said that he saw Marwan bin Al-Hakam in the mosque. He said: So I came and sat next to him, and he informed us that Zaid bin Thabit informed him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dictated to me: Those of the believers who sit at home, except those who are disabled, are not equal to those who strive in the cause of God. Ibn Umm Maktum came to him while he was dictating it to me. He said: O Messenger of God, by God, if I could strive, I would strive. He was blind, so God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his thigh was on my thigh, so it was heavy for me and I feared that my thigh would be broken. Then he was relieved, and God revealed: except those who are disabled. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, not Muslim. It was narrated from another source by Imam Ahmad, who said: Sulayman bin Dawud told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Abi al-Zinad informed us, on the authority of Kharijah bin Zaid, who said: Zaid bin Thabit said: I was sitting next to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when revelation came to him and tranquility overcame him. He said: So he raised his thigh over my thigh when tranquility overcame him. Zaid said: By God, I have never found anything heavier than So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and then he calmed down and said: Write, O Zaid. So I took a shoulder and he said: Write: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive and fight until His saying: a great reward. So I wrote that on a shoulder. When Ibn Umm Maktum heard it, he stood up and he was a blind man. He stood up when he heard the virtue of the strivers and said: O Messenger of God, what about those who are unable to strive and those who are blind and the like? Zaid said: By God, he had not finished speaking - or had only finished speaking - when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was overcome by tranquility, and his thigh fell on my thigh, and I felt as heavy as I had felt the first time. Then he was relieved, and he said: Recite. So I recited to him: Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal to those who strive hard in the cause of God and those who strive hard in the cause of God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who are not disabled. Zaid said: So I attached it, and by God it was as if I could see where it was attached to a crack in the shoulder. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Mansour, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi al-Zinad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Kharijah bin Zaid bin Thabit, on the authority of his father, with a similar chain of transmission. And Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma`mar informed us, al-Zuhri informed us, on the authority of Qubaysah ibn Dhu`ayb, on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: I was writing for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “Write: ‘Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, except for those who are disabled, and those who strive in the cause of God.’ Then Abd God ibn Umm Maktum came and said: O Messenger of God, I love striving in the cause of God, but I have a condition that you see, and my sight has gone. Zayd said: The thigh of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became so heavy on my thigh that I feared that it would break, then he was relieved, then he said: Write: ‘Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, except for those who are disabled, and those who strive in the cause of God.’” And Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it. Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Jurayj informed us, Abd al-Karim informed me, he is Ibn Malik al-Jazari, that Muqsim, the freed slave of Abd God ibn al-Harith, informed him that Ibn Abbas informed him: ‘Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home from Badr and those who went out to Badr. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, not Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi narrated it through the chain of transmission of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, said: Not equal are those believers who sit at home, except those who have a disability about Badr and those who went out to Badr. When the Battle of Badr was revealed, Abdullah bin Hijsh and Ibn Umm Maktum said: We are blind, O Messenger of God, do we have a dispensation? Then, Not equal are those believers who sit at home, except those who have a disability was revealed. God preferred the mujahidin over those who sit at home by a degree, so these are the ones who sit at home except those who have a disability. And God has preferred those who strive over those who sit at home by a great reward * Degrees from Him over those believers who sit at home, except those who have a disability. This is the wording of Al-Tirmidhi. Then he said: This is a good and strange hadith from this aspect, so his statement: Not equal are those believers who sit at home was absolute, but when the revelation except those who have a disability was revealed by rapid revelation, this became a way out for those who had excuses that permitted them to abandon jihad, such as blindness, lameness, and sickness, from being equal to those who strive in the way of God with their wealth and their lives. Then God the Almighty informed about the virtue of the mujahideen over those who sit back. Ibn Abbas said: except those who are disabled. This is how it should be, as it was established in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Zuhair ibn Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, in Madinah there are people who, whenever you travel, you do not travel through a valley except that they are with you in it. They said: And they are in Madinah, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes, they are held back by an excuse. This is how Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Adi, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, and al-Bukhari suspended it in a definite form. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Musa ibn Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You have left behind in Madinah people who, whenever you travel, you do not spend, and you do not travel through a valley except that they are with you in it. They said: How can they be with us in it, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes, they are held back by an excuse. This is the wording of Abu Dawud. In this sense, the poet said: Oh you who are departing to the ancient house, you have walked as bodies and we have walked as souls. We stayed for an excuse and for destiny, and whoever stayed for an excuse has gone. And His statement: And to each God has promised the best meaning Paradise and a great reward. This indicates that jihad is not an individual obligation, but rather a communal obligation. God the Almighty said: And God has preferred those who strive hard over those who sit at home, with a great reward. Then He, the Almighty, informed us of the degrees He has preferred them with, in the lofty chambers of Paradise, and the forgiveness of sins and mistakes, and the coming of mercy and blessings, as a kindness and honor from Him. For this reason He said: “Degrees from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.” It was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred levels that God has prepared for those who strive in His cause. Between each two levels is like the distance between the heavens and the earth.” Al-A’mash said on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever shoots an arrow will have one level of reward. A man said: O Messenger of God, what is one level? He said: “It is not your mother’s threshold. The distance between each two levels is one hundred years.”
