4:97: Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Yazid Al-Muqri' narrated to us, Haywah and others narrated to us, they said: Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Abu Al-Aswad narrated to us, he said: A mission was sent to the people of Madinah, so I registered for it, then I met Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, and I informed him, but he forbade me from that emphatically, he said: Ibn Abbas informed me that some people from the Muslims were with the polytheists, and they were increasing in number during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an arrow would come and hit one of them, killing him or striking his neck and killing him, so God revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves, and Al-Layth narrated it from Abu Al-Aswad. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur Al-Ramadi narrated to us, Abu Ahmad, meaning Al-Zubayri, narrated to us, Muhammad bin Sharik Al-Makki narrated to us, Amr bin Dinar narrated to us from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, he said: There were people from the people of Makkah who converted to Islam and they were hiding their Islam, so the polytheists expelled them with them on the day of Badr, and some of them were afflicted by the actions of others. The Muslims said: Our companions were Muslims and they were forced, so ask forgiveness for them. Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves 10:13. Ikrimah said: So he wrote to those Muslims who remained with this verse: They have no excuse. He said: So they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them, so they gave them taqiyya, so this verse was revealed: And among the people is he who says, ‘We believe in God’ 10:13. Akrima said: This verse was revealed about young men from Quraysh who spoke about Islam in Mecca, including Ali bin Umayya bin Khalaf, Abu Qais bin Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, Abu Al-Aas bin Munabbih bin Al-Hajjaj, and Al-Harith bin Zam’ah. Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about some hypocrites who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca and went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, and were afflicted among those who were afflicted. So this noble verse was revealed in general regarding everyone who stayed among the polytheists, and was able to emigrate but was not able to establish the religion, so he is unjust to himself and committing a sin by consensus, and by the text of this verse, where God Almighty says: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves meaning by abandoning emigration They will say, ‘In what state were you?’ meaning why did you stay here and abandon emigration They will say, ‘We were oppressed in the land.’ meaning we were not able to leave the country, nor go about the land They will say, ‘Was not the earth of God spacious?’ The verse. Abu Dawud said: Muhammad bin Dawud bin Sufyan told us, Yahya bin Hassan, Sulayman ibn Musa Abu Dawud told us, Ja`far ibn Sa`d ibn Samra ibn Jundub told us, Khabib ibn Sulayman told me on the authority of his father Sulayman ibn Samra, on the authority of Samra ibn Jundub, and after that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gathers with a polytheist and lives with him is like him. Al-Suddi said: When Al-Abbas, Uqayl and Nawfal were taken captive, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Abbas: Redeem yourself and your nephew. He said: O Messenger of God, have we not reached your qiblah and witnessed your testimony? He said: O Abbas, you have argued and you have disputed. Then he recited to him this verse: Was not the earth of God spacious? The verse was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And His saying: Except for the weak to the end of the verse, this is an excuse from God for these people to not emigrate, and that is because they are not able to escape from the hands of the polytheists, and if they were able they would not know how to take the path, and for this reason He said: They are not able to devise a plan nor are they guided to a way, Mujahid, Ikrimah and Al-Suddi said: He means a path. And the Almighty said: Then it is those whom God may pardon, meaning that God will forgive them for not emigrating. Perhaps is a requirement, and God is Pardoning and Forgiving. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Nu’aym told us, Shaiban told us, on the authority of Yahya, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying the ‘Isha’ prayer, he said: God hears whoever praises Him. Then he said before prostrating: “O God, save ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, O God, save Salamah ibn Hisham, O God, save al-Walid ibn al-Walid, O God, save the weak among the believers, O God, make your punishment severe upon Mudar, O God, make them years like the years of Joseph.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Muammar al-Muqri told us, Abdul-Warith told us, Ali ibn Zaid told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands after he had finished the salutation while facing the qiblah, and said: O God, save al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Salamah ibn Hisham, and the weak Muslims who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a path from the hands of the disbelievers. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told us, Hajjaj told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zaid, on the authority of Abdullah or Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Qurashi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate after the noon prayer: O God, save al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, and the weak Muslims from the hands of the polytheists who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a path. This hadith has a witness in the Sahih from another chain of transmission, as mentioned above. Abdul Razzaq said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: My mother and I were among the weak among women and children. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Al-Nu’man informed us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Abu Malikah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, except the weak, he said: My mother and I were among those whom God Almighty excused. And his saying: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find on the earth many [alternative] locations and abundance, this is an incitement to emigrate and an encouragement to separate from the polytheists, and that wherever the believer goes he will find a way out and a refuge in which to fortify himself. Al-Maraghim is a noun, and the Arabs say: So-and-so is opposing his people, opposing and opposing. Al-Nabigha ibn Ja’dah said: Like a mountain, the dear one who is reluctant and the one who escapes seeks refuge in its corners Ibn Abbas said: Maraghim means moving from one land to another. This was also narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Ath-Thawri. Mujahid said: Maraghim Katheer means moving away from what he dislikes. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said: Maraghim Katheer means towers. What appears - and God knows best - is that it is the protection that one fortifies oneself with and uses to resist the enemy. His saying ample means provision, this was said by more than one of them, including Qatada, where he said: In His saying: He will find on the earth many [alternative] places and abundance meaning from misguidance to guidance, and from scarcity to wealth, and His saying: And whoever emigrates for the sake of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon God meaning whoever emigrates for the sake of God and His Messenger and dies on the way, then he has attained the reward of the one who emigrated, as is proven in the two Sahihs and other Sahihs, Musnads and Sunans on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Ansari on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, on the authority of `Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Actions are but by intentions, and each person will have but what he intended. So whoever emigrated for the sake of God and His Messenger, then his emigration is for the sake of God and His Messenger. And whoever emigrated for a worldly gain or a woman to marry, then his emigration is for what he emigrated for.” This is general in emigration and in all actions. And from it is the authentic hadith in the two Sahihs about the man who killed ninety-nine people, then the worshipper completed the hundred and then asked a scholar: Is there any repentance for him? He said to him: Who is standing between you and repentance? Then he advised him to move from his country to another country where he would worship God. So when he left his country as a migrant to the other country, death overtook him on the way, so the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. Some said: He came repentant, and others said: He had not arrived yet. So they were ordered to measure the distance between the two lands, so whichever one he was closer to would be from it. So God ordered this one to come closer to this one, and this one to move away, so they found him closer to the land to which he had migrated by a handspan, so the angels of mercy took him. And in another narration, when death came to him, he turned his chest away to the land to which he had migrated. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Atik, on the authority of his father Abdullah bin Atik, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever leaves his home to fight in the cause of God, and then says: Where are those who fight in the cause of God? And he falls from his mount and dies, his reward is with God, or he is bitten by an mount and dies, his reward is with God, or he dies a natural death, his reward is with God - meaning a natural death in his bed. By God, this is a statement that I did not hear from any of the Arabs before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace - and whoever kills a camel deserves Paradise.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Shaiba al-Hizami told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mughirah al-Khuzami told me, on the authority of al-Mundhir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, that al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: Khalid ibn Hizam emigrated to the land of Abyssinia and was bitten by a snake on the road and died, so the following verse was revealed about him: “And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon God. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Al-Zubayr said: So I was expecting him and waiting for his arrival while I was in the land of Abyssinia, and nothing saddened me as much as the sadness of his death when it reached me, because few of those who emigrated from Quraysh were without some of their family or relatives with them, and there was no one with me from Banu Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza, and I do not hope for anyone other than him. This trace is very strange, for this story is Meccan, and the revelation of this verse is Medinan, so perhaps he meant that it was revealed to include his ruling with others, even if that was not the reason for the revelation, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, the client of Abdullah ibn Ja`far, told us, Sahl ibn `Uthman told us, `Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman told us, Ash`ath, who is Ibn Suwar, told us, on the authority of `Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: Damrah ibn Jundub went out to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he died on the way before he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse, And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger was revealed. My father told us, `Abdullah ibn Raja` told us, Israel informed us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu Damrah ibn al-`Ays al-Zarqi, who was blind and was in Mecca. When the verse, Except for the weak among men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan was revealed, I said: I am rich, and I am able to devise a plan. So he prepared himself, intending to go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but death overtook him in al-Tan`im, so this verse was revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him was revealed. Al-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan bin Arubah Al-Basri told us, Haywah bin Shureih Al-Himsi told us, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibn Thawban told us on the authority of his father, Makhul told us on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghanam Al-Ash'ari, Abu Malik told us, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "God said: Whoever volunteers to go out in My cause to fight, seeking My countenance, believing in My promise, and believing in My messengers, then he is under God's guarantee. Al-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan bin Arubah Al-Basri told us, Haywah bin Shureih Al-Himsi told us, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibn Thawban told us on the authority of his father, Makhul told us on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ghanam Al-Ash'ari, Abu Malik told us, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: "God said: Whoever volunteers to go out in My cause to fight, seeking My countenance, believing in My promise, and believing in My messengers, then he is under God's guarantee. Either He takes him with the army and admits him into Paradise, or he returns under God's guarantee. And if he pursues a slave and annoys him until he returns him to his family with whatever reward he has earned, or spoils, and gains from God's bounty and he dies, or is killed, or his horse or camel kicks him, or a snake bites him, or he dies in his bed by whatever death God wills, then he is a martyr." Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Baqiyah from the bounty of God to the end, and he added after his words: then he is a martyr, and Paradise is for him. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Ibrahim bin Ziyad Sublan told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Hamid bin Abi Hamid, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yazid al-Laithi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever goes out for Hajj and dies, the reward of the pilgrim will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out for Umrah and dies, the reward of the pilgrim will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever goes out to fight in the cause of God and dies, the reward of the fighter will be written for him until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a strange hadith from this source.
4:101: God Almighty says: And when you travel throughout the land, meaning when you travel throughout the country, as God Almighty says: He knows that there will be among you those who are ill and others who travel throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God, the verse. And his saying: There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer means to shorten it either in quantity by making the four-unit prayer two-unit prayer as the majority understood from this verse, and they used it as evidence for shortening the prayer while traveling despite their differences in that. Some say: It must be a journey of obedience such as jihad, or Hajj, or Umrah, or seeking knowledge, or visiting, and other than that, as is narrated from Ibn Umar and Ata’ and it is narrated from Malik in a narration from him similar to it, due to the apparent meaning of his saying: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, and some say: It is not a condition for a journey of worship, rather it must be permissible, due to his saying: But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin 1:13, just as he permitted him to eat dead meat while forced on condition that he is not disobedient by his travel, and this is the saying of Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad and other imams. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: We were told by Wakee’, from Al-A’mash, from Ibrahim, who said: A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I am a merchant. He went to Bahrain, and he ordered him to pray two rak’ahs. This is a mursal. Some say: It is sufficient for any travel, whether it is permissible or forbidden, even if he went out to cut off the road or frighten the wayfarer, it is permissible because of the existence of any travel. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, and Dawud, based on the generality of the verse, and the majority disagreed with them. As for the statement of God the Almighty: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, this may have been stated as the norm at the time of the revelation of this verse, because at the beginning of Islam after the migration, most of their travels were frightening, and they would only set out for a general conquest or a special expedition. All other times, it was a war against Islam and its people. If the explicit statement is stated as the norm or as an incident, then it has no meaning, like the statement of God the Almighty: And do not compel your girls to prostitution if they desire chastity, and the statement of God the Almighty: And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship [born] of your women, and the verse. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Idris told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Ammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Babih, on the authority of Ya`la bin Umayyah, she said: I asked `Umar bin Al-Khattab, I said to him: His statement: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you when the people are secure? Omar may God be pleased with him said to me: I was amazed by what you were amazed by, so I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about it, and he said: It is a charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity. Muslim and the Sunan scholars narrated it in this way from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Ammar. At-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan saheeh hadith. Ali ibn al-Madini said: This is a hasan saheeh hadith from the hadith of Omar, and it is not preserved except through this chain of transmission and its men are well-known. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Nu`aym told us, Malik ibn Mughul told us from Abu Hanzalah al-Hadha` who said: I asked Ibn Omar about the prayer of travel, and he said: It is two rak`ahs. I said: Where is the statement of God: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you while we are safe? He said: It is the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Ibn Mardawayh said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Isa told us, Ali bin Muhammad bin Saeed told us: Munjab told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Qais bin Wahb, on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, who said: I asked Ibn Umar about two rak’ahs while traveling, and he said: It is a concession that was sent down from the heavens, so if you wish, you may reject it. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Ibn Awn told us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: We prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, between Mecca and Medina, and we were safe, not fearing between them, two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs. And this is how al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdul A’la, on the authority of Khalid al-Hadha’, on the authority of Abdullah bin Awn, on his authority. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: And this is how it was narrated by Ayoub, Hisham, and Yazid bin Ibrahim Al-Tastari, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. I said: And this is how it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i, both on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out from Medina to Mecca, fearing none but the Lord of the Worlds. He prayed two rak’ahs, then Al-Tirmidhi said: It is authentic. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Muammar told us, Abdul Warith told us, Yahya bin Abi Ishaq told us, he said: I heard Anas say: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Medina to Mecca, and he was praying two rak’ahs by two rak’ahs until we returned to Medina. I said: Did you stay in Mecca for a while? He said: We stayed there for ten. And thus the rest of the group narrated it through chains of transmission on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Ishaq Al-Hadrami. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Abi Ishaq, on the authority of Haritha bin Wahb Al-Khuza`i, who said: I prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the noon and afternoon prayers in Mina, more than the people, and two rak`ahs. And the group, except Ibn Majah, narrated it through chains of transmission on the authority of Abi Ishaq Al-Sabi`i on his authority, and the wording of Al-Bukhari: Abu Al-Walid narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, Abu Ishaq informed us, I heard Haritha bin Wahb, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with us two rak`ahs in Mina, and Al-Bukhari said: Musaddad narrated to us, Yahya narrated to us, Ubaydullah narrated to us, Nafi` informed me on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, who said: I prayed two rak`ahs with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman during the beginning of his caliphate, then he completed it. And Muslim narrated it likewise from the hadith of Yahya bin Sa`id Al-Qattan on his authority. Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah told us, Abd al-Wahid told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, Ibrahim told us, I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid say: Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, led us in prayer in four rak’ahs in Mina. It was said to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, about that, so he sought refuge in God, then he said: I prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mina in two rak’ahs, and I prayed with Abu Bakr in Mina in two rak’ahs, and I prayed with Umar ibn al-Khattab in Mina in two rak’ahs. If only my portion of four rak’ahs were two accepted rak’ahs. Al-Bukhari also narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri on the authority of al-A’mash on his authority, and Muslim narrated it through various chains of narrations on his authority, including on the authority of Qutaybah, as mentioned above. These hadiths clearly indicate that shortening is not a condition of fear. For this reason, some scholars said: What is meant by shortening here is shortening the manner, not the quantity. This is the opinion of Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi, as will be explained. They also supported themselves with what Imam Malik narrated on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: Prayer was made obligatory as two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs, when traveling and when at home. So the prayer of travel was kept, and it was increased in the prayer of home. This hadith was narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yusuf At-Tanisi, and Muslim on the authority of Yahya ibn Yahya, and Abu Dawud on the authority of Al-Qa’nabi, and An-Nasa’i on the authority of Qutaybah, all four of them on the authority of Malik. They said: If the origin of prayer when traveling is two, then how can what is meant by shortening here be shortening the quantity, because what is the origin is not said about it: There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer. And more explicitly indicative of this is what Imam Ahmad narrated: We were told by Wakee’, Sufyan, and Abdur-Rahman on the authority of Zubayd. Al-Yami, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: The prayer of travel is two rak’ahs, the prayer of Eid al-Adha is two rak’ahs, the prayer of Eid al-Fitr is two rak’ahs, and the Friday prayer is two rak’ahs, complete and not shortened, on the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And thus it was narrated by al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih through various chains of transmission on the authority of Zubayd al-Yami, and this is a chain of transmission that meets the conditions of Muslim. Muslim ruled in the introduction to his book that Ibn Abi Laila heard it from Umar, and it was stated explicitly in this hadith and others, and this is correct, God willing, even though Yahya ibn Ma’in, Abu Hatim, and al-Nasa’i said that he did not hear it from him. Based on this also: it occurred in some of the chains of transmission of Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili, on the authority of al-Thawri, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of al-Thiqa, on the authority of Umar, so he mentioned it. And in Ibn Majah, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad ibn Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Zubayd, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Ujrah, on the authority of Umar, and God knows best. Muslim narrated in his Sahih, and Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Abu ‘Uwanah al-Waddah ibn ‘Abdullah al-Yashkari. Muslim and al-Nasa’i added: and Ayoub ibn ‘Aid, both of them on the authority of Bakir ibn al-Akhns, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, who said: God enjoined prayer on the tongue of your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, four rak’ahs when at home, two rak’ahs when travelling, and one rak’ah when in fear. So just as one prays before and after it when at home, so too one prays when travelling. And Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Usamah bin Zaid from Tawus himself, so this is proven from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and it does not contradict what was mentioned previously from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, because she said that the original prayer is two rak’ahs, but it was added to the prayer of the resident, so when that was established, it was correct to say: The obligation of the prayer of the resident is four, as Ibn Abbas said - and God knows best - but the hadith of Ibn Abbas and Aisha agreed that the prayer of the traveler is two rak’ahs, and that it is complete and not shortened, as is stated clearly in the hadith of Omar, may God be pleased with him, and if that is the case then what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer is shortening the manner as in the prayer of fear, and for this reason He said: If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you verse, and for this reason He said after it: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer verse, so He explained what is meant by shortening here, and mentioned its description and manner, and for this reason when Al-Bukhari wrote the book of the prayer of fear, he began it with the Almighty’s saying: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer verse. To his saying: Indeed, God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment, and thus Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding his saying: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, he said: That is when fighting, the man riding prays two takbirs wherever his face is. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding his statement: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear the verse, that if a prayer is prayed as two rak’ahs while traveling, then it is a complete shortening, and it is not permissible except if one fears that the disbelievers will tempt him away from the prayer, in which case shortening is one rak’ah. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer on the day when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions were in Usfan, and the polytheists were in Dhujnan, and they agreed, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed the noon prayer with his companions as four rak’ahs, bowing, prostrating, and standing all together, and the polytheists wanted to raid their luggage and baggage. This was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Suddi, Jabir, and Ibn ‘Umar, and he also chose this, for he said after he narrated the statements on this: It is correct. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Umayyah ibn Abdullah ibn Khalid ibn Asid, that he said to Abdullah ibn Umar: We find in the Book of God the shortening of the prayer of fear, but we do not find the shortening of the prayer of the traveler. Abdullah said: We found our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, doing an action that we did. He called the prayer of fear shortened and applied the verse to it, not to the shortening of the prayer of the traveler. Ibn Umar approved of that, and he argued for shortening the prayer while traveling by the action of the Lawgiver, not by the text of the Qur’an. More explicit than this is what Ibn Jarir also narrated: Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi told us, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn Umar about the prayer of travel, and he said: Two rak’ahs are complete and not shortened. Shortening is only in the prayer of fear. I said: What is the prayer of fear? He said: The imam prays one rak’ah with a group, then these people come to the place of those people, and those people come to the place of those people, and he prays one rak’ah with them, so the imam has two rak’ahs, and each group has one rak’ah.
4:102: The prayer of fear has many types, because sometimes the enemy is facing the Qiblah, and sometimes he is not facing it, and the prayer is sometimes four-rak'ah, and sometimes three-rak'ah like Maghrib, and sometimes two-rak'ah like Fajr and the prayer of travel, then sometimes they pray in congregation, and sometimes the war is raging and they are not able to pray in congregation, but they pray individually facing the Qiblah and not facing it, and on foot or riding, and they can walk in this case and perform consecutive strokes in the text of the prayer. Some scholars said: They pray in this case one rak'ah based on the hadith of Ibn Abbas mentioned above, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the same. Al-Mundhiri said in Al-Hawashi: And Ata', Jabir, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Al-Hakam, Qatadah, Hammad said the same, and Tawus and Al-Dahhak agreed with it. Abu Asim Al-Abbadi narrated from Muhammad ibn Nasr Al-Marwazi: that he sees returning Fajr to one rak'ah in fear, and Ibn Hazm also agreed with him. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: As for fighting, one rak'ah is sufficient, with a gesture, and if you are not able to do so, then one prostration, because it is a remembrance of God. Others said: One takbir is sufficient, so perhaps he meant one rak'ah, as Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and his companions said, and Jabir ibn Abdullah, Abdullah ibn Omar, Ka'b, and more than one of the companions and al-Suddi said the same. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, but what they narrated was narrated based on its apparent meaning that one takbir is sufficient, as is the view of Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and Prince Abdul Wahhab ibn Bakht al-Makki went with it until he said: If he is not able to say the takbir, then he should not leave it in his mind, meaning with the intention. It was narrated by Saeed ibn Mansour in his Sunan on the authority of Ismail ibn Ayyash, on the authority of Shu'ayb ibn Dinar on his authority, and God knows best. Some scholars have permitted delaying the prayer for the excuse of fighting and combat, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed the noon and afternoon prayers on the day of the Confederates, praying them after sunset, then praying the sunset prayer after them, then the night prayer. And as he said after that on the day of Banu Qurayzah when he prepared the army for them: None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. The prayer caught up with them in the middle of the road, so some of them said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted us only to hasten the journey, and he did not want us to delay the prayer past its time, so they prayed the prayer at its time on the road.” Others of them delayed the afternoon prayer and prayed it in Banu Qurayzah after sunset, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not rebuke either group. We have spoken about this in the Book of the Biography and explained that those who prayed the afternoon prayer at its time were closer to hitting the truth in the matter itself, even though the others were also excused. The argument here is in their excuse for delaying the prayer for the sake of jihad and hastening to besiege the covenant-breakers from the cursed sect, the Jews. As for the majority, they said: All of this was abrogated by the fear prayer, as it had not been revealed yet. When it was revealed, delaying the prayer was abrogated for that reason. This is clear in the hadith of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, which was narrated by al-Shafi`i, may God have mercy on him, and the people of the Sunnah. However, what al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih is problematic for him, where he said: Chapter on Prayer when confronting fortresses and meeting the enemy Al-Awza’i said: If the conquest is ready and they are not able to pray, they should pray by gesturing, each person for himself. If they are not able to gesture, they should delay the prayer until the fighting ends or they feel safe, and they should pray two rak’ahs. If they are not able to, they should pray one rak’ah and two prostrations. If they are not able to, then the takbir is not sufficient for them and they should delay it until they feel safe. Makhul said the same. Anas bin Malik said: I was present at the confrontation with the fortress of Tustar at dawn, and the fighting became intense, so they were not able to pray, so we did not pray until after the sun had risen, so we prayed it while we were with Abu Musa, and it was opened for us. Anas said: What would please me with that worldly prayer and what is in it? End of what he mentioned. Then he followed it with the hadith of delaying the prayer on the Day of the Confederates, then with the hadith of his command to them not to pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah, and it seems as if he chose that, and God knows best. Whoever is inclined towards that may cite as evidence the actions of Abu Musa and his companions on the day of the conquest of Tustar, as it is often well-known. However, that was during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and it was not reported that he or any of the companions denounced them, and God knows best. These people said: The fear prayer was prescribed in the Trench because the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa’ was before the Trench, according to the majority of scholars of biography and military campaigns. Among those who stated that were Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Musa ibn Uqbah, al-Waqidi, Muhammad ibn Sa’d, his scribe, Khalifa ibn al-Khayyat, and others. Al-Bukhari and others said: Dhat al-Riqa’ was after the Trench, based on the hadith of Abu Musa, and it was not presented until Khaybar, and God knows best. The most amazing thing is that Al-Muzani, Abu Yusuf Al-Qadi, and Ibrahim bin Ismail bin Aliyah, went to the view that the prayer of fear was abrogated by his delaying the prayer on the day of the Trench, peace and blessings be upon him, and this is very strange, and the hadiths after the Trench have proven the prayer of fear, and the interpretation of delaying the prayer on that day based on what Makhul and Al-Awza’i said is stronger and closer, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer meaning if you lead them in prayer as an imam in the prayer of fear, and this is a different situation, for that is shortened to one rak’ah as indicated by the hadith - individually, by men and on horseback, facing the qiblah or not. Then he mentioned the situation of gathering and following one imam, and how good is the evidence that was used by those who held that the congregation is obligatory from this noble verse, as many actions were forgiven for the sake of the congregation, for if it were not obligatory, that would not have been permissible. As for those who used this verse as evidence that the prayer of fear was abrogated after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of his saying: And when you are among them, after him this characteristic is lost, then this is a weak evidence, and it is refuted like the saying of those who refuse to pay zakat, who used as evidence his saying: “Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and sanctify them, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a reassurance for them.” They said: So we do not pay our zakat after him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to anyone, rather we pay it with our own hands to whomever we see, and we pay it only to the one whose prayer, that is, his supplication. They settled for us, and despite this, the companions responded to them, and rejected this evidence, and forced them to pay zakat and killed those of them who refused it. Let us first mention the reason for the revelation of this noble verse before mentioning its description. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told me, Abdullah bin Hashim told us, Saif told us on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: A group of Banu Al-Najjar asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we travel throughout the land, so how do we pray? So God, the Almighty, revealed: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer. Then the revelation was cut off, and a year later, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on a military expedition and prayed the noon prayer, and the polytheists said: Muhammad and his companions have given you power over them, why did you not attack them more severely? One of them said: They have another like it in its wake. He said: So God the Almighty revealed between the two prayers: If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you the two verses, so the fear prayer was revealed. This is a very strange context, but some of it is supported by the narration of Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi, whose name is Zayd ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, according to Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunnah. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Usfan, and the polytheists, led by Khalid ibn al-Walid, faced us, and they were between us and the qiblah. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the noon prayer. They said: They were in a state that if we had caught them by surprise, then they said: Now a prayer will come upon them that is dearer to them than their children and themselves. He said: So Gabriel came down with these verses between the noon and afternoon prayers: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer He said: So I attended, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to take up arms. He said: So we lined up behind him. Two rows, he said: Then he bowed and we all bowed, then he raised his head and we all raised our heads, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated with the row next to him and the others were standing guarding them, and when they prostrated and stood, the others sat and prostrated in their places, then these came forward to the rows of those, and those came to the rows of those, then he bowed and they all bowed, then he raised his head and they all rose, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated with the row next to him and the others were standing guarding them, and when they sat, the others sat and prostrated, then he greeted them, then he left, he said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed it twice: once in Usfan, and once in the land of Banu Sulaym. Then Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Ghundar on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Mansur with a similar chain of transmission. And thus Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Sa’id ibn Mansur, on the authority of Jarir ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Shu’bah, and ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd al-Samad, all of them on the authority of Mansur with it. And this is a sound chain of transmission and it has many corroborating evidences, including what al-Bukhari narrated where he said: Haywah ibn Shuraih narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harb narrated to us on the authority of al-Zubaidi on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and the people stood up with him, so he said the takbir and they said the takbir with him, and he bowed and some of them bowed, then he prostrated and they prostrated with him, then he stood up for the second time and those who prostrated stood up and protected their brothers, and the other group came and they bowed and prostrated with him and the people were all in prayer, but they were protecting one another. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sulayman bin Qays Al-Yashkari, that he asked Jabir bin Abdullah about shortening the prayer, on which day it was revealed or which day it is, so Jabir said: We set out to meet a caravan of Quraysh coming from Ash-Sham until we were at Nakhalah, a man from the people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, are you afraid of me? He said: No. He said: Then who can protect you from me? He said: May God protect me from you. He said: “Then draw the sword, then threaten him and promise him, then call for departure and take up arms, then call for prayer, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with a group of the people and another group guarding them, so he prayed with those next to him two rak’ahs, then those next to him retreated on their heels, so they stood in the ranks of their companions, then the others came and he prayed with them two rak’ahs, and the others guarded them, then he said the salutation, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed four rak’ahs, and the people prayed two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs, on that day God revealed about shortening the prayer and commanding the believers to take up arms. Imam Ahmad narrated it and said: Surayj told us, Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Qays al-Yashkari, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought the Muharib of Khasfa. Then a man from among them called Ghawrath ibn al-Harith came and stood over the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his sword. He said: Who can protect you from me? He said: “God.” Then the sword fell from his hand, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and said: Who can protect you from me? He said: Be the best taker. He said: Do you bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God? He said: No, but I promise you that I will not fight you nor be with people who fight you. So he let him go. He came to his people and said: I have come to you from the best of people. When the time for prayer came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the prayer of fear. The people were divided into two groups: one group facing the enemy, and one group praying with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He prayed two rak’ahs with the group who were with him and they left, so they were in the place of the group who were facing the enemy. Then those who were facing the enemy left and prayed two rak’ahs with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed four rak’ahs, and the people prayed two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs. He was unique in this regard. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abu Qatan Amr bin Al-Haitham told us, Al-Masoudi told us on the authority of Yazid Al-Faqir, who said: I asked Jabir bin Abdullah about the two rak’ahs while traveling, the shortest of them? He said: The two rak’ahs while traveling are complete, the shortening is only one when fighting. While we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in fighting, the prayer was called, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and lined up a group, and a group faced the enemy, so he prayed one rak’ah with them and prostrated with them twice, then those who were left behind went to those and stood in their place and position towards this, and those came and stood behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he prayed one rak’ah with them and prostrated with them twice, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat down and said the greeting of peace, and those behind him said the greeting of peace, and those people said the greeting of peace, so it was two rak’ahs for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and one rak’ah for the people, then he recited: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer (al-Baqarah 2:17). Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Yazid al-Faqir, on the authority of Jabir ibn `Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them in the prayer of fear. A row stood in front of him and a row stood behind him, and he led those behind him in a rak`ah and two prostrations. Then these came forward until they stood in the place of their companions, and those came until they stood in the place of these, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them in a rak`ah and two prostrations, then he gave the salutation. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had two rak`ahs, and they had one rak`ah. Al-Nasa`i narrated it from the hadith of Shu`bah, and this hadith has chains of transmission from Jabir, and it is in Sahih Muslim from another chain of transmission with a different wording. Many people have narrated it from Jabir in the Sahihs, Sunans, and Musnads. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Naim bin Hammad told us, Abdullah bin Mubarak told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: And if you are among them and lead them in prayer, he said: It is the prayer of fear. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed one rak’ah with one of the two groups, and the other group faced the enemy, and the other group that was facing the enemy faced him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with them another rak’ah, then he greeted them, then each group of them stood up and prayed one rak’ah after another. This hadith was narrated by the group in their books on the authority of Muammar, and this hadith has many chains of transmission on the authority of the group of companions, and Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh did well in listing its chains of transmission and wording, as did Ibn Jarir, and we will edit it in the book Al-Ahkam Al-Kabir, God willing, and he is trustworthy. As for the command to carry weapons in the prayer of fear, it is considered by a group of scholars to be obligatory due to the apparent meaning of the verse, and it is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, and it is indicated by the words of God Almighty: And there is no blame upon you if you are harmed by rain or you are ill if you lay down your weapons and take your precautions meaning so that you are prepared if you need them and wear them without difficulty Indeed, God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
4:103: God Almighty commands frequent remembrance of God after the fear prayer, even though it is also permissible and desirable after other prayers. However, here it is more emphatic because of the ease with which it contains its pillars, and the permission to go and return during it, and other things that are not found in other prayers, as God Almighty said about the sacred months: So do not wrong yourselves therein. Even though this is forbidden in other prayers, it is more emphatic in them because of their intense sanctity and greatness. For this reason, God Almighty said: So when you have completed the prayer, remember God standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides, meaning in all your states. Then God Almighty said: And when you are secure, establish prayer, meaning when you are secure and fear has gone, and you are secure, establish prayer, meaning complete it and establish it as you have been commanded with its limits, humility, bowing, prostration, and all its affairs. God the Almighty said: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. Ibn Abbas said: That is, it is imposed. He also said: Prayer has a time like the time of Hajj. This was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Salim ibn Abdullah, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad ibn Ali, al-Hasan, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and Atiyah al-Awfi. Abd al-Razzaq said: On the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. Ibn Mas`ud said: Prayer has a time like the time of Hajj. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times. He said: Scheduled, whenever a star passes, a star comes, meaning whenever a time passes, a time comes. And the Almighty said: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy meaning do not weaken in pursuing your enemy, but rather strive to pursue them and fight them, and lie in wait for them at every ambush. If you are suffering, they are suffering as you are suffering meaning just as you are afflicted with wounds and killing, so will they be afflicted, as the Almighty said: If a wound should touch you, a similar wound has also touched the people then the Almighty said: And you hope from God that which they do not hope for meaning you and them are equal in what befalls you and them of wounds and pain, but you hope from God reward, victory and support as He promised you in His Book and on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is a true promise and a true report, and they do not hope for anything of that, so you are more deserving of jihad than they are and more eager for it, and for establishing the word of God and raising it high, And God is Knowing and Wise meaning He is All-Knowing and Most Wise in what He decrees, decrees, implements and executes of His cosmic and legal rulings, and He is the One to be praised in every case.

4:105: God Almighty says, addressing His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book with the truth, meaning it is the truth from God, and it includes the truth in its report and its request. His statement, So that you may judge between people by what God has shown you, was used as evidence by those scholars of the principles of jurisprudence who believed that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, could judge by ijtihad, based on this verse and what was established in the two Sahihs from the narrators of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Zainab bint Umm Salamah, on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard the clamor of a litigant at the door of his room, so he went out to them and said: “Behold, I am only a human being, and I only judge according to what I hear, and perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I judge in his favor. So whoever I judge in his favor regarding the right of a Muslim, then it is only a piece of fire, so let him carry it or leave it.” Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Usamah bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disputing. In an inheritance between them that had been studied, and they had no evidence, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in his argument than others, and I only judge between you according to what I hear, so whoever I judge for something from his brother’s right, he should not take it, for I am only giving him a piece of fire that he will bring as a slap around his neck on the Day of Resurrection.” The two men wept, and each of them said: My right belongs to my brother. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for what you have said, then go and divide it, then seek the truth between you, then draw lots, then let each of you release the other. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Usamah bin Zaid with it, and he added: I only judge between you according to my opinion in matters concerning which nothing was revealed to me. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A group of Ansar went out on a raid with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in one of his raids, and the armor of one of them was stolen, and I thought it was a man from the Ansar. The owner of the armor came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Tuma bin Ubayraq stole my armor. When the thief saw that, he took it and threw it in the house of an innocent man, and said to a group of his tribe: I hid the armor and threw it in the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him. So they went to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at night and said: “O Prophet of God, our companion is innocent and the owner of the armor is so-and-so, and we have knowledge of that, so excuse our companion in front of the people and argue on his behalf, for if God does not protect him through you, he will perish.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up, acquitted him and excused him in front of the people, and God revealed: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by that which God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the deceitful. And ask forgiveness of God, for God is Knowing.” He was Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Then God the Almighty said: “For those who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealing their lies, ‘They conceal themselves from the people, but they do not conceal themselves from God’” the two verses, meaning those who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealing themselves, arguing on behalf of the traitors. Then God the Almighty said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself the verse, meaning those who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealing their lies. Then He said: And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin meaning the thief and those who argued on behalf of the thief. This is a strange context, and Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and others mentioned this verse as well: It was revealed about the thief of Banu Ubayraq, despite their different contexts, which are similar. This story was narrated at length by Muhammad ibn Ishaq. Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said when interpreting this verse in his Jami`, and Ibn Jarir said in his interpretation: “Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu`ayb Abu Muslim al-Harrani told us, Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Qatada ibn al-Nu`man, may God be pleased with him, who said: There was a family among us called Banu Ubayraq, Bishr, Bashir, and Mubashir. Bashir was a hypocrite who used to write poetry satirizing the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he would attribute it to some Arab, then he would say: So-and-so said such-and-such, and so-and-so said such-and-such. When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard that poetry, they would say: By God, none but this wicked man would write this poetry, or something like that. They would say: Ibn al-Ubayraq said it. They said: They were a family of need and poverty in the pre-Islamic period and in Islam. The people’s only food in Medina was dates and barley. When a man was wealthy, a large quantity of food would arrive from Syria.” The man bought some of them and kept them for himself, but as for the family, their food was dates and barley. Then a heavy load arrived from Syria, and my uncle Rifa’ah ibn Zayd bought a load of dirhams and put them in his drinking place. In the drinking place were weapons, a shield and a sword. Then someone attacked him from under the house, so the drinking place was dug up and the food and weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa’ah came to me and said: O son of my brother, we were attacked last night, so our drinking place was dug up and our food and weapons were taken. He said: So we searched the house and asked, and we were told: We saw Banu Ubayraq lighting a fire this night and we see nothing but some of your food. He said: And Banu Ubayraq said - while we were asking in the house -: By God, we see that your companion is none other than Labid ibn Sahl, a man from among us who is righteous and Muslim. When Labid heard that, he drew his sword and said: Am I a thief?! By God, this sword will mix with you, or you will reveal this theft. They said: Go away from us, man, for you are not its owner. So we asked in the house until we had no doubt that they were its owners. My uncle said to me: O son of my brother, if you go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mention that to him. Qatada said: So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: A family of ours, people of rudeness, went to my uncle Rifa’ah ibn Zayd, dug into his drinking place, and took his weapons and food, so let them return our weapons to us. As for the food, we have no need of it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will order that. When Banu Ubayraq heard that, they went to a man of theirs called Aseer ibn Amr and spoke to him about that. Some people from the house gathered and said: O Messenger of God, Qatada ibn al-Nu’man and his uncle went to a family of ours, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or proof. Qatada said: So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and spoke to him. He said: I went to the people of A house was mentioned among them, Islam and righteousness, and you accused them of theft without evidence or proof. He said: So I returned and I wished that I had given away some of my money and not spoken to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that. Then my uncle Rifa’ah came to me and said: O son of my brother, what did you do? So I told him what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to me, and he said: God is the one sought for help. We did not wait long before the Qur’an was revealed: “Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between people by that which God has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the deceitful,” meaning the Banu Ubayraq. And seek forgiveness from God, meaning what I said to Qatada. “Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves,” until His saying, Merciful, meaning if they had sought forgiveness from God, He would have forgiven them. “And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And God is Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns a fault or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin,” their saying to al-Bayd, And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, until His saying, We will soon give him a great reward. When the Qur’an was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with the weapon and returned it to Rifa’ah. Qatada said: When you brought the weapon to my uncle, and he was an old man who had grown old or was in his late teens—the doubt is from Abu Bakr. Jesus - in the pre-Islamic era, and I saw his Islam as questionable when I brought him weapons. He said: O son of my brother, he is in the way of God. So I knew that his Islam was correct. When the Qur’an was revealed, Bashir joined the polytheists. It was revealed to Salafah bint Sa’d bin Sumayyah, and God the Almighty revealed: “And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination. Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates with God has certainly strayed far astray.” When it was revealed to Salafah bint Sa’d, Hassan bin Thabit satirized her with verses of poetry. She took his saddlebag and put it on her head, then went out with it, and threw it in the valley. Then she said: Hassan’s poetry was given to me as a gift. You did not bring me any good. The wording of al-Tirmidhi. Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith. We do not know anyone who narrated it except Muhammad bin Salamah al-Harrani. It was narrated by Yunus bin Bakir and others on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq on the authority of Asim bin Umar bin Qatada, without mentioning the chain of transmission on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of Hashim bin Al-Qasim Al-Harrani on the authority of Muhammad bin Salamah on his authority with some of it. It was narrated by Ibn Al-Mundhir in his Tafsir: Muhammad bin Ismail, meaning Al-Sayegh, told us, Al-Hasan bin Ahmad bin Shuaib Al-Harrani told us, Muhammad bin Salamah told us, and he mentioned it in full. It was narrated by Abu Al-Shaykh Al-Asbahani in his Tafsir on the authority of Muhammad bin Ayyash bin Ayoub and Al-Hasan bin Yaqub, both of them on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ahmad. Ibn Abi Shu`ayb al-Harrani narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Salamah, and then he said at the end of it: Muhammad ibn Salamah said: Yahya ibn Ma`in, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq ibn Isra`il heard this hadith from me. Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah al-Naysaburi narrated this hadith in his book al-Mustadrak on the authority of Ibn Abbas al-Asamm, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-`Attardi, on the authority of Yunus ibn Bakir, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, with a more complete meaning and in it is poetry. Then he said: This hadith is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, and they did not include it. God the Almighty says: They hide from people, but they do not hide from God verse. This is a denial of the hypocrites for hiding their ugly deeds from people so that they will not be denounced, and they declare them to God, because He knows their secrets and knows what is in their hearts. That is why He said: “And He is with them when they spend the night saying that which does not please Him. And God is encompassing of what they do.” This is a threat and warning to them. Then God the Almighty said: Here you are, you argued for them in the life of this world verse. That is, suppose that these people were victorious in this world with what they showed or was shown to them before the rulers who rule based on appearances and are obedient to that, then what will they do on the Day of Resurrection before God the Almighty who knows the secret and what is more hidden? And who will be their representative on that Day to promote their claim? That is, no one will be their representative on that Day. That is why He said: Or who will be their representative?

As for the food, we have no need of it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will order that. When Banu Ubayraq heard that, they went to a man of theirs called Aseer ibn Amr and spoke to him about that. Some people from the house gathered and said: O Messenger of God, Qatada ibn al-Nu’man and his uncle went to a family of ours, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or proof. He said: I went to the people of A house was mentioned among them, Islam and righteousness, and you accused them of theft without evidence or proof. And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves,” until His saying, Merciful, meaning if they had sought forgiveness from God, He would have forgiven them. “And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And God is Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns a fault or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin,” their saying to al-Bayd, And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, until His saying, We will soon give him a great reward. 4:110: God Almighty tells us about His generosity and kindness, that whoever repents to Him, He will accept his repentance from whatever sin he committed. God the Almighty said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said about this verse: God informed His servants of His pardon, patience, generosity, and the breadth of His mercy and forgiveness. So whoever commits a sin, whether small or great, and then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. Even if his sins were greater than the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad bin Muthanna told us, Muhammad bin Abi Uday told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, who said: Abdullah said: When one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, he would wake up with the expiation for that sin written on his door, and if urine got on something from him, he would cut it off with scissors. A man said: God has given the Children of Israel something better. Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, said: God has not given you anything better than what He has given them. He has made water a means of purification for you. God the Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, They remembered God and asked forgiveness for their sins, and he said: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful, and he also said: Yaqub told me, Hisham told us on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, who said: A woman came to Abdullah bin Mughaffal and asked him about a woman who committed adultery and became pregnant, and when she gave birth she killed her child. Abdullah bin Mughaffal said: Hell is hers, so she left while she was crying, so he called her and then said: I do not see your case as anything but one of two matters: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful, he said: So she wiped her eye and then went away. Imam Ahmad said: Abdurrahman bin Mahdi told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Mughira, who said: I heard Ali bin Rabi’ah from Banu Asad narrating on the authority of Asma’ or Ibn Asma’ from Banu Fazara, who said: Ali may God be pleased with him said: Whenever I heard something from the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), God would benefit me as He willed from it. Abu Bakr told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - he said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: There is no Muslim who commits a sin, then performs ablution, then prays two rak’ahs, then seeks God’s forgiveness for that sin, but that He will forgive him. And he recited these two verses: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself 1:17, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves 1:17. We have already discussed this hadith and attributed it to the one who narrated it from the authors of the Sunan, and we have mentioned what is in its chain of transmission of criticism in the Musnad of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him, and some of that was also mentioned in Surat Al-Imran. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his interpretation from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ali, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad told us, Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Harrani told us, Dawwad ibn Mihran al-Dabbagh told us, Umar ibn Yazid told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Khayr, on the authority of Ali, who said: I heard Abu Bakr - who is al-Siddiq - say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no servant who commits a sin and then stands up and performs ablution and does it well, then stands up and prays and seeks forgiveness for his sin, except that it is a right upon God to forgive him,” because God says: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself (al-Baqarah 2:174). Then he narrated it from the path of Abaan ibn Abi Ayyash on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of al-Siddiq, in a similar manner. This chain of transmission is not sound. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim told us, Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqi told us, Mubashar ibn Ismail al-Halabi told us, on the authority of Tamam ibn Nujayh, Ka’b ibn Dhal al-Azdi told me: I heard Abu al-Darda’ narrating: Whenever we sat around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had a need and stood up to do so and wanted to return, he would leave his shoes in his seat or some of what was on him, and he stood up and left his shoes. Abu al-Darda’ said: He took a bowl of water and I followed him. He passed for an hour and then returned without having completed his need. He said: “A messenger from my Lord came to me and said: ‘Whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful.’ So I wanted to give good report to my companions.” Abu Darda said: The verse before it, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was difficult for the people. So I said: O Messenger of God, what if he commits adultery or steals, then seeks forgiveness from his Lord, will He forgive him? He said: Yes. Then I said a second time, and he said: Yes. Then I said a third time, and he said: Yes, and if he commits adultery or steals, then seeks forgiveness from God, God will forgive him, in spite of Abu Darda’s nose. He said: So I saw Abu Darda hitting his own nose with his finger. This is a very strange hadith from this aspect and with this context, and there is weakness in its chain of transmission. And His saying: And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself verse, like His saying, the Most High: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another verse, meaning that no one can avail another, but rather every soul shall bear what it has done, and no one else shall bear it. For this reason, the Most High said: And God is Knowing and Wise verse, meaning that from His knowledge, wisdom, justice and mercy was that. Then He said: And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then throws it at an innocent person verse, meaning just as the Banu Ubayraq accused of their ugly deed that righteous man, who was Labid bin Sahl as mentioned in the hadith, or Zayd bin al-Sameen the Jew according to what others have said, and he was innocent while they were the oppressors and traitors, as God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that. Then this rebuke and this rebuke is general for them and for others who have their characteristics and committed a sin like theirs, so he shall receive a punishment like theirs. And his saying: “And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have surely resolved to mislead you. But they mislead none but themselves, and they cannot harm you at all.” Imam Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim Al-Harrani informed us in what he wrote to me, Muhammad bin Salamah told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Omar bin Qatada Al-Ansari, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Qatada bin Al-Nu’man, and he mentioned the story of Banu Ubayraq, so God revealed: “A party of them would have resolved to mislead you. But they mislead none but themselves, and they cannot harm you at all.” He meant Asid bin Urwah and his companions, meaning by that when they praised Banu Ubayraq and blamed Qatada bin Al-Nu’man for accusing them, although they were righteous and innocent, and the matter was not as they had conveyed it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason, God revealed the finality of the case and its clarification for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then He bestowed upon him His support for him in all circumstances, and His protection of him, and what He revealed to him of the Book, which is the Qur’an, and wisdom, which is the Sunnah, And taught you what you did not know. Learn, that is, before that was revealed to you, as in His statement: “And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was,” to the end of the surah. And God Almighty said: And you did not expect that the Book would be revealed to you except as a mercy from your Lord, and for this reason He said: And the favor of God upon you has been great.

Abu Bakr told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - he said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: There is no Muslim who commits a sin, then performs ablution, then prays two rak’ahs, then seeks God’s forgiveness for that sin, but that He will forgive him. And he recited these two verses: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself 1:17, And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves 1:17. We have already discussed this hadith and attributed it to the one who narrated it from the authors of the Sunan, and we have mentioned what is in its chain of transmission of criticism in the Musnad of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him, and some of that was also mentioned in Surat Al-Imran. Then he narrated it from the path of Abaan ibn Abi Ayyash on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of al-Siddiq, in a similar manner. This chain of transmission is not sound. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Duhaim told us, Ahmad ibn Hazim told us, Musa ibn Marwan al-Raqi told us, Mubashar ibn Ismail al-Halabi told us, on the authority of Tamam ibn Nujayh, Ka’b ibn Dhal al-Azdi told me: I heard Abu al-Darda’ narrating: Whenever we sat around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had a need and stood up to do so and wanted to return, he would leave his shoes in his seat or some of what was on him, and he stood up and left his shoes. Abu al-Darda’ said: He took a bowl of water and I followed him. He passed for an hour and then returned without having completed his need. He said: “A messenger from my Lord came to me and said: ‘Whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful.’ So I wanted to give good report to my companions.” Abu Darda said: The verse before it, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was difficult for the people. So I said: O Messenger of God, what if he commits adultery or steals, then seeks forgiveness from his Lord, will He forgive him? He said: Yes. Then I said a second time, and he said: Yes. Then I said a third time, and he said: Yes, and if he commits adultery or steals, then seeks forgiveness from God, God will forgive him, in spite of Abu Darda’s nose. He said: So I saw Abu Darda hitting his own nose with his finger. This is a very strange hadith from this aspect and with this context, and there is weakness in its chain of transmission. And His saying: And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself verse, like His saying, the Most High: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another verse, meaning that no one can avail another, but rather every soul shall bear what it has done, and no one else shall bear it. For this reason, the Most High said: And God is Knowing and Wise verse, meaning that from His knowledge, wisdom, justice and mercy was that. Then He said: And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then throws it at an innocent person verse, meaning just as the Banu Ubayraq accused of their ugly deed that righteous man, who was Labid bin Sahl as mentioned in the hadith, or Zayd bin al-Sameen the Jew according to what others have said, and he was innocent while they were the oppressors and traitors, as God informed His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that. Then this rebuke and this rebuke is general for them and for others who have their characteristics and committed a sin like theirs, so he shall receive a punishment like theirs.
