But they mislead none but themselves, and they cannot harm you at all.” Imam Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim Al-Harrani informed us in what he wrote to me, Muhammad bin Salamah told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Asim bin Omar bin Qatada Al-Ansari, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Qatada bin Al-Nu’man, and he mentioned the story of Banu Ubayraq, so God revealed: “A party of them would have resolved to mislead you. 4:114: God the Almighty says: There is no good in much of their private conversation meaning the speech of people except for those who enjoin charity or righteousness or conciliation between people meaning except for the private conversation of those who say that, as came in the hadith narrated by Ibn Mardawayh: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn al-Harith told us, Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Hunays told us, he said: We entered upon Sufyan al-Thawri to visit him, then Sa`id ibn Hassan al-Makhzumi entered upon us, and Sufyan al-Thawri said to him: The hadith that you told me on the authority of Umm Salih, repeat it to me, so he said: Umm Salih told me on the authority of Safiyyah bint Shaibah on the authority of Umm Habibah, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All the speech of the son of Adam is against him and not for him except the remembrance of God the Almighty, or enjoining what is right, or forbidding what is wrong. Sufyan said: Have you not heard God say in His Book: There is no good in much of their private conversation except for those who enjoin charity or righteousness or conciliation between people? This is exactly what it is, or have you not heard God say: The Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is right. This is exactly what it is, or have you not heard God say in His Book: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss. etc.? This is exactly what it is, and this hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunais from Sa`id ibn Hassan with it, and he did not mention the words of al-Thawri to the end, then al-Tirmidhi said: A strange hadith, it is not known except from the hadith of Ibn Khunais. Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, Salih bin Kaysan told us, Muhammad bin Muslim bin Ubaidullah bin Shihab told us that Humayd bin Abd al-Rahman bin Awf told him that his mother Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah told him that she heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The liar is not the one who reconciles between people by spreading good or saying good. She said: I did not hear him grant permission for anything that people say except in three cases: in war and reconciling between people, a man speaking to his wife, and a woman speaking to her husband. He said: Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah was one of the emigrant women who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated by all except Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on the authority of al-Zuhri with a similar word. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja’d, on the authority of Umm al-Darda’, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you of something better than the degree of fasting, prayer, and charity? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Reconciling people. He said: Corruption of people’s relations is the razor. Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah. At-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim narrated to us, Surayj bin Yunus narrated to us, Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah bin Omar narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Humaid, on the authority of Anas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Ayyub: Shall I not guide you to a trade? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Seek to reconcile people if they are at odds, and bring them together if they are estranged. Then Al-Bazzar and Abdul Rahman bin Abdullah Al-Amri said: He is gentle, and he narrated hadiths that were not corroborated. That is why he said: And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of God meaning sincerely in that, seeking reward for that from God Almighty, We will give him a great reward meaning a generous, abundant, and ample reward. His statement: And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him means whoever takes a path other than the path of the Shari’ah that the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought, and thus finds himself on one side, and the Shari’ah is on another side, and that is intentionally on his part after the truth has become clear to him and has become evident to him. And his saying: And follows other than the path of the believers this is consistent with the first description, but it may be a contradiction to the text of the Lawgiver, or it may be to what the Muhammadan nation agreed upon in what is known to be their agreement upon in order to achieve, for they have been guaranteed infallibility in their agreement from error as an honor to them and a glorification of their Prophet, and many authentic hadiths have been reported in that regard, we have mentioned a good portion of them in the book of hadiths of the principles, and some scholars have claimed that their meaning is transmitted, and what Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, relied upon in his argument that consensus is an argument that prohibits contradicting this noble verse after deliberation and long thought, and it is one of the best and strongest deductions, even though some of them have found it difficult and excluded the evidence from it for that, and for this reason God the Almighty threatened for that with His saying: We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination meaning if he follows this path, We will reward him for that by making it seem good in his heart and beautifying it for him as a lure for him, as God the Almighty said: “So leave Me and whoever denies this statement. We will lead them on gradually from where they do not know.” They know,” and God Almighty said: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate, and His statement: And We left them in their transgression wandering blindly, and He made Hell their destiny in the Hereafter, because whoever deviates from guidance will have no path except to Hell on the Day of Resurrection, as God Almighty said: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses, and God Almighty said: And the criminals will see the Fire and think that they will fall into it, but they will find no escape from it.

4:116: We have already discussed this noble verse, which is His statement: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that the verse, and we have mentioned the hadiths related to it at the beginning of this surah. Al-Tirmidhi narrated: The hadith of Thawir bin Abi Fakhitah Saeed bin Alaqah on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is dearer to me than this verse: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him the verse, then he said: This is hasan ghareeb. And His statement: And whoever associates others with God has certainly strayed far astray the verse, meaning he has taken a path other than the right path, and has strayed from guidance and distanced himself from what is right, and has ruined himself and lost himself in this world and the hereafter, and has missed out on happiness in this world and the hereafter. And His statement: They invoke not besides Him except female deities. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Mahmud ibn Ghailan told us, Al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, Al-Hasan ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Abu ibn Ka’b, who said: With every idol there is a jinn. And my father told us, Muhammad ibn Salamah Al-Bahili told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Hisham, meaning Ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aishah: They invoke not besides Him except female deities. She said: Idols. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Rahman, Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse: The polytheists said that the angels are the daughters of God, and we only worship them so that they may bring us closer to God. He said: So they took them as lords, and depicted them as female slaves, so they judged and imitated, and said: These resemble the daughters of God whom we worship, meaning the angels. This interpretation is similar to the words of God the Most High: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? 17:18, and the words of God the Most High: And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females 17:18, and the words of God the Most High: And they have made between Him and the jinn a relationship 17:18. Ali bin Abi Talhah and Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They invoke besides Him only females, he said: He means dead people. Mubarak said, meaning Ibn Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan: They invoke besides Him only females. Al-Hasan said: Females are everything dead that has no soul, either dry wood or dry stone. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and it is strange. And His statement: And they invoke none but a rebellious devil means that he is the one who commanded them to do that and made it good and attractive to them, and they are only worshipping Satan in reality, as God Almighty said: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? And God Almighty said, informing us about the angels that they will say on the Day of Resurrection about the polytheists who claimed to worship them in this world: Rather, they used to worship the jinn, most of them were believers in them. And His saying: May God curse him means He expelled him and removed him from His mercy, and took him out of His vicinity. And He said: I will surely take from among Your servants a specified portion meaning a specific, predetermined, and known portion. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hell, and one to Paradise. And I will mislead them meaning from the truth, and I will arouse in them false hopes meaning I will make abandoning repentance seem attractive to them, and I will prepare for them false hopes, and I will command them to procrastinate and delay, and I will deceive them from themselves. And His saying: And I will command them to slit the ears of cattle. Qatada, Al-Suddi and others said: It means splitting it and making it a mark and sign for the Bahira, Sa’ibah and Wasilah. And I will command them to change the creation of God. Ibn Abbas said: He means castrating animals. It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Anas, Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Ikrimah, Abu Ayyad, Qatada, Abu Salih and Al-Thawri. It has been reported in a hadith prohibiting that. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He means tattooing. In Sahih Muslim, it is prohibited to tattoo the face. In another version: May God curse whoever does that. In Sahih, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: May God curse the tattooers and those who get tattooed, the pluckers and those who get plucked, and those who file their teeth for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Then he said: Shall I not curse those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed, and they are in the Book of God, the Almighty and Majestic, meaning His statement: And whatever the Messenger has given you, take it, and whatever he has forbidden you, refrain from it. Ibn Abbas said in a narration from him, and Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Hakam, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and Ata’ al-Khurasani in his statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God meaning the religion of God, the Almighty, this is like his statement: “So set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. [Adhere to] the nature of God upon which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God” according to the statement of those who made that a command, meaning do not change the nature of God and leave people to their nature, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every child is born in a state of purity, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal is born whole. Do you find among them any with their ears mutilated?” And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Iyad ibn Himar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, said: I created My servants as pure believers, then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and prohibited for them what I had permitted for them.” Then God the Almighty said: And whoever takes Satan as a friend instead of God has certainly suffered a clear loss. That is, he has lost this world and the Hereafter, and that is a loss that cannot be compensated for or recovered. God the Almighty said: “He promises them and arouses false hopes. But Satan promises them nothing but delusion.” This is a statement about reality, for Satan promises his friends and arouses false hopes that they are the ones who will succeed in this world and the Hereafter. He lied and fabricated in that regard, and for this reason God the Almighty said: And Satan promises them nothing but delusion. God the Almighty also said, informing about Iblis on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:“And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, ‘Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me but blame yourselves. I cannot be your savior, nor can you be my savior. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.’” And His saying: Those meaning those who are pleased with Him in what He promised them and what He wished for them their refuge is Hell meaning their destiny and their final destination on the Day of Resurrection and they will find no escape from it meaning they have no escape from it, no way out, no deliverance, and no escape. Then the Almighty mentioned the state of the happy and the pious and what they will have in their final destination of complete honor, so the Almighty said: And those who believe and do righteous deeds meaning their hearts are sincere and their limbs do what they are commanded to do of good deeds, and they leave what they are forbidden from of evil deeds We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning they spend them as they wish and wherever they wish to abide therein forever meaning without passing away or moving The promise of God is true meaning this is a promise from God, and the promise of God is known to be true and will inevitably come to pass, and for this reason He confirmed it with the source that indicates the realization of the report, which is His saying truly, then the Almighty said: And who is more truthful than God in statement meaning no one is more truthful than Him in statement, meaning there is no god but Him and no lord but Him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say in His sermon: “The most truthful speech is the speech of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire.”

4:122: We have already discussed this noble verse, which is His statement: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that the verse, and we have mentioned the hadiths related to it at the beginning of this surah. Al-Tirmidhi narrated: The hadith of Thawir bin Abi Fakhitah Saeed bin Alaqah on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is dearer to me than this verse: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him the verse, then he said: This is hasan ghareeb. And His statement: And whoever associates others with God has certainly strayed far astray the verse, meaning he has taken a path other than the right path, and has strayed from guidance and distanced himself from what is right, and has ruined himself and lost himself in this world and the hereafter, and has missed out on happiness in this world and the hereafter. And His statement: They invoke not besides Him except female deities. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Mahmud ibn Ghailan told us, Al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, Al-Hasan ibn Waqid told us, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, on the authority of Abu ibn Ka’b, who said: With every idol there is a jinn. And my father told us, Muhammad ibn Salamah Al-Bahili told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Hisham, meaning Ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aishah: They invoke not besides Him except female deities. She said: Idols. And something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu Salamah ibn Abd Al-Rahman, Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Al-Suddi, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak regarding the verse: The polytheists said that the angels are the daughters of God, and we only worship them so that they may bring us closer to God. He said: So they took them as lords, and depicted them as female slaves, so they judged and imitated, and said: These resemble the daughters of God whom we worship, meaning the angels. This interpretation is similar to the words of God the Most High: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? 17:18, and the words of God the Most High: And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females 17:18, and the words of God the Most High: And they have made between Him and the jinn a relationship 17:18. Ali bin Abi Talhah and Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They invoke besides Him only females, he said: He means dead people. Mubarak said, meaning Ibn Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan: They invoke besides Him only females. Al-Hasan said: Females are everything dead that has no soul, either dry wood or dry stone. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and it is strange. And His statement: And they invoke none but a rebellious devil means that he is the one who commanded them to do that and made it good and attractive to them, and they are only worshipping Satan in reality, as God Almighty said: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? And God Almighty said, informing us about the angels that they will say on the Day of Resurrection about the polytheists who claimed to worship them in this world: Rather, they used to worship the jinn, most of them were believers in them. And His saying: May God curse him means He expelled him and removed him from His mercy, and took him out of His vicinity. And He said: I will surely take from among Your servants a specified portion meaning a specific, predetermined, and known portion. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will go to Hell, and one to Paradise. And I will mislead them meaning from the truth, and I will arouse in them false hopes meaning I will make abandoning repentance seem attractive to them, and I will prepare for them false hopes, and I will command them to procrastinate and delay, and I will deceive them from themselves. And His saying: And I will command them to slit the ears of cattle. Qatada, Al-Suddi and others said: It means splitting it and making it a mark and sign for the Bahira, Sa’ibah and Wasilah. And I will command them to change the creation of God. Ibn Abbas said: He means castrating animals. It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Anas, Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Ikrimah, Abu Ayyad, Qatada, Abu Salih and Al-Thawri. It has been reported in a hadith prohibiting that. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He means tattooing. In Sahih Muslim, it is prohibited to tattoo the face. In another version: May God curse whoever does that. In Sahih, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, he said: May God curse the tattooers and those who get tattooed, the pluckers and those who get plucked, and those who file their teeth for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God, the Almighty and Majestic. Then he said: Shall I not curse those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed, and they are in the Book of God, the Almighty and Majestic, meaning His statement: And whatever the Messenger has given you, take it, and whatever he has forbidden you, refrain from it. Ibn Abbas said in a narration from him, and Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Hakam, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and Ata’ al-Khurasani in his statement: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God meaning the religion of God, the Almighty, this is like his statement: “So set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. [Adhere to] the nature of God upon which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God” according to the statement of those who made that a command, meaning do not change the nature of God and leave people to their nature, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every child is born in a state of purity, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal is born whole. Do you find among them any with their ears mutilated?” And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Iyad ibn Himar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, said: I created My servants as pure believers, then the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion, and prohibited for them what I had permitted for them.” Then God the Almighty said: And whoever takes Satan as a friend instead of God has certainly suffered a clear loss. That is, he has lost this world and the Hereafter, and that is a loss that cannot be compensated for or recovered. God the Almighty said: “He promises them and arouses false hopes. But Satan promises them nothing but delusion.” This is a statement about reality, for Satan promises his friends and arouses false hopes that they are the ones who will succeed in this world and the Hereafter. He lied and fabricated in that regard, and for this reason God the Almighty said: And Satan promises them nothing but delusion. God the Almighty also said, informing about Iblis on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:“And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, ‘Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me but blame yourselves. I cannot be your savior, nor can you be my savior. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.’” And His saying: Those meaning those who are pleased with Him in what He promised them and what He wished for them their refuge is Hell meaning their destiny and their final destination on the Day of Resurrection and they will find no escape from it meaning they have no escape from it, no way out, no deliverance, and no escape. Then the Almighty mentioned the state of the happy and the pious and what they will have in their final destination of complete honor, so the Almighty said: And those who believe and do righteous deeds meaning their hearts are sincere and their limbs do what they are commanded to do of good deeds, and they leave what they are forbidden from of evil deeds We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning they spend them as they wish and wherever they wish to abide therein forever meaning without passing away or moving The promise of God is true meaning this is a promise from God, and the promise of God is known to be true and will inevitably come to pass, and for this reason He confirmed it with the source that indicates the realization of the report, which is His saying truly, then the Almighty said: And who is more truthful than God in statement meaning no one is more truthful than Him in statement, meaning there is no god but Him and no lord but Him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say in His sermon: “The most truthful speech is the speech of God, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire.”
4:123: Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted, so the People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, so we are closer to God than you. The Muslims said: We are closer to God than you and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes the books that came before it. So God revealed: “It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? The verse. Then God made the argument of the Muslims prevail over those who opposed them from the people of religions. This was also narrated from Al-Suddi, Masruq, Al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and others. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said about this verse: The people of religions quarreled, so the people of the Torah said: Our Book is the best of books, and our Prophet is the best of prophets. The people of the Gospel said the same, and the people of Islam said: There is no religion but Islam, and our Book abrogated every book, and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets. You were commanded and we were commanded to believe in your Book and work. By our Book, so God judged between them, and said: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And He chose between religions, saying: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? until His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend. Mujahid said: The Arabs said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished, and the Jews and Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, and they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment or wishful thinking, but rather what is established in the hearts and confirmed by actions. Not everyone who claims something will have his words heard simply by his claim, nor will everyone who says that he is on the truth be heard simply by that, so that he will have proof from God. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “It is not by your desires nor by the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” That is, is it not for you or for them to be saved simply by wishing? Rather, the point is to obey God Almighty and follow what He has legislated on the tongues of the noble messengers. That is why He said after it, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, like His saying, So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed, it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair, who said: I was told that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, how can there be success after this verse: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it”? So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not get sick? Do you not suffer from fatigue? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer from hardships?” He said: Yes. He said: Then it is among what you will be recompensed for. Saeed bin Mansour narrated it on the authority of Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on his authority, and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri on the authority of Ismail on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us on the authority of Ziyad al-Jassas, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Hisham bin Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya bin Abi Talib narrated to us, Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abdullah bin Umar said: Look at the place where Abdullah bin al-Zubayr was crucified and do not pass by it. He said: The boy forgot and Abdullah bin Umar looked at Ibn al-Zubayr and said: May God forgive you three times. By God, I only knew you to be fasting, standing in prayer and maintaining family ties. By God, I hope that despite the faults you have committed, God will not punish you after this. He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil in this world It was narrated by Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in his Musnad on the authority of al-Fadl ibn Sahl, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’, in an abbreviated form. Ibn al-Zubayr said in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamir al-Aruqi told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim ibn Hayyan told us, my father told me on the authority of my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bastam, who said: I was with Ibn Umar when he passed by Abd God ibn al-Zubayr while he was being crucified, so he said: May God have mercy on you, Abu Khabib, I heard your father, meaning al-Zubayr, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil will be punished for it in this world and the Hereafter.” Then he said: We do not know that it is narrated on the authority of al-Zubayr except from this source. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Kamil told us, Muhammad bin Saad Al-Awfi told us, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, Mawla bin Saba’ told me, he said: I heard Ibn Umar narrating on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, he said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this verse was revealed: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Then recite it to me. But I do not know except that I felt a split in my back until I stretched out for it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr? I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, which of us has not done evil, while we will be recompensed for every evil that we have done? The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your believing companions, you will be rewarded for that in this world until you meet God with no sins on your part. As for the others, that will be gathered together for them until they are rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection." This is how At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Musa and Abd ibn Hamid on the authority of Ruh ibn Ubadah. Then he said: Musa ibn Ubaydah is considered weak, and the freed slave of Ibn Saba' is unknown. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah told me, he said: When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: It has come as a backbreaker. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: They are only the calamities in this world. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Siddiq Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq Al-Askari told us, Muhammad ibn Amir Al-Saadi told us, Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Fadil ibn Ayyad told us on the authority of Salman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Muslim ibn Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said: O Messenger of God, how severe is this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Calamities, illnesses, and sorrows in this world are a recompense. Another path Ibn Jarir said: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad and Ahmad bin Mansour told me: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Abdul Malik bin Al-Hasan Al-Maharbi told us, Muhammad bin Zaid bin Qunfudh told us on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for everything we do? He said: O Abu Bakr, is such and such not happening to you? Is it expiation? Another hadith Saeed bin Mansour said: Abdullah bin Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Bakr bin Sawada informed him that Yazid bin Abi Yazid informed him on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha that a man recited this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he said: We will be recompensed for everything we know, then we will be lost. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Yes, the believer will be recompensed for it in this world, in his soul, in his body, in whatever harms him. Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Salamah ibn Bashir told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Amir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, I know the most severe verse in the Qur’an. He said: What is it, O Aisha? I said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: It is whatever befalls a believing slave, even a calamity befalls him. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hisham on his authority. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abu Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz on his authority. Another way Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Umayyah that she asked Aisha about this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. She said: No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “O Aisha, this is God’s pledge to the servant regarding what befalls him of fever, calamity, and thorns, even the merchandise that he puts in his sleeve, and he is alarmed by it, and he finds it in his pocket, so that the believer emerges from his sins, just as gold emerges from the bellows.” Another path Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Abu al-Qasim told us, Sarij ibn Yunus told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about this verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: The believer will be rewarded for everything, even when he is taken at death. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God said: If the sins of a servant increase and he has nothing to expiate them, God will test him with grief to expiate them for him. Another hadith Sa`id ibn Mansur said, on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, on the authority of `Umar ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah narrating that Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Be moderate and approach, for in everything that befalls a Muslim there is expiation, even a thorn that pricks him or a misfortune that befalls him. This is how Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah with it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ruh and Mu`tamir, both of them from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from `Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” we cried and were sad, and we said: O Messenger of God, this verse has not left anything behind. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it was revealed just as it was, but… Be glad, draw near, and strive hard, for no calamity befalls any of you in this world except that God expiates some of his sins because of it, even the thorn that pricks one of you in the foot.” Ata’ ibn Yasar said, on the authority of Abu Sa’id and Abu Hurayrah: They heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No fatigue, illness, or sorrow befalls a Muslim, even a worry that worries him, except that God expiates some of his sins. Narrated by both of them. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ishaq, Zainab bint Ka`b ibn `Ujrah told me on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: What do you think of these illnesses that afflict us? He said: They are expiations. My father said: And if you ask, he said: Even a thorn or anything greater than that. My father then invoked God against himself that the illness would not leave him until he died, that it would not distract him from Hajj, `Umrah, jihad in the way of God, or obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him except that he felt his heat until he died, may God be pleased with him. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another Hadith Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Husayn ibn Waqid on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: Yes, and whoever does a good deed will be recompensed for it tenfold, so whoever’s one good deed outweighs his tens perished. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Hamid on the authority of Al-Hasan, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: The disbeliever, then he recited: And do We recompense except the disbeliever? This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Saeed ibn Jubayr that they interpreted evil here as referring to polytheism as well. And His statement, And he will not find for himself besides God a protector or a helper, Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except that he repents, then God will accept his repentance. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and the correct view is that this is general in all deeds, based on the aforementioned Hadiths, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and God knows best. And His saying: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer, the verse, when He mentioned the recompense for bad deeds and that He must take what is due from the servant either in this world, which is better for him, or in the Hereafter, and we seek refuge with God from that, and we ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and pardon, forgiveness and pardon, He began to explain His kindness, generosity and mercy in accepting righteous deeds from His servants, males and females, on the condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them from their good deeds or even the amount of a speck, which is the speck in the back of a date pit. We have already spoken about the fatil, which is the thread in the slit of the pit, and this speck, which are both in the date pit, and likewise the qatmir, which is the wrapping on the date pit, and the three are in the Qur’an. Then God the Almighty said: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God sincerely works for his Lord Almighty, so he works out of faith and seeking reward, and is a doer of good meaning he follows in his work what God has prescribed for him, and what He sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth. And without these two conditions, the work of a worker is not valid, meaning it is sincere and correct. Sincerity is for God, and correctness is for it to follow the Shariah, so its outward appearance is correct by following, and its inward appearance is correct by sincerity. So when the work lacks one of these two conditions, it is corrupt. So when sincerity is lost, it is a hypocrite, and they are those who show off to people, and whoever loses following is misguided and ignorant. And when he combines them, it is the work of the believers, from whom the best of what they did is accepted and their bad deeds are overlooked, the verse. And for this reason God the Almighty said: And follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth and they are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection. As God Almighty said: Indeed, the people who have the most right to Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet verse, and God Almighty said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ The inclining toward truth is the one who intentionally turns away from polytheism, meaning he abandons it with insight, and turns to the truth with all his might, with no one turning him away from it, and no one turning him away from it. And His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend, this is from the perspective of encouraging people to follow him, because he is an imam who is followed, as he reached the ultimate goal of what the servants draw near to Him with, for he reached the level of friendship, which is the highest level of love, and that is only because of his frequent obedience to his Lord, as He described him with in His saying: And Abraham who fulfilled, many of the scholars of the Salaf said: meaning he carried out everything he was commanded to do in every station of worship, so no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a great matter from a small one. And God Almighty said: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them, the verse. God the Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God. The verse and the verse after it. Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu’adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer and recited: And God took Abraham as a friend. A man from the people said: The eye of Abraham’s mother has been comforted. Ibn Jarir mentioned in his interpretation of the hadith on the authority of some of them: God called him a friend because drought had befallen the people of his region, so he traveled to a friend of his from the people of Mosul. Some of them from the people of Egypt said: To buy food for his family from before him, but he did not find what he needed there. When he came close to his family, he settled in a desert with sand, and said: If only I filled my buckets with this sand so that my family would not be saddened by my returning to them without provisions, and so that they would think that I had brought them what they love. So he did that and the sand in the buckets turned into flour. When he reached His house was asleep, and his family got up and opened the ovens and found flour, so they kneaded it and baked bread. He woke up and asked them about the flour they baked, and they said: It is from the flour that you brought from your friend, so he said: Yes, it is from my friend, God, so God called him a friend, and there is a question about the authenticity of this and its occurrence, and its ultimate goal is that it is an Israelite report that is neither true nor false, and he was called the friend of God because of the intensity of his Lord’s love for him, the Almighty, for what he did of obedience that He loves and is pleased with, and for this reason it was established in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed them in the last sermon he delivered, he said: As for what follows, O people, if I were to take a friend from the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr bin Abi Quhafah as a friend, but your companion is the friend of God. It came through the path of Jundub bin Abdullah Al-Bajali and Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and Abdullah bin Masoud from the Prophet, who said: God took me as a friend, just as He took Abraham as a friend. Abu Bakr said: Ibn Mardawayh: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Ismail ibn Ahmad ibn Asid told us, Ibrahim ibn Yaqub al-Jawzjani told us in Mecca, Abdullah al-Hanafi told us, Zama’ah Abu Salih told us on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahran, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God sat waiting for him, so he came out and when he approached them he heard them discussing, so he heard their conversation, and some of them said: It is amazing that God has chosen a friend from among His creation, and Abraham is His friend. Another said: What is more amazing than that God spoke to Moses directly? Another said: Jesus is the spirit of God and His word. Another said: God chose Adam, so he came out to them and greeted them, and said: “I have heard your talk and your amazement that Abraham is the friend of God, and he is like that, and Moses is His speaker, and Jesus is His spirit and His word, and Adam was chosen by God and he is like that, and so did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Beware, I am the beloved of God, and I do not boast that I am the first intercessor and the first to be interceded for, and I do not boast that I am the first to move the ring of Paradise and God opens And he will let me enter it with the poor believers, and I am not boasting. I will be the most honorable of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I am not boasting.” This is a strange hadith from this aspect, and some of it has corroborating evidence in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Qatada said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Are you surprised that the friendship was for Abraham, the speech was for Moses, and the vision was for Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all? Narrated by Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari, and they did not include it. And it was also narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik and more than one of the Companions, Followers, and Imams from the early and later generations. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya bin Abdak Al-Qazwini told us, Muhammad, meaning Saeed bin Sabeq, told us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qais, told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Rashid, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, who said: Abraham, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out looking for someone to host him, but he did not find anyone to host him. So he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: O servant of God, why did you enter my house without my permission? He said: I entered it with the permission of its Lord. He said: Who are you? He said: I am the Angel of Death, my Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good report that God has taken him as a friend. He said: Who is he? By God, if you tell me about it, and he is in the farthest part of the country, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as his neighbor until death separates us. He said: That slave is you. He said: Me? He said: Yes. He said: Why did my Lord take me as a friend? He said: You give to people and do not ask them. And my father told us, Mahmoud bin Khalid Al-Sulami told us, Al-Walid told us on the authority of Ishaq bin Yasar, he said: When God took Abraham as a friend, He cast fear into his heart until the palpitations of his heart could be heard from afar as one hears the palpitations of birds in the air. And thus it came in the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he could hear a sizzling sound from his chest like the sizzling of a cauldron when it boils intensely from crying. And His statement: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth means that all of it is His, His servants and His creation, and He is the One who controls all of it. There is no one who can avert what He has decreed, nor can He challenge what He has ruled, nor can He be questioned about what He does due to His greatness, power, justice, wisdom, kindness and mercy. And His statement: And God encompasses all things means that His knowledge is comprehensive in all of it. Nothing of His servants is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller or larger than that. Not an atom’s weight of what is visible to the observers or what is hidden is hidden from Him.
4:124: Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted, so the People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, so we are closer to God than you. The Muslims said: We are closer to God than you and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes the books that came before it. So God revealed: “It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? The verse. Then God made the argument of the Muslims prevail over those who opposed them from the people of religions. This was also narrated from Al-Suddi, Masruq, Al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and others. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said about this verse: The people of religions quarreled, so the people of the Torah said: Our Book is the best of books, and our Prophet is the best of prophets. The people of the Gospel said the same, and the people of Islam said: There is no religion but Islam, and our Book abrogated every book, and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets. You were commanded and we were commanded to believe in your Book and work. By our Book, so God judged between them, and said: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And He chose between religions, saying: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? until His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend. Mujahid said: The Arabs said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished, and the Jews and Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, and they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment or wishful thinking, but rather what is established in the hearts and confirmed by actions. Not everyone who claims something will have his words heard simply by his claim, nor will everyone who says that he is on the truth be heard simply by that, so that he will have proof from God. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “It is not by your desires nor by the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” That is, is it not for you or for them to be saved simply by wishing? Rather, the point is to obey God Almighty and follow what He has legislated on the tongues of the noble messengers. That is why He said after it, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, like His saying, So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed, it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair, who said: I was told that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, how can there be success after this verse: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it”? So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not get sick? Do you not suffer from fatigue? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer from hardships?” He said: Yes. He said: Then it is among what you will be recompensed for. Saeed bin Mansour narrated it on the authority of Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on his authority, and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri on the authority of Ismail on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us on the authority of Ziyad al-Jassas, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Hisham bin Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya bin Abi Talib narrated to us, Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abdullah bin Umar said: Look at the place where Abdullah bin al-Zubayr was crucified and do not pass by it. He said: The boy forgot and Abdullah bin Umar looked at Ibn al-Zubayr and said: May God forgive you three times. By God, I only knew you to be fasting, standing in prayer and maintaining family ties. By God, I hope that despite the faults you have committed, God will not punish you after this. He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil in this world It was narrated by Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in his Musnad on the authority of al-Fadl ibn Sahl, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’, in an abbreviated form. Ibn al-Zubayr said in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamir al-Aruqi told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim ibn Hayyan told us, my father told me on the authority of my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bastam, who said: I was with Ibn Umar when he passed by Abd God ibn al-Zubayr while he was being crucified, so he said: May God have mercy on you, Abu Khabib, I heard your father, meaning al-Zubayr, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil will be punished for it in this world and the Hereafter.” Then he said: We do not know that it is narrated on the authority of al-Zubayr except from this source. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Kamil told us, Muhammad bin Saad Al-Awfi told us, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, Mawla bin Saba’ told me, he said: I heard Ibn Umar narrating on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, he said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this verse was revealed: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Then recite it to me. But I do not know except that I felt a split in my back until I stretched out for it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr? I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, which of us has not done evil, while we will be recompensed for every evil that we have done? The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your believing companions, you will be rewarded for that in this world until you meet God with no sins on your part. As for the others, that will be gathered together for them until they are rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection." This is how At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Musa and Abd ibn Hamid on the authority of Ruh ibn Ubadah. Then he said: Musa ibn Ubaydah is considered weak, and the freed slave of Ibn Saba' is unknown. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah told me, he said: When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: It has come as a backbreaker. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: They are only the calamities in this world. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Siddiq Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq Al-Askari told us, Muhammad ibn Amir Al-Saadi told us, Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Fadil ibn Ayyad told us on the authority of Salman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Muslim ibn Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said: O Messenger of God, how severe is this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Calamities, illnesses, and sorrows in this world are a recompense. Another path Ibn Jarir said: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad and Ahmad bin Mansour told me: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Abdul Malik bin Al-Hasan Al-Maharbi told us, Muhammad bin Zaid bin Qunfudh told us on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for everything we do? He said: O Abu Bakr, is such and such not happening to you? Is it expiation? Another hadith Saeed bin Mansour said: Abdullah bin Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Bakr bin Sawada informed him that Yazid bin Abi Yazid informed him on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha that a man recited this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he said: We will be recompensed for everything we know, then we will be lost. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Yes, the believer will be recompensed for it in this world, in his soul, in his body, in whatever harms him. Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Salamah ibn Bashir told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Amir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, I know the most severe verse in the Qur’an. He said: What is it, O Aisha? I said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: It is whatever befalls a believing slave, even a calamity befalls him. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hisham on his authority. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abu Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz on his authority. Another way Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Umayyah that she asked Aisha about this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. She said: No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “O Aisha, this is God’s pledge to the servant regarding what befalls him of fever, calamity, and thorns, even the merchandise that he puts in his sleeve, and he is alarmed by it, and he finds it in his pocket, so that the believer emerges from his sins, just as gold emerges from the bellows.” Another path Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Abu al-Qasim told us, Sarij ibn Yunus told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about this verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: The believer will be rewarded for everything, even when he is taken at death. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God said: If the sins of a servant increase and he has nothing to expiate them, God will test him with grief to expiate them for him. Another hadith Sa`id ibn Mansur said, on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, on the authority of `Umar ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah narrating that Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Be moderate and approach, for in everything that befalls a Muslim there is expiation, even a thorn that pricks him or a misfortune that befalls him. This is how Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah with it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ruh and Mu`tamir, both of them from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from `Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” we cried and were sad, and we said: O Messenger of God, this verse has not left anything behind. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it was revealed just as it was, but… Be glad, draw near, and strive hard, for no calamity befalls any of you in this world except that God expiates some of his sins because of it, even the thorn that pricks one of you in the foot.” Ata’ ibn Yasar said, on the authority of Abu Sa’id and Abu Hurayrah: They heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No fatigue, illness, or sorrow befalls a Muslim, even a worry that worries him, except that God expiates some of his sins. Narrated by both of them. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ishaq, Zainab bint Ka`b ibn `Ujrah told me on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: What do you think of these illnesses that afflict us? He said: They are expiations. My father said: And if you ask, he said: Even a thorn or anything greater than that. My father then invoked God against himself that the illness would not leave him until he died, that it would not distract him from Hajj, `Umrah, jihad in the way of God, or obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him except that he felt his heat until he died, may God be pleased with him. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another Hadith Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Husayn ibn Waqid on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: Yes, and whoever does a good deed will be recompensed for it tenfold, so whoever’s one good deed outweighs his tens perished. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Hamid on the authority of Al-Hasan, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: The disbeliever, then he recited: And do We recompense except the disbeliever? This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Saeed ibn Jubayr that they interpreted evil here as referring to polytheism as well. And His statement, And he will not find for himself besides God a protector or a helper, Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except that he repents, then God will accept his repentance. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and the correct view is that this is general in all deeds, based on the aforementioned Hadiths, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and God knows best. And His saying: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer, the verse, when He mentioned the recompense for bad deeds and that He must take what is due from the servant either in this world, which is better for him, or in the Hereafter, and we seek refuge with God from that, and we ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and pardon, forgiveness and pardon, He began to explain His kindness, generosity and mercy in accepting righteous deeds from His servants, males and females, on the condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them from their good deeds or even the amount of a speck, which is the speck in the back of a date pit. We have already spoken about the fatil, which is the thread in the slit of the pit, and this speck, which are both in the date pit, and likewise the qatmir, which is the wrapping on the date pit, and the three are in the Qur’an. Then God the Almighty said: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God sincerely works for his Lord Almighty, so he works out of faith and seeking reward, and is a doer of good meaning he follows in his work what God has prescribed for him, and what He sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth. And without these two conditions, the work of a worker is not valid, meaning it is sincere and correct. Sincerity is for God, and correctness is for it to follow the Shariah, so its outward appearance is correct by following, and its inward appearance is correct by sincerity. So when the work lacks one of these two conditions, it is corrupt. So when sincerity is lost, it is a hypocrite, and they are those who show off to people, and whoever loses following is misguided and ignorant. And when he combines them, it is the work of the believers, from whom the best of what they did is accepted and their bad deeds are overlooked, the verse. And for this reason God the Almighty said: And follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth and they are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection. As God Almighty said: Indeed, the people who have the most right to Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet verse, and God Almighty said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ The inclining toward truth is the one who intentionally turns away from polytheism, meaning he abandons it with insight, and turns to the truth with all his might, with no one turning him away from it, and no one turning him away from it. And His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend, this is from the perspective of encouraging people to follow him, because he is an imam who is followed, as he reached the ultimate goal of what the servants draw near to Him with, for he reached the level of friendship, which is the highest level of love, and that is only because of his frequent obedience to his Lord, as He described him with in His saying: And Abraham who fulfilled, many of the scholars of the Salaf said: meaning he carried out everything he was commanded to do in every station of worship, so no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a great matter from a small one. And God Almighty said: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them, the verse. God the Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God. The verse and the verse after it. Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu’adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer and recited: And God took Abraham as a friend. A man from the people said: The eye of Abraham’s mother has been comforted. Ibn Jarir mentioned in his interpretation of the hadith on the authority of some of them: God called him a friend because drought had befallen the people of his region, so he traveled to a friend of his from the people of Mosul. Some of them from the people of Egypt said: To buy food for his family from before him, but he did not find what he needed there. When he came close to his family, he settled in a desert with sand, and said: If only I filled my buckets with this sand so that my family would not be saddened by my returning to them without provisions, and so that they would think that I had brought them what they love. So he did that and the sand in the buckets turned into flour. When he reached His house was asleep, and his family got up and opened the ovens and found flour, so they kneaded it and baked bread. He woke up and asked them about the flour they baked, and they said: It is from the flour that you brought from your friend, so he said: Yes, it is from my friend, God, so God called him a friend, and there is a question about the authenticity of this and its occurrence, and its ultimate goal is that it is an Israelite report that is neither true nor false, and he was called the friend of God because of the intensity of his Lord’s love for him, the Almighty, for what he did of obedience that He loves and is pleased with, and for this reason it was established in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed them in the last sermon he delivered, he said: As for what follows, O people, if I were to take a friend from the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr bin Abi Quhafah as a friend, but your companion is the friend of God. It came through the path of Jundub bin Abdullah Al-Bajali and Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and Abdullah bin Masoud from the Prophet, who said: God took me as a friend, just as He took Abraham as a friend. Abu Bakr said: Ibn Mardawayh: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Ismail ibn Ahmad ibn Asid told us, Ibrahim ibn Yaqub al-Jawzjani told us in Mecca, Abdullah al-Hanafi told us, Zama’ah Abu Salih told us on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahran, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God sat waiting for him, so he came out and when he approached them he heard them discussing, so he heard their conversation, and some of them said: It is amazing that God has chosen a friend from among His creation, and Abraham is His friend. Another said: What is more amazing than that God spoke to Moses directly? Another said: Jesus is the spirit of God and His word. Another said: God chose Adam, so he came out to them and greeted them, and said: “I have heard your talk and your amazement that Abraham is the friend of God, and he is like that, and Moses is His speaker, and Jesus is His spirit and His word, and Adam was chosen by God and he is like that, and so did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Beware, I am the beloved of God, and I do not boast that I am the first intercessor and the first to be interceded for, and I do not boast that I am the first to move the ring of Paradise and God opens And he will let me enter it with the poor believers, and I am not boasting. I will be the most honorable of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I am not boasting.” This is a strange hadith from this aspect, and some of it has corroborating evidence in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Qatada said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Are you surprised that the friendship was for Abraham, the speech was for Moses, and the vision was for Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all? Narrated by Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari, and they did not include it. And it was also narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik and more than one of the Companions, Followers, and Imams from the early and later generations. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya bin Abdak Al-Qazwini told us, Muhammad, meaning Saeed bin Sabeq, told us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qais, told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Rashid, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, who said: Abraham, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out looking for someone to host him, but he did not find anyone to host him. So he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: O servant of God, why did you enter my house without my permission? He said: I entered it with the permission of its Lord. He said: Who are you? He said: I am the Angel of Death, my Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good report that God has taken him as a friend. He said: Who is he? By God, if you tell me about it, and he is in the farthest part of the country, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as his neighbor until death separates us. He said: That slave is you. He said: Me? He said: Yes. He said: Why did my Lord take me as a friend? He said: You give to people and do not ask them. And my father told us, Mahmoud bin Khalid Al-Sulami told us, Al-Walid told us on the authority of Ishaq bin Yasar, he said: When God took Abraham as a friend, He cast fear into his heart until the palpitations of his heart could be heard from afar as one hears the palpitations of birds in the air. And thus it came in the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he could hear a sizzling sound from his chest like the sizzling of a cauldron when it boils intensely from crying. And His statement: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth means that all of it is His, His servants and His creation, and He is the One who controls all of it. There is no one who can avert what He has decreed, nor can He challenge what He has ruled, nor can He be questioned about what He does due to His greatness, power, justice, wisdom, kindness and mercy. And His statement: And God encompasses all things means that His knowledge is comprehensive in all of it. Nothing of His servants is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller or larger than that. Not an atom’s weight of what is visible to the observers or what is hidden is hidden from Him.
4:125: Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted, so the People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, so we are closer to God than you. The Muslims said: We are closer to God than you and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes the books that came before it. So God revealed: “It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? The verse. Then God made the argument of the Muslims prevail over those who opposed them from the people of religions. This was also narrated from Al-Suddi, Masruq, Al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and others. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said about this verse: The people of religions quarreled, so the people of the Torah said: Our Book is the best of books, and our Prophet is the best of prophets. The people of the Gospel said the same, and the people of Islam said: There is no religion but Islam, and our Book abrogated every book, and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets. You were commanded and we were commanded to believe in your Book and work. By our Book, so God judged between them, and said: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And He chose between religions, saying: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? until His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend. Mujahid said: The Arabs said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished, and the Jews and Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, and they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment or wishful thinking, but rather what is established in the hearts and confirmed by actions. Not everyone who claims something will have his words heard simply by his claim, nor will everyone who says that he is on the truth be heard simply by that, so that he will have proof from God. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “It is not by your desires nor by the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” That is, is it not for you or for them to be saved simply by wishing? Rather, the point is to obey God Almighty and follow what He has legislated on the tongues of the noble messengers. That is why He said after it, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, like His saying, So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.
