It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed, it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair, who said: I was told that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, how can there be success after this verse: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it”? So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not get sick? Do you not suffer from fatigue? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer from hardships?” He said: Yes. He said: Then it is among what you will be recompensed for. Saeed bin Mansour narrated it on the authority of Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on his authority, and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri on the authority of Ismail on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us on the authority of Ziyad al-Jassas, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Hisham bin Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya bin Abi Talib narrated to us, Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abdullah bin Umar said: Look at the place where Abdullah bin al-Zubayr was crucified and do not pass by it. He said: The boy forgot and Abdullah bin Umar looked at Ibn al-Zubayr and said: May God forgive you three times. By God, I only knew you to be fasting, standing in prayer and maintaining family ties. By God, I hope that despite the faults you have committed, God will not punish you after this. He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil in this world It was narrated by Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in his Musnad on the authority of al-Fadl ibn Sahl, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’, in an abbreviated form. Ibn al-Zubayr said in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamir al-Aruqi told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim ibn Hayyan told us, my father told me on the authority of my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bastam, who said: I was with Ibn Umar when he passed by Abd God ibn al-Zubayr while he was being crucified, so he said: May God have mercy on you, Abu Khabib, I heard your father, meaning al-Zubayr, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil will be punished for it in this world and the Hereafter.” Then he said: We do not know that it is narrated on the authority of al-Zubayr except from this source. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Kamil told us, Muhammad bin Saad Al-Awfi told us, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, Mawla bin Saba’ told me, he said: I heard Ibn Umar narrating on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, he said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this verse was revealed: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Then recite it to me. But I do not know except that I felt a split in my back until I stretched out for it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr? I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, which of us has not done evil, while we will be recompensed for every evil that we have done? The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your believing companions, you will be rewarded for that in this world until you meet God with no sins on your part. As for the others, that will be gathered together for them until they are rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection." This is how At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Musa and Abd ibn Hamid on the authority of Ruh ibn Ubadah. Then he said: Musa ibn Ubaydah is considered weak, and the freed slave of Ibn Saba' is unknown. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah told me, he said: When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: It has come as a backbreaker. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: They are only the calamities in this world. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Siddiq Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq Al-Askari told us, Muhammad ibn Amir Al-Saadi told us, Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Fadil ibn Ayyad told us on the authority of Salman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Muslim ibn Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said: O Messenger of God, how severe is this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Calamities, illnesses, and sorrows in this world are a recompense. Another path Ibn Jarir said: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad and Ahmad bin Mansour told me: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Abdul Malik bin Al-Hasan Al-Maharbi told us, Muhammad bin Zaid bin Qunfudh told us on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for everything we do? He said: O Abu Bakr, is such and such not happening to you? Is it expiation? Another hadith Saeed bin Mansour said: Abdullah bin Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Bakr bin Sawada informed him that Yazid bin Abi Yazid informed him on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha that a man recited this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he said: We will be recompensed for everything we know, then we will be lost. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Yes, the believer will be recompensed for it in this world, in his soul, in his body, in whatever harms him. Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Salamah ibn Bashir told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Amir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, I know the most severe verse in the Qur’an. He said: What is it, O Aisha? I said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: It is whatever befalls a believing slave, even a calamity befalls him. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hisham on his authority. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abu Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz on his authority. Another way Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Umayyah that she asked Aisha about this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. She said: No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “O Aisha, this is God’s pledge to the servant regarding what befalls him of fever, calamity, and thorns, even the merchandise that he puts in his sleeve, and he is alarmed by it, and he finds it in his pocket, so that the believer emerges from his sins, just as gold emerges from the bellows.” Another path Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Abu al-Qasim told us, Sarij ibn Yunus told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about this verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: The believer will be rewarded for everything, even when he is taken at death. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God said: If the sins of a servant increase and he has nothing to expiate them, God will test him with grief to expiate them for him. Another hadith Sa`id ibn Mansur said, on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, on the authority of `Umar ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah narrating that Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Be moderate and approach, for in everything that befalls a Muslim there is expiation, even a thorn that pricks him or a misfortune that befalls him. This is how Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah with it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ruh and Mu`tamir, both of them from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from `Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” we cried and were sad, and we said: O Messenger of God, this verse has not left anything behind. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it was revealed just as it was, but… Be glad, draw near, and strive hard, for no calamity befalls any of you in this world except that God expiates some of his sins because of it, even the thorn that pricks one of you in the foot.” Ata’ ibn Yasar said, on the authority of Abu Sa’id and Abu Hurayrah: They heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No fatigue, illness, or sorrow befalls a Muslim, even a worry that worries him, except that God expiates some of his sins. Narrated by both of them. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ishaq, Zainab bint Ka`b ibn `Ujrah told me on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: What do you think of these illnesses that afflict us? He said: They are expiations. My father said: And if you ask, he said: Even a thorn or anything greater than that. My father then invoked God against himself that the illness would not leave him until he died, that it would not distract him from Hajj, `Umrah, jihad in the way of God, or obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him except that he felt his heat until he died, may God be pleased with him. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another Hadith Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Husayn ibn Waqid on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: Yes, and whoever does a good deed will be recompensed for it tenfold, so whoever’s one good deed outweighs his tens perished. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Hamid on the authority of Al-Hasan, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: The disbeliever, then he recited: And do We recompense except the disbeliever? This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Saeed ibn Jubayr that they interpreted evil here as referring to polytheism as well. And His statement, And he will not find for himself besides God a protector or a helper, Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except that he repents, then God will accept his repentance. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and the correct view is that this is general in all deeds, based on the aforementioned Hadiths, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and God knows best. And His saying: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer, the verse, when He mentioned the recompense for bad deeds and that He must take what is due from the servant either in this world, which is better for him, or in the Hereafter, and we seek refuge with God from that, and we ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and pardon, forgiveness and pardon, He began to explain His kindness, generosity and mercy in accepting righteous deeds from His servants, males and females, on the condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them from their good deeds or even the amount of a speck, which is the speck in the back of a date pit. We have already spoken about the fatil, which is the thread in the slit of the pit, and this speck, which are both in the date pit, and likewise the qatmir, which is the wrapping on the date pit, and the three are in the Qur’an. Then God the Almighty said: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God sincerely works for his Lord Almighty, so he works out of faith and seeking reward, and is a doer of good meaning he follows in his work what God has prescribed for him, and what He sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth. And without these two conditions, the work of a worker is not valid, meaning it is sincere and correct. Sincerity is for God, and correctness is for it to follow the Shariah, so its outward appearance is correct by following, and its inward appearance is correct by sincerity. So when the work lacks one of these two conditions, it is corrupt. So when sincerity is lost, it is a hypocrite, and they are those who show off to people, and whoever loses following is misguided and ignorant. And when he combines them, it is the work of the believers, from whom the best of what they did is accepted and their bad deeds are overlooked, the verse. And for this reason God the Almighty said: And follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth and they are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection. As God Almighty said: Indeed, the people who have the most right to Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet verse, and God Almighty said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ The inclining toward truth is the one who intentionally turns away from polytheism, meaning he abandons it with insight, and turns to the truth with all his might, with no one turning him away from it, and no one turning him away from it. And His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend, this is from the perspective of encouraging people to follow him, because he is an imam who is followed, as he reached the ultimate goal of what the servants draw near to Him with, for he reached the level of friendship, which is the highest level of love, and that is only because of his frequent obedience to his Lord, as He described him with in His saying: And Abraham who fulfilled, many of the scholars of the Salaf said: meaning he carried out everything he was commanded to do in every station of worship, so no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a great matter from a small one. And God Almighty said: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them, the verse. God the Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God. The verse and the verse after it. Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu’adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer and recited: And God took Abraham as a friend. A man from the people said: The eye of Abraham’s mother has been comforted. Ibn Jarir mentioned in his interpretation of the hadith on the authority of some of them: God called him a friend because drought had befallen the people of his region, so he traveled to a friend of his from the people of Mosul. Some of them from the people of Egypt said: To buy food for his family from before him, but he did not find what he needed there. When he came close to his family, he settled in a desert with sand, and said: If only I filled my buckets with this sand so that my family would not be saddened by my returning to them without provisions, and so that they would think that I had brought them what they love. So he did that and the sand in the buckets turned into flour. When he reached His house was asleep, and his family got up and opened the ovens and found flour, so they kneaded it and baked bread. He woke up and asked them about the flour they baked, and they said: It is from the flour that you brought from your friend, so he said: Yes, it is from my friend, God, so God called him a friend, and there is a question about the authenticity of this and its occurrence, and its ultimate goal is that it is an Israelite report that is neither true nor false, and he was called the friend of God because of the intensity of his Lord’s love for him, the Almighty, for what he did of obedience that He loves and is pleased with, and for this reason it was established in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed them in the last sermon he delivered, he said: As for what follows, O people, if I were to take a friend from the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr bin Abi Quhafah as a friend, but your companion is the friend of God. It came through the path of Jundub bin Abdullah Al-Bajali and Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and Abdullah bin Masoud from the Prophet, who said: God took me as a friend, just as He took Abraham as a friend. Abu Bakr said: Ibn Mardawayh: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Ismail ibn Ahmad ibn Asid told us, Ibrahim ibn Yaqub al-Jawzjani told us in Mecca, Abdullah al-Hanafi told us, Zama’ah Abu Salih told us on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahran, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God sat waiting for him, so he came out and when he approached them he heard them discussing, so he heard their conversation, and some of them said: It is amazing that God has chosen a friend from among His creation, and Abraham is His friend. Another said: What is more amazing than that God spoke to Moses directly? Another said: Jesus is the spirit of God and His word. Another said: God chose Adam, so he came out to them and greeted them, and said: “I have heard your talk and your amazement that Abraham is the friend of God, and he is like that, and Moses is His speaker, and Jesus is His spirit and His word, and Adam was chosen by God and he is like that, and so did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Beware, I am the beloved of God, and I do not boast that I am the first intercessor and the first to be interceded for, and I do not boast that I am the first to move the ring of Paradise and God opens And he will let me enter it with the poor believers, and I am not boasting. I will be the most honorable of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I am not boasting.” This is a strange hadith from this aspect, and some of it has corroborating evidence in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Qatada said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Are you surprised that the friendship was for Abraham, the speech was for Moses, and the vision was for Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all? Narrated by Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari, and they did not include it. And it was also narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik and more than one of the Companions, Followers, and Imams from the early and later generations. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya bin Abdak Al-Qazwini told us, Muhammad, meaning Saeed bin Sabeq, told us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qais, told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Rashid, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, who said: Abraham, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out looking for someone to host him, but he did not find anyone to host him. So he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: O servant of God, why did you enter my house without my permission? He said: I entered it with the permission of its Lord. He said: Who are you? He said: I am the Angel of Death, my Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good report that God has taken him as a friend. He said: Who is he? By God, if you tell me about it, and he is in the farthest part of the country, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as his neighbor until death separates us. He said: That slave is you. He said: Me? He said: Yes. He said: Why did my Lord take me as a friend? He said: You give to people and do not ask them. And my father told us, Mahmoud bin Khalid Al-Sulami told us, Al-Walid told us on the authority of Ishaq bin Yasar, he said: When God took Abraham as a friend, He cast fear into his heart until the palpitations of his heart could be heard from afar as one hears the palpitations of birds in the air. And thus it came in the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he could hear a sizzling sound from his chest like the sizzling of a cauldron when it boils intensely from crying. And His statement: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth means that all of it is His, His servants and His creation, and He is the One who controls all of it. There is no one who can avert what He has decreed, nor can He challenge what He has ruled, nor can He be questioned about what He does due to His greatness, power, justice, wisdom, kindness and mercy. And His statement: And God encompasses all things means that His knowledge is comprehensive in all of it. Nothing of His servants is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller or larger than that. Not an atom’s weight of what is visible to the observers or what is hidden is hidden from Him.
4:126: Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted, so the People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, so we are closer to God than you. The Muslims said: We are closer to God than you and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes the books that came before it. So God revealed: “It is not according to your desires nor the desires of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? The verse. Then God made the argument of the Muslims prevail over those who opposed them from the people of religions. This was also narrated from Al-Suddi, Masruq, Al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and others. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that he said about this verse: The people of religions quarreled, so the people of the Torah said: Our Book is the best of books, and our Prophet is the best of prophets. The people of the Gospel said the same, and the people of Islam said: There is no religion but Islam, and our Book abrogated every book, and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets. You were commanded and we were commanded to believe in your Book and work. By our Book, so God judged between them, and said: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” And He chose between religions, saying: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God while he is a doer of good? until His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend. Mujahid said: The Arabs said: We will not be resurrected and we will not be punished, and the Jews and Christians said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian, and they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. The meaning of this verse is that religion is not by adornment or wishful thinking, but rather what is established in the hearts and confirmed by actions. Not everyone who claims something will have his words heard simply by his claim, nor will everyone who says that he is on the truth be heard simply by that, so that he will have proof from God. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “It is not by your desires nor by the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it.” That is, is it not for you or for them to be saved simply by wishing? Rather, the point is to obey God Almighty and follow what He has legislated on the tongues of the noble messengers. That is why He said after it, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, like His saying, So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed, it was difficult for many of the Companions. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us, Ismail told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair, who said: I was told that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: O Messenger of God, how can there be success after this verse: “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it”? So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Do you not get sick? Do you not suffer from fatigue? Do you not grieve? Do you not suffer from hardships?” He said: Yes. He said: Then it is among what you will be recompensed for. Saeed bin Mansour narrated it on the authority of Khalaf bin Khalifa, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid on his authority, and Al-Hakim narrated it on the authority of Sufyan Ath-Thawri on the authority of Ismail on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us on the authority of Ziyad al-Jassas, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard Abu Bakr say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Muhammad bin Hisham bin Juhaymah narrated to us, Yahya bin Abi Talib narrated to us, Abdul Wahhab bin Ata’ narrated to us, Ziyad al-Jassas narrated to us on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Abdullah bin Umar said: Look at the place where Abdullah bin al-Zubayr was crucified and do not pass by it. He said: The boy forgot and Abdullah bin Umar looked at Ibn al-Zubayr and said: May God forgive you three times. By God, I only knew you to be fasting, standing in prayer and maintaining family ties. By God, I hope that despite the faults you have committed, God will not punish you after this. He said: Then he turned to me and said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil in this world It was narrated by Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in his Musnad on the authority of al-Fadl ibn Sahl, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata’, in an abbreviated form. Ibn al-Zubayr said in his Musnad: Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamir al-Aruqi told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim ibn Hayyan told us, my father told me on the authority of my grandfather Hayyan ibn Bastam, who said: I was with Ibn Umar when he passed by Abd God ibn al-Zubayr while he was being crucified, so he said: May God have mercy on you, Abu Khabib, I heard your father, meaning al-Zubayr, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever does evil will be punished for it in this world and the Hereafter.” Then he said: We do not know that it is narrated on the authority of al-Zubayr except from this source. Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Kamil told us, Muhammad bin Saad Al-Awfi told us, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, Mawla bin Saba’ told me, he said: I heard Ibn Umar narrating on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, he said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when this verse was revealed: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Then recite it to me. But I do not know except that I felt a split in my back until I stretched out for it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr? I said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, which of us has not done evil, while we will be recompensed for every evil that we have done? The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your believing companions, you will be rewarded for that in this world until you meet God with no sins on your part. As for the others, that will be gathered together for them until they are rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection." This is how At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Yahya ibn Musa and Abd ibn Hamid on the authority of Ruh ibn Ubadah. Then he said: Musa ibn Ubaydah is considered weak, and the freed slave of Ibn Saba' is unknown. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah told me, he said: When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: It has come as a backbreaker. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: They are only the calamities in this world. Another chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Siddiq Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ishaq Al-Askari told us, Muhammad ibn Amir Al-Saadi told us, Yahya ibn Yahya told us, Fadil ibn Ayyad told us on the authority of Salman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Muslim ibn Subaih, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq said: O Messenger of God, how severe is this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Calamities, illnesses, and sorrows in this world are a recompense. Another path Ibn Jarir said: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad and Ahmad bin Mansour told me: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Abdul Malik bin Al-Hasan Al-Maharbi told us, Muhammad bin Zaid bin Qunfudh told us on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for everything we do? He said: O Abu Bakr, is such and such not happening to you? Is it expiation? Another hadith Saeed bin Mansour said: Abdullah bin Wahb informed us, Amr bin Al-Harith informed me that Bakr bin Sawada informed him that Yazid bin Abi Yazid informed him on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, on the authority of Aisha that a man recited this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he said: We will be recompensed for everything we know, then we will be lost. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Yes, the believer will be recompensed for it in this world, in his soul, in his body, in whatever harms him. Another chain of transmission Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Salamah ibn Bashir told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Amir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, I know the most severe verse in the Qur’an. He said: What is it, O Aisha? I said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: It is whatever befalls a believing slave, even a calamity befalls him. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hisham on his authority. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Abu Amir Salih ibn Rustum al-Khazzaz on his authority. Another way Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd, on the authority of Umayyah that she asked Aisha about this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. She said: No one has asked me about this verse since I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “O Aisha, this is God’s pledge to the servant regarding what befalls him of fever, calamity, and thorns, even the merchandise that he puts in his sleeve, and he is alarmed by it, and he finds it in his pocket, so that the believer emerges from his sins, just as gold emerges from the bellows.” Another path Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Abu al-Qasim told us, Sarij ibn Yunus told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ismail, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhajir, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about this verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: The believer will be rewarded for everything, even when he is taken at death. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God said: If the sins of a servant increase and he has nothing to expiate them, God will test him with grief to expiate them for him. Another hadith Sa`id ibn Mansur said, on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, on the authority of `Umar ibn `Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhaysin, who heard Muhammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah narrating that Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Be moderate and approach, for in everything that befalls a Muslim there is expiation, even a thorn that pricks him or a misfortune that befalls him. This is how Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah, and Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah with it, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Ruh and Mu`tamir, both of them from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from `Abdullah ibn Ibrahim, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: When this verse was revealed, “It is not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,” we cried and were sad, and we said: O Messenger of God, this verse has not left anything behind. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it was revealed just as it was, but… Be glad, draw near, and strive hard, for no calamity befalls any of you in this world except that God expiates some of his sins because of it, even the thorn that pricks one of you in the foot.” Ata’ ibn Yasar said, on the authority of Abu Sa’id and Abu Hurayrah: They heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No fatigue, illness, or sorrow befalls a Muslim, even a worry that worries him, except that God expiates some of his sins. Narrated by both of them. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ishaq, Zainab bint Ka`b ibn `Ujrah told me on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: What do you think of these illnesses that afflict us? He said: They are expiations. My father said: And if you ask, he said: Even a thorn or anything greater than that. My father then invoked God against himself that the illness would not leave him until he died, that it would not distract him from Hajj, `Umrah, jihad in the way of God, or obligatory prayer in congregation. No one touched him except that he felt his heat until he died, may God be pleased with him. Ahmad alone transmitted it. Another Hadith Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Husayn ibn Waqid on the authority of Al-Kalbi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said: O Messenger of God, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: Yes, and whoever does a good deed will be recompensed for it tenfold, so whoever’s one good deed outweighs his tens perished. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us on the authority of Hamid on the authority of Al-Hasan, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, he said: The disbeliever, then he recited: And do We recompense except the disbeliever? This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Saeed ibn Jubayr that they interpreted evil here as referring to polytheism as well. And His statement, And he will not find for himself besides God a protector or a helper, Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except that he repents, then God will accept his repentance. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and the correct view is that this is general in all deeds, based on the aforementioned Hadiths, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and God knows best. And His saying: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer, the verse, when He mentioned the recompense for bad deeds and that He must take what is due from the servant either in this world, which is better for him, or in the Hereafter, and we seek refuge with God from that, and we ask Him for well-being in this world and the Hereafter, and pardon, forgiveness and pardon, He began to explain His kindness, generosity and mercy in accepting righteous deeds from His servants, males and females, on the condition of faith, and that He will admit them into Paradise and will not wrong them from their good deeds or even the amount of a speck, which is the speck in the back of a date pit. We have already spoken about the fatil, which is the thread in the slit of the pit, and this speck, which are both in the date pit, and likewise the qatmir, which is the wrapping on the date pit, and the three are in the Qur’an. Then God the Almighty said: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God sincerely works for his Lord Almighty, so he works out of faith and seeking reward, and is a doer of good meaning he follows in his work what God has prescribed for him, and what He sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth. And without these two conditions, the work of a worker is not valid, meaning it is sincere and correct. Sincerity is for God, and correctness is for it to follow the Shariah, so its outward appearance is correct by following, and its inward appearance is correct by sincerity. So when the work lacks one of these two conditions, it is corrupt. So when sincerity is lost, it is a hypocrite, and they are those who show off to people, and whoever loses following is misguided and ignorant. And when he combines them, it is the work of the believers, from whom the best of what they did is accepted and their bad deeds are overlooked, the verse. And for this reason God the Almighty said: And follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth and they are Muhammad and his followers until the Day of Resurrection. As God Almighty said: Indeed, the people who have the most right to Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet verse, and God Almighty said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ The inclining toward truth is the one who intentionally turns away from polytheism, meaning he abandons it with insight, and turns to the truth with all his might, with no one turning him away from it, and no one turning him away from it. And His saying: And God took Abraham as a friend, this is from the perspective of encouraging people to follow him, because he is an imam who is followed, as he reached the ultimate goal of what the servants draw near to Him with, for he reached the level of friendship, which is the highest level of love, and that is only because of his frequent obedience to his Lord, as He described him with in His saying: And Abraham who fulfilled, many of the scholars of the Salaf said: meaning he carried out everything he was commanded to do in every station of worship, so no great matter distracted him from a small one, nor a great matter from a small one. And God Almighty said: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them, the verse. God the Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God. The verse and the verse after it. Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: When Mu’adh came to Yemen, he led them in the dawn prayer and recited: And God took Abraham as a friend. A man from the people said: The eye of Abraham’s mother has been comforted. Ibn Jarir mentioned in his interpretation of the hadith on the authority of some of them: God called him a friend because drought had befallen the people of his region, so he traveled to a friend of his from the people of Mosul. Some of them from the people of Egypt said: To buy food for his family from before him, but he did not find what he needed there. When he came close to his family, he settled in a desert with sand, and said: If only I filled my buckets with this sand so that my family would not be saddened by my returning to them without provisions, and so that they would think that I had brought them what they love. So he did that and the sand in the buckets turned into flour. When he reached His house was asleep, and his family got up and opened the ovens and found flour, so they kneaded it and baked bread. He woke up and asked them about the flour they baked, and they said: It is from the flour that you brought from your friend, so he said: Yes, it is from my friend, God, so God called him a friend, and there is a question about the authenticity of this and its occurrence, and its ultimate goal is that it is an Israelite report that is neither true nor false, and he was called the friend of God because of the intensity of his Lord’s love for him, the Almighty, for what he did of obedience that He loves and is pleased with, and for this reason it was established in the two Sahihs from the narration of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed them in the last sermon he delivered, he said: As for what follows, O people, if I were to take a friend from the people of the earth, I would have taken Abu Bakr bin Abi Quhafah as a friend, but your companion is the friend of God. It came through the path of Jundub bin Abdullah Al-Bajali and Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and Abdullah bin Masoud from the Prophet, who said: God took me as a friend, just as He took Abraham as a friend. Abu Bakr said: Ibn Mardawayh: Abd al-Rahim ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, Ismail ibn Ahmad ibn Asid told us, Ibrahim ibn Yaqub al-Jawzjani told us in Mecca, Abdullah al-Hanafi told us, Zama’ah Abu Salih told us on the authority of Salamah ibn Wahran, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Some of the companions of the Messenger of God sat waiting for him, so he came out and when he approached them he heard them discussing, so he heard their conversation, and some of them said: It is amazing that God has chosen a friend from among His creation, and Abraham is His friend. Another said: What is more amazing than that God spoke to Moses directly? Another said: Jesus is the spirit of God and His word. Another said: God chose Adam, so he came out to them and greeted them, and said: “I have heard your talk and your amazement that Abraham is the friend of God, and he is like that, and Moses is His speaker, and Jesus is His spirit and His word, and Adam was chosen by God and he is like that, and so did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Beware, I am the beloved of God, and I do not boast that I am the first intercessor and the first to be interceded for, and I do not boast that I am the first to move the ring of Paradise and God opens And he will let me enter it with the poor believers, and I am not boasting. I will be the most honorable of the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, and I am not boasting.” This is a strange hadith from this aspect, and some of it has corroborating evidence in the Sahihs and elsewhere. Qatada said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Are you surprised that the friendship was for Abraham, the speech was for Moses, and the vision was for Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all? Narrated by Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, and he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari, and they did not include it. And it was also narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik and more than one of the Companions, Followers, and Imams from the early and later generations. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya bin Abdak Al-Qazwini told us, Muhammad, meaning Saeed bin Sabeq, told us, Amr, meaning Ibn Abi Qais, told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Rashid, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, who said: Abraham, peace be upon him, used to host people. One day he went out looking for someone to host him, but he did not find anyone to host him. So he returned to his house and found a man standing in it. He said: O servant of God, why did you enter my house without my permission? He said: I entered it with the permission of its Lord. He said: Who are you? He said: I am the Angel of Death, my Lord sent me to one of His servants to give him the good report that God has taken him as a friend. He said: Who is he? By God, if you tell me about it, and he is in the farthest part of the country, I will go to him, and I will not leave him as his neighbor until death separates us. He said: That slave is you. He said: Me? He said: Yes. He said: Why did my Lord take me as a friend? He said: You give to people and do not ask them. And my father told us, Mahmoud bin Khalid Al-Sulami told us, Al-Walid told us on the authority of Ishaq bin Yasar, he said: When God took Abraham as a friend, He cast fear into his heart until the palpitations of his heart could be heard from afar as one hears the palpitations of birds in the air. And thus it came in the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he could hear a sizzling sound from his chest like the sizzling of a cauldron when it boils intensely from crying. And His statement: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth means that all of it is His, His servants and His creation, and He is the One who controls all of it. There is no one who can avert what He has decreed, nor can He challenge what He has ruled, nor can He be questioned about what He does due to His greatness, power, justice, wisdom, kindness and mercy. And His statement: And God encompasses all things means that His knowledge is comprehensive in all of it. Nothing of His servants is hidden from Him, and not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth escapes His knowledge, nor anything smaller or larger than that. Not an atom’s weight of what is visible to the observers or what is hidden is hidden from Him.
4:127: Al-Bukhari said: Ubaid bin Ismail told us, Abu Usamah told us, Hisham bin Urwah told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: “And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book about orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and you desire to marry them.” Aisha said: It is a man who has an orphan girl and he is her guardian and heir, so she shares his wealth with him, even in the bunch of dates, so he desires to marry her and he hates to marry her to a man who shares his wealth with him, so he prevents her, so this verse was revealed. Muslim narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Kurayb, and on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, both of them on the authority of Usamah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: I read on the authority of Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Urwah bin Az-Zubayr told me, Aisha said: Then the people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a legal opinion. And after this verse in them, God revealed: “And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book” the verse. He said: And what God mentioned that is recited to him in the Book is the first verse in which God said: And if you fear that you will not be able to deal justly with orphan girls, then marry women of your choice and with this chain of transmission on the authority of Aisha, she said: And the statement of God, the Almighty, the Majestic: And you desire to marry them is the desire of one of you for his orphan girl who is in his care when she is of little wealth and beauty, so they were forbidden to marry those of the orphan women whose wealth and beauty they desired except with justice because of their desire for them, and its origin is proven in the two Sahihs through the path of Yunus bin Yazid al-Ayli with it, and the intended meaning is that if a man has an orphan girl in his care, it is permissible for him to marry her, and sometimes he desires to marry her, so God commanded him to give her a dowry similar to that of other women, and if he does not do so, then let him switch to other women, for God, the Almighty, the Majestic, has given plenty, and this is the meaning in the first verse in The beginning of the surah, and sometimes he has no desire for her because of her ugliness in his eyes or in the matter itself, so God Almighty forbade him from preventing her from marrying husbands for fear that they would share with him his wealth that was between him and her, as Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the verse, which is His saying: In the orphan girls the verse, the man in the pre-Islamic era would have an orphan girl with him and he would throw his garment over her, and if he did that no one would be able to marry her ever, so if she was beautiful and he desired her, he would marry her and eat her wealth, and if she was ugly, men would keep her away forever until she died, and when she died, he would inherit her, so God forbade that and prohibited it. He said in his statement: And the weak among children in the pre-Islamic era they were not given inheritance from the young or the girls, and that is his statement: Do not give them what is prescribed for them so God forbade that and explained to each person with a share his share, so he said: For the male is equal to the share of two females whether young or old, and this is what Saeed bin Jubair and others said, and Saeed bin Jubair said in his statement: And that you deal justly with orphans as if she was beautiful and wealthy, you marry her and keep her for yourself, likewise if she was neither wealthy nor beautiful, then marry her and keep her for yourself. And his statement: And whatever good you do - indeed, God is ever Knowing of it is an encouragement to do good deeds and obey the commands, and God the Almighty is aware of all of that, and He will reward for it with the most abundant and complete reward.
4:128: The Almighty says, informing and legislating about the situation of the spouses, sometimes in the case of the man’s aversion to the woman, sometimes in the case of his agreement with her, and sometimes in the case of his separation from her. The first situation is when the woman fears that her husband will be averse to her or turn away from her, then she has the right to waive her right or part of it, such as maintenance, clothing, a night’s stay, or any other right she has over him, and he has the right to accept that from her, so there is no blame on her for giving it to him, nor on him for accepting it from her. For this reason, the Almighty said: “There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves,” then He said: “And peace is better,” meaning than separation. And His statement: And the souls are aroused by greed, meaning peace in times of quarrel is better than separation. For this reason, when Sawdah bint Zam’ah grew old, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, decided to separate from her, so she made peace with him on the condition that he would keep her and leave her day to Aisha, so he accepted that from her and kept her as such. Mentioning the narration of that Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Sulayman ibn Muadh narrated to us on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Sawdah feared that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would divorce her, so she said: O Messenger of God, do not divorce me, and give my day to Aisha. So he did, and this verse was revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no blame upon them (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Abbas said: Whatever they agree upon is permissible. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, and he said: It is hasan ghareeb. Ash-Shafi’i said: Muslim told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died leaving nine wives, and he used to divide his time among eight. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said: When Sawdah bint Zam’ah grew old, she gave her day to Aisha, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to divide Sawdah’s day for her. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwa, on the authority of Aisha, something similar. Saeed bin Mansour said: Abd al-Rahman bin Abi al-Zinad informed us on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father Urwa, who said: God revealed about Sawda and those like her: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, because Sawda was an old woman, so she was afraid that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would leave her and she was miserly with her position with him. She knew of the love of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for Aisha and her position with him, so she gave her day from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Aisha, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted that. Al-Bayhaqi said: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Zinad in a connected chain of transmission. This is the way Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq Al-Faqih told us, Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ziyad told us, Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Al-Zinad told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha that she said to him: O son of my sister, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not prefer some of us over others in his stay with us, and there was hardly a day without him going around to us and approaching every woman without touching her until he reached the one whose day it was and he would spend the night with her. And Sawdah bint Zam’ah said when she had grown old and was afraid that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would leave her, O Messenger of God, this day is for Aisha, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted that. Aisha said: So it was about that that God revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion and Abu Dawud narrated it likewise on the authority of Ahmad ibn Yunus, and Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Bilal al-Ash’ari on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, with a similar narration, and on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, in an abbreviated form, and God knows best. Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dughuli said at the beginning of his dictionary: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Hisham al-Dastawai told us, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza told us: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent word to Sawdah bint Zam’ah to divorce her. When he came to her, she sat for him on the path of Aisha. When she saw him, she said to him: I ask you by the One who sent down His words to you and chose you over His creation, why do you take me back? I have grown old and have no need for men, but I want to be sent with your wives on the Day of Resurrection. So he took her back, and she said: I have dedicated my day and my night to the love of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a strange, mursal hadith. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Muqatil told us, Abdullah told us, Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or disdain, he said: A man has an elderly woman with him who he does not like much of and wants to separate from her, so she says: I will release you from my affair, so this verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir said: Wakee’ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, And if a woman fears desertion or evasion on the part of her husband, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves - and settlement is best. She said: This is about a woman who is with a man, and perhaps he will not be satisfied with her, and she will not have a child, and she will be a companion, so she says: Do not divorce me while you are free from my concern. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Hajjaj ibn Munhal narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears desertion or evasion on the part of her husband, she said: It is a man who has two wives, one of whom is old, or ugly, and he does not feel satisfied with her, so she says: Do not divorce me while you are free from my concern. This hadith is proven in the two Sahihs from more than one chain of narration on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, in a manner similar to what was mentioned, and praise and thanks be to God. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us on the authority of Ash’ath on the authority of Ibn Sirin who said: A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and asked him about a verse, and he disliked it so he hit him with a whip. Then another asked him about this verse: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, then he said about something like this, then ask. Then he said: This woman is with the man and has passed her age, so he marries the young woman in order to seek her child, so whatever they agree upon is permissible. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Hasanjani told us, Musaddad told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, who said: A man came to Ali bin Abi Talib and asked him about the statement of God Almighty: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, there is no blame upon them. Ali said: A man may be with a woman and his eyes turn away from her because of her ugliness or her old age, or her bad character, or her impudence, so he hates to leave him. If she gives him something from her dowry, it is permissible for him, and if she gives him some of her days, there is no blame. And Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah and Abu al-Ahwas, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Israel, all four of them on the authority of Samak on his authority. And this is how Ibn Abbas, Ubaydah al-Salmani, Mujahid ibn Jubayr, al-Sha’bi, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ata’, Atiyah al-Awfi, Makhul, al-Hasan, al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, Qatadah and more than one of the early Muslims and imams interpreted it. I do not know of any disagreement that this is what is meant by this verse, and God knows best. Al-Shafi’i said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, that the daughter of Muhammad ibn Muslim was married to Rafi’ ibn Khadij, and he disliked something from her, either because of arrogance or something else, so he wanted to divorce her, but she said: Do not divorce me and divide for me whatever you wish. So God, the Almighty, revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion 1:13. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar in a longer context than this. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Sulayman mentioned the reconciliation that God the Almighty said: “There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves, and peace is best.” It was mentioned to me that Rafi’ bin Khadij Al-Ansari, who was one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a wife until she grew old, then he married a young girl in addition to her. He preferred the young woman over her, so she asked him for a divorce, so he divorced her once, then he gave her time until she was almost permissible, so he took her back. Then he preferred the young woman over her again, so she asked him for a divorce, so he said to her: As you wish, only one divorce remains for you, so if you wish, you may settle for what you see as preference, and if you wish, I will separate from you. She said: No, rather I will settle for preference, so he kept her on that, and that was their reconciliation, and Rafi did not see any sin on him when she agreed to settle with him on the preference in what he preferred her with. And thus it was narrated in full by Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu al-Yaman, on the authority of Shu`ayb, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar, so he mentioned it in full, and God knows best. And his saying: And reconciliation is better. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means that giving her the choice between staying and separation is better than the husband persisting in favoring someone else over her. And what is apparent from the verse is that their reconciliation on the basis of giving up some of her rights to the husband and the husband accepting that is better than separation completely, just as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept Sawdah bint Zam’ah on the condition that she left her day to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and he did not separate from her, but rather he left her among his wives and he did that so that his nation would follow his example in the permissibility and permissibility of that, so it is better in his right, may God bless him and grant him peace. And since reconciliation is more beloved to God than separation, he said: And reconciliation is better. Rather, divorce is hateful to Him, the Most High, and for this reason it came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, all on the authority of Katheer bin Ubaid, on the authority of Muhammad bin Khalid, on the authority of Maruf bin Wasil, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most hated of permissible things to God is divorce. Then Abu Dawood narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Yunus, on the authority of Maruf, on the authority of Muharrib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned its meaning without a chain of transmission. And His saying: And if you do good and fear God, then indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted. And if you endure the hardship of patience for what you dislike from them and share for them an example similar to their peers, then indeed, God is aware of that and will reward you for that with the greatest reward. And the Almighty said: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so. That is, you, O people, will never be able to treat women equally in all respects, for even if the formal division occurs for a night and a night, there must be a difference in love, desire, and intercourse, as Ibn Abbas, Ubaydah al-Salmani, Mujahid, al-Hasan al-Basri, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Husayn al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malikah, who said: This verse And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so was revealed about Aisha, meaning that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved her more than others, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunnah from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yazid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would divide between his wives and be just, then he would say: O God, this is my division in what I own, so do not blame me in what You own, nor… “I own” means the heart. However, Al-Tirmidhi said: It was narrated by Hammad bin Zaid and others on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Abu Qilabah, without a chain of transmission. He said: This is more sound. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi bin Anas, As-Suddi and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Its meaning is neither married nor divorced. This is how Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Hammam bin Yahya from Qatadah. At-Tirmidhi said: Hammam only attributed it to him, and Hisham Ad-Dastawai narrated it from Qatadah. He said: It was said: This hadith is not known to be traced back to the Prophet except from the hadith of Hammam. And the statement: And if you amend and fear God, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning if you amend your affairs and divide justly what you own and fear God in all circumstances, God will forgive you for any inclination towards some women over others. Then God the Almighty said: “And if they separate, God will enrich each from His abundance. And ever is God All-Encompassing, All-Wise.” This is the third case, which is the case of separation. And God the Almighty has informed us that if they separate, then God will enrich him from her and she from him by God replacing him with someone who is better for him than her, and will replace her with someone who is better for her than him. And ever is God All-Encompassing, All-Wise, meaning He is Vast in His favor, Great in His grace, Wise in all His actions, decrees, and laws.

For this reason, the Almighty said: “There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves,” then He said: “And peace is better,” meaning than separation. And His statement: And the souls are aroused by greed, meaning peace in times of quarrel is better than separation. For this reason, when Sawdah bint Zam’ah grew old, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, decided to separate from her, so she made peace with him on the condition that he would keep her and leave her day to Aisha, so he accepted that from her and kept her as such.
