Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi said: Hammam informed us on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of An-Nadr bin Anas, on the authority of Bashir bin Nahik, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has two wives and inclines towards one of them, will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides hanging down. This is how Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Hammam bin Yahya from Qatadah. At-Tirmidhi said: Hammam only attributed it to him, and Hisham Ad-Dastawai narrated it from Qatadah. He said: It was said: This hadith is not known to be traced back to the Prophet except from the hadith of Hammam. And the statement: And if you amend and fear God, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning if you amend your affairs and divide justly what you own and fear God in all circumstances, God will forgive you for any inclination towards some women over others. Then God the Almighty said: “And if they separate, God will enrich each from His abundance. And ever is God All-Encompassing, All-Wise.” This is the third case, which is the case of separation. And God the Almighty has informed us that if they separate, then God will enrich him from her and she from him by God replacing him with someone who is better for him than her, and will replace her with someone who is better for her than him. And ever is God All-Encompassing, All-Wise, meaning He is Vast in His favor, Great in His grace, Wise in all His actions, decrees, and laws.
4:130: The Almighty says, informing and legislating about the situation of the spouses, sometimes in the case of the man’s aversion to the woman, sometimes in the case of his agreement with her, and sometimes in the case of his separation from her. The first situation is when the woman fears that her husband will be averse to her or turn away from her, then she has the right to waive her right or part of it, such as maintenance, clothing, a night’s stay, or any other right she has over him, and he has the right to accept that from her, so there is no blame on her for giving it to him, nor on him for accepting it from her. For this reason, the Almighty said: “There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves,” then He said: “And peace is better,” meaning than separation. And His statement: And the souls are aroused by greed, meaning peace in times of quarrel is better than separation. For this reason, when Sawdah bint Zam’ah grew old, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, decided to separate from her, so she made peace with him on the condition that he would keep her and leave her day to Aisha, so he accepted that from her and kept her as such. Mentioning the narration of that Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Sulayman ibn Muadh narrated to us on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Sawdah feared that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would divorce her, so she said: O Messenger of God, do not divorce me, and give my day to Aisha. So he did, and this verse was revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion, there is no blame upon them (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Abbas said: Whatever they agree upon is permissible. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, and he said: It is hasan ghareeb. Ash-Shafi’i said: Muslim told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died leaving nine wives, and he used to divide his time among eight. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said: When Sawdah bint Zam’ah grew old, she gave her day to Aisha, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to divide Sawdah’s day for her. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwa, on the authority of Aisha, something similar. Saeed bin Mansour said: Abd al-Rahman bin Abi al-Zinad informed us on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father Urwa, who said: God revealed about Sawda and those like her: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, because Sawda was an old woman, so she was afraid that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would leave her and she was miserly with her position with him. She knew of the love of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for Aisha and her position with him, so she gave her day from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Aisha, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted that. Al-Bayhaqi said: Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Zinad in a connected chain of transmission. This is the way Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq Al-Faqih told us, Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ziyad told us, Ahmad ibn Yunus told us, Abd Al-Rahman ibn Abi Al-Zinad told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha that she said to him: O son of my sister, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not prefer some of us over others in his stay with us, and there was hardly a day without him going around to us and approaching every woman without touching her until he reached the one whose day it was and he would spend the night with her. And Sawdah bint Zam’ah said when she had grown old and was afraid that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would leave her, O Messenger of God, this day is for Aisha, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted that. Aisha said: So it was about that that God revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion and Abu Dawud narrated it likewise on the authority of Ahmad ibn Yunus, and Al-Hakim in Al-Mustadrak, then he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Abu Bilal al-Ash’ari on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad, with a similar narration, and on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad al-Darawardi on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, in an abbreviated form, and God knows best. Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dughuli said at the beginning of his dictionary: Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, Hisham al-Dastawai told us, al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza told us: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent word to Sawdah bint Zam’ah to divorce her. When he came to her, she sat for him on the path of Aisha. When she saw him, she said to him: I ask you by the One who sent down His words to you and chose you over His creation, why do you take me back? I have grown old and have no need for men, but I want to be sent with your wives on the Day of Resurrection. So he took her back, and she said: I have dedicated my day and my night to the love of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a strange, mursal hadith. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Muqatil told us, Abdullah told us, Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or disdain, he said: A man has an elderly woman with him who he does not like much of and wants to separate from her, so she says: I will release you from my affair, so this verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir said: Wakee’ narrated to us, my father narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, And if a woman fears desertion or evasion on the part of her husband, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves - and settlement is best. She said: This is about a woman who is with a man, and perhaps he will not be satisfied with her, and she will not have a child, and she will be a companion, so she says: Do not divorce me while you are free from my concern. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Hajjaj ibn Munhal narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, regarding his statement: And if a woman fears desertion or evasion on the part of her husband, she said: It is a man who has two wives, one of whom is old, or ugly, and he does not feel satisfied with her, so she says: Do not divorce me while you are free from my concern. This hadith is proven in the two Sahihs from more than one chain of narration on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, in a manner similar to what was mentioned, and praise and thanks be to God. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us on the authority of Ash’ath on the authority of Ibn Sirin who said: A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and asked him about a verse, and he disliked it so he hit him with a whip. Then another asked him about this verse: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, then he said about something like this, then ask. Then he said: This woman is with the man and has passed her age, so he marries the young woman in order to seek her child, so whatever they agree upon is permissible. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Hasanjani told us, Musaddad told us, Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, who said: A man came to Ali bin Abi Talib and asked him about the statement of God Almighty: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, there is no blame upon them. Ali said: A man may be with a woman and his eyes turn away from her because of her ugliness or her old age, or her bad character, or her impudence, so he hates to leave him. If she gives him something from her dowry, it is permissible for him, and if she gives him some of her days, there is no blame. And Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah and Abu al-Ahwas, and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Israel, all four of them on the authority of Samak on his authority. And this is how Ibn Abbas, Ubaydah al-Salmani, Mujahid ibn Jubayr, al-Sha’bi, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ata’, Atiyah al-Awfi, Makhul, al-Hasan, al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, Qatadah and more than one of the early Muslims and imams interpreted it. I do not know of any disagreement that this is what is meant by this verse, and God knows best. Al-Shafi’i said: Ibn Uyaynah informed us on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, that the daughter of Muhammad ibn Muslim was married to Rafi’ ibn Khadij, and he disliked something from her, either because of arrogance or something else, so he wanted to divorce her, but she said: Do not divorce me and divide for me whatever you wish. So God, the Almighty, revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion 1:13. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar in a longer context than this. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Saeed bin Abi Amr told us, Abu Muhammad Ahmad bin Abdullah Al-Muzani told us, Ali bin Muhammad bin Isa told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shuaib bin Abi Hamza told me on the authority of Al-Zuhri, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Sulayman bin Yasar told me that the Sunnah in these two verses in which God mentioned the man’s rebellion and his turning away from his wife in His saying: And if a woman fears from her husband contempt or evasion to the end of the two verses, is that if a man rebels against his wife and prefers her over her, then it is right for him to offer her that he divorce her or that she stay with him based on what she preferred in the division of his wealth and himself, and that is good for him and her reconciliation is like that. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Sulayman mentioned the reconciliation that God the Almighty said: “There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves, and peace is best.” It was mentioned to me that Rafi’ bin Khadij Al-Ansari, who was one of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a wife until she grew old, then he married a young girl in addition to her. He preferred the young woman over her, so she asked him for a divorce, so he divorced her once, then he gave her time until she was almost permissible, so he took her back. Then he preferred the young woman over her again, so she asked him for a divorce, so he said to her: As you wish, only one divorce remains for you, so if you wish, you may settle for what you see as preference, and if you wish, I will separate from you. She said: No, rather I will settle for preference, so he kept her on that, and that was their reconciliation, and Rafi did not see any sin on him when she agreed to settle with him on the preference in what he preferred her with. And thus it was narrated in full by Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu al-Yaman, on the authority of Shu`ayb, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar, so he mentioned it in full, and God knows best. And his saying: And reconciliation is better. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means that giving her the choice between staying and separation is better than the husband persisting in favoring someone else over her. And what is apparent from the verse is that their reconciliation on the basis of giving up some of her rights to the husband and the husband accepting that is better than separation completely, just as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept Sawdah bint Zam’ah on the condition that she left her day to Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and he did not separate from her, but rather he left her among his wives and he did that so that his nation would follow his example in the permissibility and permissibility of that, so it is better in his right, may God bless him and grant him peace. And since reconciliation is more beloved to God than separation, he said: And reconciliation is better. Rather, divorce is hateful to Him, the Most High, and for this reason it came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, all on the authority of Katheer bin Ubaid, on the authority of Muhammad bin Khalid, on the authority of Maruf bin Wasil, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most hated of permissible things to God is divorce. Then Abu Dawood narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Yunus, on the authority of Maruf, on the authority of Muharrib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned its meaning without a chain of transmission. And His saying: And if you do good and fear God, then indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted. And if you endure the hardship of patience for what you dislike from them and share for them an example similar to their peers, then indeed, God is aware of that and will reward you for that with the greatest reward. And the Almighty said: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so. That is, you, O people, will never be able to treat women equally in all respects, for even if the formal division occurs for a night and a night, there must be a difference in love, desire, and intercourse, as Ibn Abbas, Ubaydah al-Salmani, Mujahid, al-Hasan al-Basri, and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Husayn al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malikah, who said: This verse And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so was revealed about Aisha, meaning that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved her more than others, as came in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunnah from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Yazid, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would divide between his wives and be just, then he would say: O God, this is my division in what I own, so do not blame me in what You own, nor… “I own” means the heart. This is the wording of Abu Dawud, and this is a sound chain of transmission. However, Al-Tirmidhi said: It was narrated by Hammad bin Zaid and others on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Abu Qilabah, without a chain of transmission. He said: This is more sound. And His statement: So do not incline completely means if you incline towards one of them, do not exaggerate in inclining completely, and leave her hanging meaning that the other one remains hanging. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi bin Anas, As-Suddi and Muqatil bin Hayyan said: Its meaning is neither married nor divorced. Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi said: Hammam informed us on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of An-Nadr bin Anas, on the authority of Bashir bin Nahik, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has two wives and inclines towards one of them, will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides hanging down. This is how Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunan narrated it from the hadith of Hammam bin Yahya from Qatadah. At-Tirmidhi said: Hammam only attributed it to him, and Hisham Ad-Dastawai narrated it from Qatadah. He said: It was said: This hadith is not known to be traced back to the Prophet except from the hadith of Hammam. And the statement: And if you amend and fear God, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning if you amend your affairs and divide justly what you own and fear God in all circumstances, God will forgive you for any inclination towards some women over others. Then God the Almighty said: “And if they separate, God will enrich each from His abundance. And ever is God All-Encompassing, All-Wise.” This is the third case, which is the case of separation. And God the Almighty has informed us that if they separate, then God will enrich him from her and she from him by God replacing him with someone who is better for him than her, and will replace her with someone who is better for her than him. And ever is God All-Encompassing, All-Wise, meaning He is Vast in His favor, Great in His grace, Wise in all His actions, decrees, and laws.
4:131: God the Almighty informs us that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth and that He is the Ruler over them, and for this reason He said: And We have enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you and upon you meaning We enjoined upon you what We enjoined upon them of fearing God the Almighty by worshipping Him alone with no partner. Then He said: But if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth the verse, just as God the Almighty said, informing us about Moses that he said to his al-Nas 114:If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy. And He said: "So they disbelieved and turned away, and God became Free of need, and God is Free of need of His servants, Praiseworthy meaning He is praised in all that He decrees and legislates. His statement: "And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs" meaning He is the One who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned, the Watchful Witness over everything. And His statement: “If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others. And God is ever competent to do that.” That is, He is able to do away with you and replace you with others if you disobey Him. And as He said: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you. And some of the Salaf said: How unimportant the servants are to God if they neglect His command. And God the Almighty said: “If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for God.” That is, it is not impossible for Him. And His statement: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. That is, O you who have no concern except this world, know that with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter, and if you ask Him for this, He will enrich you, give you, and satisfy you, as God the Almighty said: “And of the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter. And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’ Those will have a share of what they have earned.” And God the Almighty said: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest. And God the Almighty said: “Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn, reprehensible and banished. But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer - for those, their effort is ever appreciated. No, We extend to these and those from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord is never.” * Forbidden * Look how We have favored some of them over others "the verse, and Ibn Jarir claimed that the meaning of this verse is Whoever desires the reward of this world i.e. of the hypocrites who showed faith for that reason then with God is the reward of this world which is what he obtained of spoils and other things with the Muslims, and his saying: and the Hereafter i.e. and with God is the reward of the Hereafter which is what He has saved for them of punishment in the fire of Hell and made it like his saying: "Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein. But whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer - for those, their effort is ever appreciated. No, We extend to these and those from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord is never.” * Forbidden * Look how We have favored some of them over others the verse, and Ibn Jarir claimed that the meaning of this verse is Whoever desires the reward of this world" i.e. of the hypocrites who showed faith for that reason "then with God is the reward of this world" which is what he obtained of spoils and other things with the Muslims, and his saying: "and the Hereafter" i.e. and with God is the reward of the Hereafter which is what He has saved for them of punishment in the fire of Hell and made it like his saying: "Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We fully repay them for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire, and what they did therein will be in vain, and what they used to do will be in vain" There is no doubt that the meaning of this verse is clear, and as for his interpretation of the first verse with this, there is a consideration in it, for his saying: "then with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter" is clear in obtaining good in this world and the Hereafter i.e. in His hand this and that, so the one with limited ambition should not limit himself to striving for this world only, but let his ambition be lofty to attaining high demands in this world and the Hereafter, for all of that is referred to the One in Whose hand is harm and benefit, And He is God, there is no god but Him, who has divided happiness and misery among people in this world and the Hereafter, and has been just among them in what He knows of them, who deserves this and who deserves that. That is why He said: And God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
4:134: God the Almighty informs us that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth and that He is the Ruler over them, and for this reason He said: And We have enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you and upon you meaning We enjoined upon you what We enjoined upon them of fearing God the Almighty by worshipping Him alone with no partner. Then He said: But if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth the verse, just as God the Almighty said, informing us about Moses that he said to his al-Nas 114:If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy. And He said: "So they disbelieved and turned away, and God became Free of need, and God is Free of need of His servants, Praiseworthy meaning He is praised in all that He decrees and legislates. His statement: "And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs" meaning He is the One who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned, the Watchful Witness over everything. And His statement: “If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others. And God is ever competent to do that.” That is, He is able to do away with you and replace you with others if you disobey Him. And as He said: And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you. And some of the Salaf said: How unimportant the servants are to God if they neglect His command. And God the Almighty said: “If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for God.” That is, it is not impossible for Him. And His statement: Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. That is, O you who have no concern except this world, know that with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter, and if you ask Him for this, He will enrich you, give you, and satisfy you, as God the Almighty said: “And of the people is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ but he will have no share in the Hereafter. And among them is he who says, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.’ Those will have a share of what they have earned.” And God the Almighty said: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his harvest. 4:135: God the Almighty commands His believing servants to be upright in justice, that is, in fairness, so that they do not deviate from it to the right or to the left, and that they are not deterred by the blame of a blamer in God's cause, nor are they distracted from it by anyone, and that they are cooperative, helpful, supportive and supportive in it. His statement: Witnesses for God is like His statement: And establish the testimony for God meaning that its performance should be for the sake of God, then it will be correct, just, truly, free from distortion, alteration and concealment. For this reason He said: Even against yourselves meaning bear witness to the truth even if its harm comes back to you, and if you are asked about a matter, speak the truth in it even if its harm comes back to you, for God will make for the one who obeys Him a way out and a way out from every matter that constrains him. His statement: or parents and relatives means that if the testimony is against your parents and relatives, do not fear them in it, but bear witness to the truth even if its harm comes back to them, for the truth is the judge over everyone. His saying: If he is rich or poor, God is more worthy of them both. That is, do not take care of him because of his wealth, nor feel sorry for him because of his poverty. God takes care of them both. Rather, He is more worthy of them than you are, and He knows best what is best for them. And His statement: So do not follow your own desires to be just, meaning, do not let your own desires, partisanship, and people’s hatred of you lead you to abandon justice in your affairs and matters. Rather, adhere to justice in any situation, as God Almighty said: “And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.” And of this type is the statement of Abdullah bin Rawahah when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to estimate the fruits and crops of the people of Khaybar, and they wanted to bribe him to be kind to them, so he said: By God, I have come to you from the most beloved of creation to me, and you are more hateful to me than your numbers of monkeys and pigs. My love for him and my hatred for you do not lead me to be just toward you. They said: This is how the heavens and the earth were established. And the hadith will come with a chain of transmission in Surat Al-Ma’idah, God willing. And His statement: And if they distort or turn away, Mujahid and more than one of the Salaf said: Twist means they distort the testimony and change it, which is distortion and intentional lying. God Almighty said: And among them is a party who distort the Scripture with their tongues (al-Baqarah 2:17). Turning away is concealing the testimony and abandoning it. God Almighty said: And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best of the witnesses is the one who bears witness before he is asked for it. For this reason God threatened them with His statement: Then God is ever, with what you do, Knowing, meaning He will reward you for that.
4:136: God Almighty commands His believing servants to enter into all the laws of faith, its branches, pillars and supports, and this is not for the sake of obtaining the inevitable, but rather for the sake of completing the complete, confirming it, establishing it and continuing upon it, as the believer says in every prayer, Guide us to the straight path, meaning, guide us to it, increase our guidance and make us steadfast upon it. So He commanded them to believe in Him and in His Messenger, as God Almighty said, O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. And His statement: And the Book which He sent down to His Messenger means the Qur’an, and the Book which He sent down before and this is a category that includes all the previous books. And He said about the Qur’an: It was sent down because it was sent down in parts, in stages, according to what the servants needed in their worldly life and their afterlife. As for the previous books, they were sent down all at once, so God Almighty said: And the Book which He sent down before, then God Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray, meaning he has strayed from the path of guidance and has strayed far from the goal.
4:137: God the Almighty tells us about the one who entered into faith, then turned back from it, then returned to it, then returned and continued in his misguidance and increased until he died, then there is no repentance after his death, nor will God forgive him, nor will He make for him a way out or a way out from what he is in, nor a path to guidance. For this reason He said: God would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a way. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abdah told us, Hafs ibn Juma' told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: Then they increased in disbelief, he said: They persisted in their disbelief until they died, and Mujahid said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Jabir al-Mualla on the authority of Aamer al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: The apostate is given three times to repent, then he recited this verse: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - never will God forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way. Then he said: Give the hypocrites tidings that they will have a painful punishment. He meant that the hypocrites are of this description, for they believed then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed. Then he described them as taking the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, meaning that they are with them in reality, befriending them and showing them affection, and they say to them when they are alone with them: We are only with you, we are only mocking, meaning the believers, in our outward appearance of agreement with them. God Almighty said, denouncing them for their behavior of befriending the disbelievers: Do they seek honor with them? Then God Almighty informed that all honor is His alone, with no partner for Him, and for whomever He has given it, as God Almighty said in the other verse: Whoever desires honor, to God belongs all honor. God the Almighty said: To God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know. The purpose of this is to encourage people to seek honor from God, to turn to His worship, and to be included among His believing servants who will be granted victory in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. It is appropriate here to mention the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Husayn ibn Muhammad told us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash ibn Hamid al-Kindi told us, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Nusay, on the authority of Abu Rayhanah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever claims to have nine infidel fathers, seeking honor and pride through them, will be the tenth of them in the Fire. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it, and this Abu Rayhanah is from Azd, and it is said that he is from Ansar, and his name is Shimon, with the voiced letter, according to what al-Bukhari said, and others said: with the silent letter, and God knows best. And His statement: “And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of God being denied and ridiculed, then do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation. Indeed, then you would be like them.” That is, if you commit the prohibition after it has reached you and are satisfied to sit with them in a place where the verses of God are denied, ridiculed and belittled, and you approve of them doing so, then you have shared in what they are doing. For this reason, the Most High said: Indeed, then you would be like them in the sin, as came in the hadith: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table where wine is being passed around. What is referred to in this verse of the prohibition in that is the statement of the Most High in Surat Al-An’am, which is Meccan: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them al-An’am. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This verse in Surat Al-An’am abrogated, meaning His statement: Indeed, then you would be like them because of His statement: And there is not upon those who fear God any account of their account, but it is a reminder that perhaps they will fear God. And His saying: Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together, meaning just as they shared in disbelief, so God will share with them in eternal Hellfire forever and will gather them in the abode of punishment and chastisement, chains and shackles, and the drink of boiling water and pure water, not pure water.

4:141: The Almighty tells us about the hypocrites that they are waiting for the believers to go to evil circles, meaning they are waiting for their state to fall, for disbelief to appear among them, and for their religion to go away. But if you have a victory from God, meaning victory, support, triumph, and spoils, they will say, ‘Were we not with you?’ meaning they are currying favor with the believers with this statement. And if the disbelievers have a share, meaning they are sometimes given the upper hand over the believers, as happened on the Day of Uhud, for the messengers are tested and then they have the consequences. They will say, ‘Did we not gain control over you and protect you from the believers?’ meaning we helped you in secret, and we did not spare them any confusion or discouragement until you were victorious over them. Al-Suddi said: We gain control over you, we will overcome you, like His statement: Satan gained control over them. This is also a way of currying favor with them, for they were flattering these and those so that they would gain favor with them and be safe from their plots, and that is only because of their weak faith and little conviction. The Almighty said: Then God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, meaning according to what He knows of you, O you. Hypocrites are among the evil inward beings, so do not be deceived by the outward application of the Sharia rulings to you in this worldly life, because there is wisdom in that. On the Day of Resurrection, your outward appearances will not benefit you, but it is a day on which the secrets will be exposed and what is in the chests will be revealed. And his saying: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. Abd al-Razzaq said: Al-Thawri informed us on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Dhirr, on the authority of Subay’ al-Kindi, who said: A man came to Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: How is this verse And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers? Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Bring him closer, bring him closer, for God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. And Ibn Jurayj narrated likewise on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. He said: That is on the Day of Resurrection. And al-Suddi narrated likewise on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ashja’i, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Suddi said: A way, i.e. an argument. It is possible that the meaning is that God will not give the disbelievers a way over the believers, i.e. in this world, by having them completely take control of them, and if they sometimes gain victory over some people, then the outcome is for the righteous in this world and the hereafter, as God Almighty said: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world Al-Ma’idah 2:17. Based on this, it is a response to the hypocrites regarding what they hoped for, hoped for, and awaited regarding the disappearance of the state of the believers, and regarding what they followed in their dealings with the disbelievers out of fear for themselves from them if they were to prevail over the believers and eradicate them, as God Almighty said: “Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening into them, saying, ‘We fear that a misfortune may strike us.’ But perhaps God will bring about victory or a decision from Him, and they will become, over what they have concealed within themselves, regretful.” Many scholars have used this noble verse as evidence for the most correct of the two opinions of scholars, which is the prohibition of selling a Muslim slave to a disbeliever, because in the validity of his purchase there is power over him and humiliation. And those of them who said that it is valid, it orders him to remove He took control of it immediately, as God Almighty said: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers.
4:142: It was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah that God the Almighty said: They deceive God and those who believe, and He said here: Indeed, the hypocrites deceive God, and it is He who deceives them, and there is no doubt that God does not deceive, for He is the All-Knowing of secrets and consciences, but the hypocrites, due to their ignorance and lack of knowledge and intellect, believe that their matter is as it is popular among the people and the rulings of the Shari'ah are applied to them outwardly, so their judgment will be with God on the Day of Resurrection and that their matter will be popular with Him, as God the Almighty informed us about them that on the Day of Resurrection they will swear to Him that they were on the right path and correctness, and they believe that this is beneficial to them with Him, as God the Almighty said: The Day God will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and His saying: He is the one who deceives them means He is the one who lures them into their transgression and misguidance, and disappoints them from the truth and reaching it in this world, and likewise on the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: "The Day the hypocrites, men and women, will say to those who believe, 'Wait a minute, so that we may learn from the Your light. It was said, "Go back behind you and seek light." Then a wall was set up between them with a door, inside of which is mercy, but outside of it is torment. They will call out to them, "Were we not with you? They will say, Yes, but you tempted yourselves and waited and doubted, and wishful thinking deceived you until the command of God came, and the Deceiver deceived you about God. So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is your protector, and wretched is the destination. It was mentioned in the hadith, Whoever hears, God hears him, and whoever sees, God sees him. And in another hadith, Indeed, God orders the servant to Paradise in what appears to people and directs him to the Fire." We seek refuge with God from that. And His saying: And when they stand up for prayer, they stand with laziness the verse, this is a description of the hypocrites in the most noble, best and best of deeds, which is prayer. When they stand up for it, they stand with laziness about it, because they have no intention in it, no faith in it, no fear, and they do not understand its meaning as Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Zahr on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Imran on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: It is disliked for a man to stand up for prayer while he is lazy, but he stands up for it with a cheerful face, great desire and intense joy, because he is communing with God and God is facing him, forgiving him and answering him when he calls upon Him, then he recites this verse: And when they stand up for prayer, they stand with laziness and it was narrated from another source on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar, so the saying of God Almighty: And when they stand up for prayer, they stand with laziness this is a description of their outward appearance as He said: And they do not come to prayer except with laziness then God Almighty mentioned the description of their corrupt inward appearance, so He said: They show off to people meaning they have no sincerity and no dealings with God, rather they only bear witness People are cautious and polite, and for this reason they often miss prayers that they do not see, such as the Isha prayer in the dark, and the Fajr prayer in the early morning, as it was proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The most burdensome prayers for the hypocrites are the Isha prayer and the Fajr prayer. If they knew what was in them, they would come to them even if they had to crawl. I was thinking of ordering the prayer to be called, then ordering a man to lead the people in prayer, then setting out with men carrying bundles of firewood to people who do not attend the prayer and burning their houses with fire.” In another narration: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a fat vein or two beautiful spears, he would attend the prayer. Were it not for the women and children in the houses, I would have burned their houses with them.” Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, Muhammad ibn Dinar told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays well when people can see him and prays badly when he is alone, that is an act of disdain with which he disdains his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. And His statement, and they remember God only a little means that in their prayer they do not have humility and do not know what they are saying, rather they are heedless and distracted in their prayer, and they turn away from what is intended for them of good. Imam Malik narrated on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “That is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite. He sits watching the sun until it is between the horns of Satan, then he stands and performs four rak’ahs in which he remembers God only a little.” Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Ismail ibn Ja’far al-Madani on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn Abd al-Rahman, and al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. And His statement: Wavering between that, neither with these nor with those means the hypocrites are confused between faith and disbelief, so they are neither with the believers outwardly nor inwardly, nor with the disbelievers outwardly and inwardly. Rather, their outward appearance is with the believers and their inward appearance is with the disbelievers. Some of them are overcome by doubt, so sometimes they lean towards these and sometimes towards those. Whenever it is illuminated for them, they walk therein, and when darkness falls upon them, they stand still verse. And Mujahid said: Wavering between that, neither with these meaning the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor with those meaning the Jews. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Ubaydullah told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The example of the hypocrite is that of a stray sheep between two flocks, it goes to this one once and to that one another time, and it does not know which of them to follow. Muslim alone transmitted it, and he transmitted it on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna another time, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab, stopping at Ibn Umar and not attributing it to the Prophet. He said: Abd al-Wahhab transmitted it to us twice, that is what I said. Imam Ahmad transmitted it on the authority of Ishaq ibn Yusuf on the authority of Ubaydullah, and Ismail ibn Ayyash and Ali ibn Asim transmitted it on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shaybah transmitted it on the authority of Abdah, on the authority of Abd God, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Hammad ibn Salamah transmitted it on the authority of Ubaydullah or Abd God ibn Umar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. It was also narrated by Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, al-Hudhayl ibn Bilal narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ubayd that he was sitting one day in Mecca and Abdullah ibn Umar was with him, and my father said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The likeness of the hypocrite on the Day of Resurrection is that of a sheep between two flocks of sheep. If it comes to these, it will butt it, and if it comes to those, it will butt it.” Ibn Umar said to him: You have lied. The people praised my father for something good or well, and Ibn Umar said: I do not think your companion is anything other than what you say, but I bear witness to God when He said: Like a sheep between two flocks of sheep, and He said: He is the same. He said: This is how I heard it. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Al-Masoudi told us on the authority of Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali, who said: While `Ubayd ibn `Umair was telling stories and `Abdullah ibn `Umar was with him, `Ubayd ibn `Umair said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The example of the hypocrite is that of a sheep between two pastures. When it comes to these, it butts it, and when it comes to those, it butts it.” Ibn `Umair said: “That is not the case. Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Like a sheep between two flocks.’” He said: The old man was cautious and became angry, and when Ibn `Umar saw that, he said: If I had not heard him, I would not have repeated that to you. Another way from Ibn Umar - Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us from Uthman ibn Budawayh, from Ya`far ibn Zudhi, he said: I heard Ubayd ibn Umair while he was narrating, saying: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of the hypocrite is like that of a sheep crouching between two sheep. Ibn Umar said: Woe to you, do not lie about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only said: The example of the hypocrite is like that of a stray sheep between two sheep. Ahmad also narrated it through various chains of transmission from Ubayd ibn Umair, from Ibn Umar, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it: My father told us, Ubaydullah ibn Musa told us, Isra’il told us from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas`ud, he said: The example of the believer, the hypocrite, and the disbeliever is like three men who came to a valley, one of them fell and crossed, then the other fell until he reached the middle of the valley, and the one on the edge of the valley called out to him: Woe to you, where are you going to perish? Return your stick. Upon your beginning, the one who crossed called out to him: Come to salvation, so he looked at this one time and that one time, he said: Then a flood came and drowned him, so the one who crossed was the believer, and the one who drowned was the hypocrite wavering between that, neither with these nor with those, and the one who remained was the disbeliever. Ibn Jarir said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Qatada, wavering between that, neither with these nor with those, meaning: they are not sincere believers, nor openly polytheists. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give an example for the believer, the hypocrite, and the disbeliever, like a group of three who were pushed into a river. The believer fell and was cut off, then the hypocrite fell until he was about to reach the believer. The disbeliever called out to him, Come to me, for I fear for you, and the believer called out to him, Come to me, for with me you have what is with you. The hypocrite continued to waver between them until he came upon something harmful and drowned him. The hypocrite continued to be in doubt and suspicion until death came upon him while he was in that state. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “The example of the hypocrite is like that of a sheep bleating between two sheep. She saw sheep on a high slope, so she came to them and smelled them, but she did not recognize them. Then she saw sheep on a high slope, so she came to them and smelled them, but she did not recognize them. You know, and for this reason the Almighty said: “And he whom God sends astray - you will not find for him a way,” meaning, and he whom He turns away from the path of guidance, you will not find for him a protector to guide, nor a rescuer for them from what they are in, for the Almighty has no one to question His judgment, nor is He questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned.

4:144: God the Almighty forbids His believing servants from taking the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, meaning befriending them, advising them, secretly loving them, and disclosing the inner states of the believers to them, as God the Almighty said: "Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with God, unless you fear them out of fear. And God warns you of Himself." That is, He warns you of His punishment for committing what He has forbidden. That is why He said here: Do you want to make for God a clear authority over you? That is, an argument against you in His punishment of you. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Malik bin Ismail told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: a clear authority, he said: Every authority in the Qur'an is an argument. This is a sound chain of transmission, and this is also what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Muhammad bin Ka'b al-Qurazi, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and al-Nadr bin Arabi said. Then God the Almighty informed us, Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, as a reward for their severe disbelief. Al-Walibi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, In the lowest depths of the Fire, meaning at the bottom of the Fire. Another said: Hell has levels just as Paradise has degrees. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Dhakwan Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, he said, in coffins that shake over them: this is how Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Wakee’, on the authority of Yahya ibn Yaman, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain of transmission. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Musa, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, he said: The lowest depths are houses with doors that close over them, and fires are lit from below and above them. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Khaithama, on the authority of Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas`ud, Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. He said: In coffins of fire that will be closed over them, meaning locked and sealed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Ashja, on the authority of Wakee`, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Khaithama, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. He said: In coffins of iron that will be sealed over them. The meaning of his saying: locked, sealed, and one cannot find the place to open them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, my father told us, Abu Salamah told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ali bin Yazid told us on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman that Ibn Masoud was asked about the hypocrites, and he said: They will be placed in coffins of fire that will close over them in the lowest level of Hell. And you will not find for them a helper, meaning someone who will save them from what they are in and bring them out of the painful torment. Then the Almighty informed us that whoever repents among them in this world, He will accept his repentance and accept his regret if he is sincere in his repentance and corrects his actions, and holds fast to his Lord in all his affairs. And if he is patient, then it is better for him. Abu Dawud said: Abdullah bin Muadh told us, my father told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Aisha, she said: Something of hers was stolen, so she began to supplicate against him, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not supplicate against him. And Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He should not supplicate against him, but rather say: O God, help me against him, and extract my right from him. And in a narration on his authority, he said: He has permitted him to supplicate against the one who wronged him without transgressing against him. Abdul Karim bin Malik Al-Jazari said about this verse: It is the man who curses you, so you curse him, but if he slanders you, do not slander him, because God says: And whoever retaliates after being wronged - against them there is no blame. Abu Dawud said: Al-Qa’nabi told us, Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The two who slander each other, whatever they say, is at fault, as long as the wronged one does not retaliate. Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Muthanna bin Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged, he said: A man hosted a man but did not fulfill his right to hospitality, so when he left he told the people and said: I hosted so-and-so but he did not fulfill my right to hospitality. He said: So that is the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged until the other fulfills his right to hospitality. Ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. He said: He said: It is the man who visits a man and he does not treat him well as a guest, so he leaves and says: He treated me badly and did not treat him well. In another narration: It is the guest who has been transferred from his place of residence, so he speaks ill of his companion. This is also narrated on the authority of more than one person on the authority of Mujahid, and the group, except for al-Nasa’i and al-Tirmidhi, narrated on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa’d, and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, both of them on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib on the authority of Abu al-Khayr Marthad ibn Abdullah on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: We said: O Messenger of God, you send us and we stay with a people and they do not welcome us, so what do you think about that? He said: “If you stay with a people and they command you what is appropriate for a guest, then accept it from them, and if you do not do so, then take from them the right of a guest that is appropriate for them.” Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Abu al-Judi narrating on the authority of Sa`id ibn Muhajir, on the authority of al-Miqdam ibn Abi Karimah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If a Muslim hosts people and the guest wakes up deprived, then it is the duty of every Muslim to support him until he takes what he needs for the night from his crops and wealth. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this chain of narration. Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Shu`bah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Sha`bi, on the authority of al-Miqdam ibn Abi Karimah, who heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The guest’s night is obligatory upon every Muslim, and if he wakes up deprived in his courtyard, then it is a debt owed to him, so if he wishes, he may collect it, and if he wishes, he may leave it. Then he also narrated it on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu`bah. And on the authority of Ziyad ibn `Abdullah al-Bakka`i, on the authority of Wakee` and Abu Nu`aym, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, all three of them on the authority of Mansur, on his authority. Abu Dawud also narrated it from the hadith of Abu `Awanah, on the authority of Mansur, on his authority. From these hadiths and their likes, Ahmad and others went to the obligation of hospitality. From this type is the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar: Amr bin Ali told us, Safwan bin Isa told us, Muhammad bin Ajlan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I have a neighbor who annoys me. So he said to him: Take out your belongings and put them on the road. So the man took his belongings and threw them on the road, and everyone who passed by him said: What is the matter with you? He said: My neighbor is harming me, so he says: O God, curse him, O God, disgrace him. He said: The man said: Go back to your home, by God I will never harm you again. Abu Dawud narrated it in the Book of Etiquette on the authority of Abu Tawbah al-Rabi’ ibn Nafi’, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Hayyan Abu Khalid al-Ahmar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, on his authority. Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know that he narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurayrah except with this chain of transmission. Abu Juhayfah Wahb ibn Abdullah narrated it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Yusuf ibn Abdullah ibn Salam on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His saying: Whether you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an evil, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Competent. That is, whether you, O people, disclose good or conceal it or pardon those who have wronged you, then that is something that will bring you closer to God and will increase your reward with Him, for it is among His attributes that He pardons His servants even though He is able to punish them. For this reason, He said: For indeed, God is Forgiving and Competent. For this reason, it was reported in the hadith that the bearers of the Throne glorify God, and some of them say: Glory be to You for Your forbearance after Your knowledge, and some of them say: Glory be to You for Your pardon after Your power. And in the authentic hadith: No wealth is decreased by charity, and God does not increase a servant through pardon except in honor, and whoever humbles himself before God, He will raise him up.

4:150: God the Most High threatens those who disbelieve in Him and His Messengers, from the Jews and Christians, because they differentiated between God and His Messengers in faith, so they believed in some of the Prophets and disbelieved in others merely out of desire and habit, and what they had accustomed their fathers to, not because of evidence that led them to that, for there is no way for them to do that, but rather merely out of desire and fanaticism. The Jews - may God’s curses be upon them - believed in the Prophets except Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon them, and the Christians believed in the Prophets and disbelieved in their Seal and most honorable of them, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Samaritans do not believe in a Prophet after Joshua, the successor of Moses, son of Imran, and the Magians are said to have believed in a Prophet of theirs called Zoroaster, then they disbelieved in his law, so he was removed from among them, and God knows best. The point is that whoever disbelieves in a Prophet has disbelieved in all the Prophets, for faith is obligatory in every Prophet sent by God to the people of the earth. So whoever rejects his prophethood out of envy, fanaticism, or desire, it becomes clear that His belief in the prophets he believed in is not a legitimate belief, but rather it is based on purpose, desire and fanaticism. That is why God Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieve in God and His messengers, so He described them as disbelievers in God and His messengers, and they want to differentiate between God and His messengers, that is, in faith, and say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others,’ and they want to adopt a way in between, that is, a path and a course. Then God Almighty informed about them and said: Those are the disbelievers in truth, that is, their disbelief is certainly certain in the one they claimed to believe in, because it is not legitimate. If they had believed in him because he was the Messenger of God, they would have believed in his counterpart and in someone whose proof is clearer and whose evidence is stronger than his, or they would have looked at his prophethood with the right consideration. And His statement: And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment means just as they belittled those who disbelieved in Him, either because they did not consider what he brought to them from God and turned away from it and focused on collecting the debris of this world that they did not need, or because they disbelieved in him after knowing about his prophethood, as many of the Jewish rabbis did in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they envied him for the great prophethood that God had given him and they opposed him and denied him and opposed him and fought him, so God inflicted upon them worldly humiliation connected to the humiliation of the Hereafter and humiliation and wretchedness were imposed upon them, and they incurred the wrath of God in this world and the Hereafter. And His statement: And those who believe in God and His messengers and make no distinction between any of them means by that the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for they believe in every book that God revealed and every prophet that God sent, as God Almighty said: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God” 1:13. Then God Almighty informed us that He has prepared for them a great reward, a magnificent recompense, and a beautiful gift, and He said: Those - He will give them their reward for what they believed in God and His messengers, and God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning for their sins, meaning if some of them had sins.

4:153: Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi, Al-Suddi and Qatadah said: The Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to send down to them a book from the heavens, just as the Torah was sent down to Moses in writing. Ibn Jurayj said: They asked him to send down to them written pages from God to so-and-so and so-and-so, confirming what he brought to them. They said this out of stubbornness, obstinacy, disbelief and atheism, just as the infidels of Quraysh before them asked something similar, as mentioned in Surat Al-Subhan: And they said, ‘We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth’ (Surat Al-Baqarah 2:17). For this reason, God the Almighty said: “They asked Moses even greater than that. They said, ‘Show us God openly.’ So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing,” meaning for their tyranny, transgression, insolence and obstinacy. This is explained in Surat Al-Baqarah, where God the Almighty says: “And when you said, ‘O Moses, we will not believe in you until we see God openly.’ So the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on. Then We resurrected you after your death.” Perhaps you will be grateful. And the Almighty said: Then they took the calf after the clear proofs had come to them meaning after they saw the dazzling signs and compelling evidence at the hands of Moses, peace be upon him, in the land of Egypt, and the destruction of their enemy Pharaoh and all his soldiers in the sea. They had only passed it a little, until they came upon a people who were devoted to their idols, so they said to Moses, Make for us a god as they have gods verses 2. Then the Almighty mentioned the story of their taking the calf in detail in Surat Al-A’raf and in Surat Taha, after Moses went to commune with God Almighty, then when he returned and what happened happened, God made their repentance for what they had done and innovated, that whoever among them did not worship the calf should be killed from among those who worshipped it, so they began to kill each other, then God Almighty revived them, and God Almighty said: So We pardoned that and gave Moses a clear authority verse 2. Then He said: And We raised above them the Mount with their covenant verse 2. That was when they refused to adhere to the rulings of the Torah, and they showed their refusal to what had come to them. By Moses, peace be upon him, and God raised a mountain over their heads, then they adhered and prostrated, and they began to look above their heads, fearing that it would fall on them, as God Almighty said: And when We lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought that it would fall on them, [saying], ‘Take what We have given you with strength,’ (al-Baqarah 2:17), And We said to them, ‘Enter the gate in prostration,’ meaning they disobeyed what they were commanded to say and do, for they were commanded to enter the gate of the Holy House in prostration while saying, Repentance, meaning, O God, forgive us our sins for abandoning jihad and refraining from it, until we wandered in the wilderness for forty years, so they entered crawling on their buttocks while saying, Wheat in a hair. “And We said to them, ‘Do not transgress on the Sabbath,’” meaning, We commanded them to observe the Sabbath and adhere to what God has forbidden them, as long as it is permissible for them. And We took from them a firm covenant, meaning, a strong one, so they disobeyed and rebelled and plotted to commit what God Almighty has forbidden, as is explained in detail in Surat Al-A’raf at His saying: And ask them about the town that was by the sea and the verses, and the hadith of Safwan bin Assal will come in Surat Al-Subhan when he says: And We gave Moses nine clear signs and in it: And upon you in particular the Jews is not to transgress on the Sabbath.

4:155: This is one of the sins they committed, which necessitated their being cursed, expelled, and distanced from guidance. It is their breaking of the covenants and agreements that were taken from them, and their disbelief in the signs of God, that is, His proofs and evidence, and the miracles that they witnessed at the hands of the prophets, peace be upon them. His statement: And their killing of the prophets without right is due to the abundance of their crimes and their audacity towards the prophets of God, as they killed a large group of prophets, peace be upon them. And their saying: Our hearts are covered. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, Qatadah, and others said: meaning in a cover. This is like the saying of the polytheists: And they said, ‘Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us.’ (Al-Baqarah 2:100), and it was said that its meaning is that they claimed that their hearts were covered for knowledge, meaning that they were vessels for knowledge that contained and acquired it. Al-Kalbi narrated it on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. A similar statement was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. God Almighty said: Rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief. According to the first statement, it is as if they are apologizing to Him by saying that their hearts do not comprehend what He is saying, because they are covered and concealed. God said: Rather, they are sealed upon them because of their disbelief. According to the second statement, what they claimed was reversed from them in every way. We have already discussed something similar to this in Surat al-Baqarah 2:So they do not believe except a little, meaning their hearts were trained in disbelief, tyranny, and little faith. And because of their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning that they accused her of adultery. And likewise. Al-Suddi, Juwaybir, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others said: It is apparent from the verse that they accused her and her son of great sins, making her an adulteress and she became pregnant with her child from that. Some of them added: And she was menstruating, so upon them are the curses of God that continue until the Day of Resurrection. And their saying: We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of God means this one who claims this position for himself, we have killed him. This from them is from the perspective of mockery and ridicule, like the saying of the polytheists: O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad. And it was from the report of the Jews, upon them be the curses of God, His wrath, anger and punishment, that when God sent Jesus, son of Mary, with clear proofs and guidance, they envied him for what God the Most High had given him of prophethood and the dazzling miracles with which he would heal the blind and the lepers and bring the dead back to life by God’s permission, and he would fashion a bird from clay, then breathe into it, and it would become a bird whose flight could be seen by God the Almighty’s permission, in addition to other miracles with which God honored him and performed through his hands. Despite this, They denied him, opposed him, and sought to harm him with all they could, until the Prophet of God, Jesus, peace be upon him, did not live with them in one town, but rather he and his mother, peace be upon them, would frequently travel. But that did not convince them, so they sought the king of Damascus at that time, who was a polytheist who worshipped the stars, and his people were called the Greeks. They informed him that in Jerusalem there was a man who tempted and led people astray, and corrupted the king’s subjects. The king became angry at this and wrote to his deputy in Jerusalem to take precautions against the aforementioned man, to crucify him and put thorns on his head, and to stop his harm to the people. When the letter arrived, the governor of Jerusalem complied with that, and he and a group of Jews went to the house where Jesus, peace be upon him, was, and he was with a group of his companions, twelve or thirteen, and it was said seventeen people. That was on Friday after the afternoon on Saturday night, so they besieged him there. When he sensed them and that they would inevitably enter upon him or he would go out to them, he said to his companions: Which of you will cast my likeness upon him while he is my companion in Paradise? A young man from among them was appointed for this, but he seemed to think he was too young for this, so he repeated it a second and a third time, and all of that no one was appointed except that young man, so he said: You are he, and God cast upon him the likeness of Jesus until it was as if he were him, and a window was opened from the ceiling of the house, and Jesus, peace be upon him, fell asleep a year, and he was raised to heaven while he was like that, as God Almighty said: When God said, O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Me verse, so when he was raised, those people came out, and when they saw that young man, they thought he was Jesus, so they took him at night and crucified him, and put thorns on his head, and the Jews showed that they sought to crucify him, and they boasted about that and groups of Christians surrendered to them, that was due to their ignorance and lack of intelligence, except for those who were in the house with Christ, for they witnessed his being raised. As for the rest, they thought, as the Jews thought, that the one crucified was the Messiah, son of Mary, until they mentioned that Mary sat under that crucified one and cried, and it is said that he spoke to her, and God knows best, and all of this is from God’s testing of His servants, because of the great wisdom He has in that. God has made the matter clear, evident and evident, and made it manifest in the Great Qur’an, which He revealed to His noble Messenger, supported by miracles, clear proofs and evidence. The Most High said: And He is the most truthful of speakers and the Lord of the worlds, the Knower of secrets and consciences, the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth, the Knower of what was and what will be and what would not have been if it had been, how it would have been. And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear to them meaning they saw his resemblance and thought it was him. That is why He said: “And indeed, those who differ therein are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption” meaning by that those Jews who claimed that he killed him, and those ignorant Christians who handed him over to them, all of them in doubt about that and confusion and misguidance and madness. That is why He said: And they did not kill him for certain meaning they did not kill him, certain that it was him, but rather they doubted and imagined it. “Rather, God raised him up to Himself. And God is Exalted in Might” meaning His side is inviolable, and no one who seeks refuge at His door is wronged, Wise meaning in all that He decrees and decides of the matters that He created it, and He has the perfect wisdom, the conclusive argument, the great authority, and the ancient command. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God wanted to raise Jesus to heaven, he came out to his companions, and in the house were twelve men from the disciples, meaning he came out to them from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping with water, and he said: Among you is he who will disbelieve in me twelve times, after having believed in me. He said: Then he said: Which of you will be cast upon my likeness so that he will be killed in my place and be with me in my degree? Then a young man from the youngest of them stood up and said to him: Sit down. Then he repeated it to them. The young man stood up and said: Sit down. Then he repeated it to them. The young man stood up and said: I am. Then he said: It is you. Then the likeness of Jesus was cast upon him, and Jesus was raised from a window in the house to heaven. He said: The request came from the Jews, so they took the likeness and killed him and then crucified him. Some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after they had believed in him, and they split into three groups. One group said: God was with us as He willed, then He ascended to heaven.
