This is not good, since his belief does not necessarily mean that he becomes a Muslim. Do you not see the statement of Ibn Abbas: Even if he were to fall from a high place or be struck with a sword or be devoured by a wild beast, he would necessarily believe in Jesus? Faith in this case is not beneficial and does not remove its owner from his disbelief, for what we have presented. And God knows best. Whoever ponders carefully and looks closely, it will become clear to him that this is the reality, but this does not necessarily mean that this is what was meant by this verse. Rather, what was meant by it is what we mentioned of confirming the existence of Jesus, peace be upon him, and the continuation of his life in heaven, and that he will descend to earth before the Day of Resurrection to refute these and those from the Jews and Christians whose statements about him differed and clashed. And they were contradictory and opposite and devoid of the truth, so these Jews went too far, and these Christians went too far in belittling the Jews with what they accused him and his mother of of the great things, and the Christians praised him to the point that they claimed in him what he did not have, so they raised him in contrast to those from the position of prophethood to the position of divinity, exalted be He above what these and those say, greatly exalted, and He is transcendent and sanctified, there is no god but Him. Mentioning the hadiths that were reported about the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, to Earth from heaven at the end of time Before the Day of Resurrection, and that he calls for the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said in the Book of Mentioning the Prophets in his Sahih, which is accepted: The descent of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa`id bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the son of Mary will soon descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and wealth will overflow to the point that no one will accept it, and prostration will be better for them than the world and what is in it.” Then Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: “And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.” Muslim narrated it likewise on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Halwani and Abd bin Hamid, both on the authority of Yaqub, on his authority. Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Al-Zuhri on his authority. And they narrated it on the authority of Al-Layth on the authority of Al-Zuhri on his authority, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Hafsah on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The son of Mary will soon descend among you as a just judge. He will kill the Antichrist, kill the pig, break the cross, abolish the jizyah, and wealth will be abundant. Prostration will be for God, Lord of the worlds, but only one.” Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death, the death of Jesus, son of Mary. Then Abu Hurairah repeated it three times. Another way On the authority of Abu Hurairah, Imam Ahmad said: Ruh bin Abi Hafsah told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hanzala bin Ali Al-Aslami, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Jesus will enter the state of ihram at Faj Al-Rawha’ for Hajj or Umrah, or both of them together. Muslim narrated it in this way alone on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, and Yunus bin Yazid, all three of them on the authority of Al-Zuhri on this authority. Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Sufyan Ibn Husayn told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Jesus, son of Mary, will descend and kill the pig, and the cross will be erased, and prayers will be collected for him, and money will be given until it is no longer accepted, and the tax will be abolished, and he will descend to Ar-Rawha’ and perform Hajj or Umrah from there, or combine them.” He said: Abu Hurayrah recited: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death, the verse, so Hanzala claimed that Abu Hurayrah said: He will believe in him before the death of Jesus, so I do not know whether all of this is a hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or something that Abu Hurayrah said, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Musa Muhammad Ibn Al-Muthanna, on the authority of Yazid Ibn Harun, on the authority of Sufyan Ibn Husayn, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on his authority. Another chain of transmission Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Nafi’, the freed slave of Abu Qatada Al-Ansari, that Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will you be when the Messiah, son of Mary, descends among you and your Imam is from among you? Aqeel and Al-Awza’i followed him, and Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Uthman ibn Umar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, both of them on the authority of Al-Zuhri with it. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Yunus, Al-Awza’i, and Ibn Dhi’b with it. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The prophets are brothers by bloodline, their mothers are different, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him: a square-built man, reddish and white, wearing two Egyptian garments, as if his head were dripping even if no wetness had touched him. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and call people to Islam. God will destroy all religions in his time except Islam, and God will destroy the Antichrist in his time. Then security will prevail on the earth until lions will graze with camels, leopards with cows, and wolves with sheep, and children will play with snakes that will not harm them. He will remain for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him.” Abu Dawud narrated it likewise on the authority of Hadiya ibn Khalid, on the authority of Hammam ibn Yahya. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and no one else mentioned this verse except him, on the authority of Bishr bin Muadh, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, both of them on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Adam, who is the client of Umm Barthan, the owner of the water-carrier, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, and he said: People will fight for the sake of Islam. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu al-Yaman, on the authority of Shu’ayb, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, and the prophets are paternal brothers, there is no prophet between me and him. Then Muhammad bin Sinan narrated it on the authority of Falih bin Sulayman, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, in this world and the hereafter. The prophets are paternal brothers, their mothers are different, but their religion is one.” Ibrahim bin Tahman said, on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah, on the authority of Safwan bin Salim, on the authority of Ata bin Bashar, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Another hadith Muslim said in his Sahih: Zuhair bin Harb told me, Ya`la bin Mansur told us, Sulayman bin Bilal told us, Suhayl told us on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the Romans descend upon al-`Amaq or Dabiq, and an army from Medina will come out to them from the best people of the earth on that day. When they line up, the Romans will say: ‘Leave us alone with those who were taken captive from us so that we may fight them.’ The Muslims will say: ‘No, by God, we will not leave you alone with our brothers.’ So they will fight them, and a third will be defeated, and God will never forgive them. A third will be killed, and they are the best martyrs in the sight of God. A third will be conquered, and they will never be tempted. Then they will conquer Constantinople. While they are dividing the spoils, having hung their swords on olive trees, Satan will shout at them: ‘The Messiah has left you with your families.’ So they will go out, and that is false. When they reach al-Sham, he will come out. While they are preparing for battle, straightening the ranks, the prayer will be called, and Jesus, son of Mary, will descend.” He leads them in prayer, and when the enemy of God sees him, he melts away as salt melts in water. If he were to leave him alone, he would melt away until he perishes. But God kills him with His hand, and He shows them his blood on his spear. Another hadith Ahmad said: Hisham narrated to us on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab, on the authority of Jabalah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Muathir bin Ghafarah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “On the night of my ascension, I met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them, and they discussed the matter of the Hour. They referred their matter to Abraham, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Moses, and he said: I have no knowledge of it. They referred their matter to Jesus, and he said: As for its occurrence, no one knows about it except God. And what my Lord, the Almighty, the Majestic, has entrusted to me is that the Antichrist will come forth with two rods, and when he sees me he will melt like lead melts. He said: God will destroy him when he sees me, until even the rocks and trees will say: O Muslim, there is an unbeliever beneath me, so come and kill him. He said: God will destroy them, then the people will return to their lands and homelands. At that time, Gog and Magog will emerge, and they will swarm from every hill, and they will tread upon their lands, and they will not come upon anything except that they will destroy it, and they will not pass by water except that they will not…” They drank it. He said: Then the people will return complaining about them, so they will call upon God against them, so that He will destroy them and cause them to die until the earth is dry from the stench of their stench, and the rain will fall and sweep away their bodies until it throws them into the sea. So, in what my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, has entrusted to me, if that is the case, the Hour will be like a pregnant woman who has just given birth, and her people will not know when she will surprise them with her birth, at night or during the day.” Narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Yazid ibn Harun, on the authority of Al-Awam ibn Hawshab, with a similar wording. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, who said: We came to Uthman bin Abi Al-Aas on a Friday to show him our copy of the Qur’an on his copy of the Qur’an. When the Friday prayer came, he ordered us to wash ourselves, then we were brought perfume and perfumed ourselves, then we came to the mosque and sat with a man who told us about the Antichrist. Then Uthman bin Abi Al-Aas came, so we stood up to him and sat, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Muslims will have three cities: Egypt at the confluence of the two seas, Egypt at Al-Hirah, and Egypt in Ash-Sham. People will be frightened three times. The Antichrist will emerge among the people and will be defeated from the east. The first city he will return to will be the city at the confluence of the two seas. Its people will be divided into three groups: a group that will say, ‘We will set up a watchtower to see what will happen,’ a group that will join the Bedouins, and a group that will join the city next to them. With the Antichrist will be seventy thousand wearing armour, and most of those with him will be Jews and women, and the Muslims will withdraw.” To Aqaba Afiq, they send out their troops, but their troops are destroyed and this becomes difficult for them, and they are afflicted with severe famine and extreme hardship, so much so that one of them burns the string of his bow and eats it. While they are like this, a caller calls out at dawn: O people, relief has come to you three times. Some of them say to each other: This is the voice of a man who is full. And Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, descends at dawn prayer, and their leader says to him: O Spirit of God, advance and pray. He says: This nation is leaders, some of them over others. So their leader advances and prays, until when he has finished his prayer, Jesus takes his spear and goes towards the Antichrist. When the Antichrist sees him, he melts like lead melts. So he places his spear between his breasts and kills him, and his companions are defeated. On that day, there is nothing to cover any of them, until the tree says: O believer, this is an infidel, and the stone says: O believer, this is an infidel. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source. Another hadith Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah said in his Sunan: Ali bin Muhammad told us, Abdul Rahman Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Rafi’ Abi Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah Al-Shaibani Yahya bin Abi Amr, on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a sermon, and most of his sermon was a hadith. We told him about the Antichrist and warned him about it. Among his words was that he said: “There has been no trial on earth since God created the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, greater than the trial of the Antichrist. God did not send a prophet except that he warned his nation about the Antichrist. I am the last of the prophets and you are the last of the nations, and he will emerge among you inevitably. If he emerges while I am among you, then I am the pilgrim of every Muslim, and if he emerges after me, then each one of them will be his own pilgrim. God is my successor over every Muslim, and he will emerge from a gap between Syria and Iraq, and he will cause mischief to the right and to the left. O servants of God: O people, be steadfast, and I will describe him to you in a manner that no prophet before me has described him to: He will begin.” He says: I am a prophet, and there is no prophet after me. Then he repeats his words and says: I am your Lord, and you will not see your Lord until you die. He is one-eyed, and your Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, is not one-eyed. And written between his eyes is: Disbeliever, and every believer, literate and illiterate, will read it. And among his trials is that with him is Paradise and Hell. His Hell is Paradise and his Paradise is Hell. So whoever is afflicted with his Hell should seek help from God and recite the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf, and it will be cool and peaceful for him, just as Hell was cool and peaceful for Abraham. And among his trials is that he will say to the Bedouin: Tell me, if I resurrect your mother and your father, will you testify that I am your Lord? He says: Yes. Then two devils appear to him in the form of his father and mother and say: O my son, follow him, for he is your Lord. And among his trials is that he will give power over a single soul and saw it with a saw until it is split in two. Then he says: Look at this servant of Mine, for I will resurrect him now. Then he will claim that he has a Lord other than Me. So God resurrects him and the evil one says to him: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God, and you are the enemy of God, the Antichrist. By God, I have never been more aware of you than I am today. Abu al-Hasan al-Tanafisi said: Al-Maharibi told us, Ubayd God ibn al-Walid al-Wassafi told us on the authority of Atiyyah on the authority of Abu Sa`id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That man will have the highest rank of my nation in Paradise. Abu Sa`id said: By God, we did not see that man as anyone but Umar ibn al-Khattab, until he passed away. Then Al-Maharibi said: We returned to the hadith of Abu Rafi’ who said: Among his trials is that he will command the sky to rain and it rains, then he will command the earth to grow and it will grow. Among his trials is that he will pass by a tribe and they will deny him, so no grazing animal will remain except that it will perish. Among his trials is that he will pass by a tribe and they will believe him, then he will command the sky to rain and it will rain, and he will command the earth to grow and it will grow until their livestock return that day fatter than ever, with the largest and longest flanks and the most fertile udders, and nothing on earth will remain except that he will tread upon it and prevail over it, except Mecca and Medina, for he will not come to them from one of their passages except that the angels will meet him with drawn swords until he descends at the red mountain at the end of the salt marsh, then Medina will shake with its people three times, and no hypocrite, male or female, will remain except that he will go out to him, and the filth will be banished from it as the bellows banish the filth of iron, and that day will be called the Day of Deliverance. Umm Sharik bint Abi Al-Akr said: O Messenger of God, where will the Arabs be on that day? He said: “They will be few and most of them will be in Jerusalem on that day, and their imam will be a righteous man. While their imam has advanced to lead them in the dawn prayer, Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, will descend. That imam will walk backwards for Jesus, peace be upon him, to advance. Jesus will place his hand between his shoulders and say: ‘Advance and pray, for it has been established for you.’ So their imam will lead them in prayer. When he has finished, Jesus will say: ‘Open the door.’ So it will be opened, and behind him will be the Antichrist with seventy thousand Jews, all of them with a decorated sword and a shield. When the Antichrist looks at him, he will melt as salt melts in water and will run away. Jesus will say: ‘I have a blow against you that you have never dealt to me before.’ He will catch up with him at the eastern gate of Ludd and kill him. God will defeat the Jews, and nothing that God Almighty has created will remain in which a Jew could hide, except that God will make that thing speak, neither stone, nor tree, nor wall, nor animal - except the gharqadah, for it is one of their trees that does not speak - except that it will say: ‘O Muslim servant of God, this is a Jew, so come and kill him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘His days will be forty years, and the year is like half a twig.’” The year, and the year is like the month, and the month is like a Friday, and its last days are like a spark. One of you will be at the gate of the city and will not reach its other gate until the evening.” It was said to him: How do we pray, O Prophet of God, during those short days? He said: You can estimate the prayer as you estimate it during these long days, then pray. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then Jesus, son of Mary, will be in my nation a just judge and a fair leader. He will break the cross and slaughter the pig, and abolish the jizya, and abandon the charity. He will not seek to harm a sheep or a camel. Hatred and animosity will be lifted and the venom of every venomous creature will be removed until a newborn puts his hand into a snake and it will not harm him, and a newborn lion will flee and it will not lead her astray. The wolf will be among the sheep as if it were its dog. The earth will be filled with peace as it fills water, and the word will be one and none will be worshipped except God. War will lay down its burdens and the Quraysh will be stripped of their kingdom, and the earth will have the light of silver and its plants will grow as they did during the time of Adam until a group of people will gather to pick grapes and satisfy them, and a group of people will gather around a pomegranate and it will satisfy them.” The bull will be worth so-and-so in money, and the horse will be worth dirhams.” It was said: O Messenger of God, what makes a horse cheap? He said: It will never be ridden for war. It was said to him: What makes a bull expensive? He said: “It will plough the entire earth, and before the emergence of the Antichrist there will be three difficult years in which people will be afflicted with severe famine. God will command the sky in the first year to withhold a third of its rain, and command the earth to withhold a third of its vegetation. Then God will command the sky in the second year to withhold two-thirds of its rain, and command the earth to withhold two-thirds of its vegetation. Then God the Almighty will command the sky in the third year to withhold all of its rain, so that not a single drop will fall, and command the earth to withhold all of its vegetation, so that no hoofed animal will remain except that it will perish, except what God wills.” It was said: How will people live at that time? He said: Tahlil, Takbir, Tasbih, and Tahmid, and this will be done to them like food. Ibn Majah said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Tanafisi say: I heard Abd al-Rahman al-Maharibi say: This hadith should be given to the teacher so that he can teach it to the children in school. This hadith is very strange from this aspect, and some of it has supporting evidence from other hadiths, including what was narrated by Muslim, and the hadith of Nafi’ and Salim on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You will fight the Jews and kill them until a stone says: O Muslim, this is a Jew, so come and kill him.” And he has it on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the Muslims fight the Jews and the Muslims kill them until a Jew hides behind a stone or a tree, and the stone or tree says: O Muslim, O servant of God, there is a Jew behind me, so come and kill him - except for the gharqad, for it is one of the trees of the Jews.” Let us mention the hadith of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an here because of its similarity to this hadith. Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Abu Khaithamah Zuhair bin Harb told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber told us, Yahya bin Jaber Al-Ta’i, the judge of Homs told me, Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair told me on the authority of his father Jubair bin Nufayr Al-Hadrami that he heard Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an Al-Kalabi H. Muhammad bin Mihran Al-Razi told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber told us on the authority of Yahya bin Jaber Al-Ta’i, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair, on the authority of his father Jubair bin Nufayr, on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the Antichrist one morning, and he lowered and raised his voice until we thought he was in a group of palm trees. When we went to him, he could see that in our faces, so he said: What is the matter with you? We said: O Messenger of God, you mentioned the Antichrist one morning, so you lowered your voice and raised it until we thought he was among a group of palm trees. He said: "I fear nothing for you except the Antichrist. He will emerge while I am among you, then I will be his opponent on your behalf. But if he emerges while I am not among you, then every man will be his own opponent, and God will be my successor over every Muslim. He is a young, well-built man with a bulging eye. I liken him to Abd al-Uzza ibn Qatan. Whoever among you meets him, let him recite to him the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf. He will emerge from a gap between Syria and Iraq, and he will ravage right and left. O servants of God, be steadfast." We said: O Messenger of God, how long will he remain on earth? He said: "Forty days, one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days." We said: O Messenger of God, and how quickly will he travel on earth? He said: “Like rain that the wind has turned back, so he comes to a people and calls them and they believe in him and respond to him. He orders the sky to rain, and the earth to produce vegetation, and their livestock return to them with the tallest peaks, the most abundant udders, and the most abundant flanks. Then he comes to the people and calls them and they respond to him, so he turns away from them and they become destitute and have nothing of their wealth in their hands. He passes by a ruin and says to it: Bring forth your treasures, and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees. Then he calls a man full of youth and strikes him with the sword and cuts him into two pieces, like a target shot. Then he calls him and he accepts and his face lights up and he laughs. While he is like this, God sends the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and he descends at the white minaret east of Damascus between two wells, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, it drips, and when he raises it, pearls flow from it. It is not permissible for an unbeliever to find the scent of his breath except that he dies, and his breath ends where his gaze ends, so he seeks it.” Until he catches up with him at the gate of Ludd, and kills him, then Jesus, peace be upon him, will come to a people whom God has protected from him, and he will wipe their faces and tell them of their degrees in Paradise. While he is like that, God Almighty will inspire Jesus: I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one can fight, so protect My servants to the mountain. God will send Gog and Magog, and they will swarm from every side. The first of them will pass by the Sea of Galilee and drink what is in it, and the last of them will pass by and say: There was once water here. The Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will attend until the head of a bull for one of them is better than a hundred dinars for one of you today. The Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will desire it, and God will send upon them the filth in their necks, and they will become like the death of a single soul. Then the Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will descend to the earth, and they will not find a space on the earth a span but that it will be filled with their stench and stench. The Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will desire God, and God will send birds like the necks of camels, and they will carry them and throw them wherever He wills. God, then God sends rain from which no house of mud or hair can withstand, and it washes the earth until it leaves it like a slate. Then it is said to the earth: Bring forth your fruit and return your blessing. On that day, a group will eat from the pomegranate and seek shade under its shell, and God will bless the Messengers until even a single camel will suffice the groups. While they are like that, God sends a pleasant wind that takes them under their armpits, and God takes the soul of every believer and every Muslim, and the worst of people will remain, fighting each other like donkeys, and the Hour will come upon them.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the People of Sunnah from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir with it. We will also mention it from the path of Ahmad when God the Almighty says in Surat al-Anbiya’: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose (al-Anbiya’: 11). Another hadith Muslim also said in his Sahih: Ubayd God ibn Muadh al-Anbari told us, my father told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya’qub ibn Asim ibn Urwah ibn Mas’ud al-Thaqafi say: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr, and a man came to him and said: What is this hadith that you are talking about, saying that the Hour will come at such and such a time? He said: Glory be to God, or there is no god but God, or a word like them, I intended not to tell anyone anything ever, but I said: You will see in a little while a great matter: He will burn the House and it will happen and it will happen, then he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Antichrist will emerge among my nation and will remain for forty, I do not know whether it will be a day or forty months or forty years, then God, the Most High, will send Jesus, son of Mary, who looks like Urwah ibn Mas`ud, and he will seek him out and kill him, then the people will remain for seven years with no enmity between two people, then God will send a cold wind from the direction of Ash-Sham, and no one will remain on the face of the earth in whose heart there is an atom’s weight of goodness - or faith - except that it will seize him, so that if one of you were to enter the heart of a mountain, it would enter it until it seizes him.” He said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “The worst of people will remain as light as birds and as dreamy as wild beasts, they will not recognize good and will not denounce evil, then Satan will appear to them and say: Will you not respond? They will say: What do you command us to do?” He will command them to worship idols, and they will have their livelihood and good living. Then the trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he will listen attentively and raise his head. He said: The first one to hear it will be a man filling the water tank of his camels. He said: He will be struck dumb and the people will be struck dumb. Then God will send - or he said - God will send down rain like dew - or he said the shade - of Nu'man the doubter - and the bodies of the people will grow from it. Then it will be blown again and they will be standing and looking. Then it will be said: O people, come to your Lord. Stop them, for they will be questioned. Then it will be said: Bring out the people of Hell. It will be said: From how many? It will be said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. He said: That is a day when the children will turn gray, and that is a day when the shin will be uncovered. Then Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it in their interpretation together on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of Nu'man ibn Salim on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd God ibn Tha’labah al-Ansari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, on the authority of Mujammi ibn Jariyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The son of Mary will kill the Antichrist at the gate of Ludd - or next to Ludd. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah from the hadith of al-Layth and al-Awza’i, all three of them on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd God ibn Tha’labah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of his uncle Mujammi ibn Jariyah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The son of Mary will kill the Antichrist at the gate of Ludd. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth, and he said: This is a sound hadith. He said: There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, Nafi’ ibn Utbah, Abu Barzah, Hudhayfah ibn Asid, Abu Hurayrah, Kaysan, Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As, Jabir, Abu Umamah, Ibn Mas’ud, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Samurah. Ibn Jundub, Al-Nawwas Ibn Sam’an, Amr Ibn Awf, and Hudhayfah Ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with them. What he meant by the narration of these is what mentions the Antichrist and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, killing him. As for the hadiths that mention the Antichrist only, they are very many, and they are more than can be counted due to their prevalence and the frequency of their narration in the Sahihs, Hassans, Musnads, and other books. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Furat, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked down upon us from Arafat while we were discussing the Hour, and he said: “The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, and the Antichrist, and three landslides: one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden and drive - or gather - the people, spending the night with them wherever they spend the night, and resting with them wherever they rest.” And Muslim and the people of the Sunnah narrated it in this way from the hadith of Furat al-Qazzaz. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’ on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Abu Sarihah, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid al-Ghifari, with a chain of transmission ending with him, and God knows best. These are successive hadiths on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas’ud, Uthman bin Abi al-‘As, Abu Umamah, al-Nawwas bin Sam’an, Abdullah bin Amr bin al-‘As, Mujammi’ bin Jariyah, Abu Sarihah, and Hudhayfah bin Asid, may God be pleased with them. In them is evidence of the manner in which he will descend and his place, that he will be in the Levant, or rather in Damascus, near the eastern minaret, and that this will be when the dawn prayer is performed. In these times, in the year 741, a white minaret was built for the Umayyad Mosque from carved stones in place of the minaret that was destroyed due to the fire attributed to the actions of the Christians - upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection - and most of its construction was done with their money. It was strongly suspected that it was the one on which the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, would descend, and he would kill the pig, break the cross, and impose the jizya tax. It is not acceptable except for Islam, as mentioned in the two Sahihs. This is a statement from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and a confirmation, legislation, and justification for it in that time, when their ailments will be removed and their doubts will be removed from themselves. For this reason, they will all enter the religion of Islam, following Jesus, peace be upon him, and through his hands. For this reason, God Almighty said: There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death 1:13. This verse is like His statement: And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour 1:13. It was read 1:13 with a fat-ha, meaning a sign and evidence of the approach of the Hour, because he will descend after the emergence of the Antichrist, and God will kill him at his hands. As it is proven in the Sahih that God did not create a disease without sending down a cure for it, and God will send Gog and Magog in his days, and God Almighty will destroy them through the blessing of his supplication. God Almighty said: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they stream forth from every mound, * And the true promise draws near 1:13. (Description of Jesus, peace be upon him) It was mentioned in the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “So when you see him, recognize him: a square-built man with a reddish-white complexion, wearing two white garments, as if his head were dripping even if no wetness had befallen him.” And in the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an: “He will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus between two Mahroudahs, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, it drips, and when he raises it, something like pearls flows from it. It is not permissible for a disbeliever to smell the scent of his own breath except that he dies, and his breath ends where his glance ends.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the night of my ascension, I met Moses. He said: So I described him, and I thought he was a man. He said: A man with a swaying head, as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah. He said: And I met Jesus. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him and said: Squat, red, as if he had emerged from Dimas, meaning the bathhouse. And I saw Abraham, and I resembled his son to him. Hadith, and Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Mujahid from Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw Moses, Jesus and Abraham. As for Jesus, he was red, curly-haired and broad-chested. As for Moses, he was dark-skinned, large and straight-chested, as if he were from the Zutt men.” And he and Muslim narrated from Musa bin Uqbah from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the Antichrist one day among the people, and said: “God is not one-eyed. Beware, the Antichrist is blind in his right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape.” And Muslim narrated from him, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “And God showed me at the Kaaba in a dream, and there was a dark man, the most handsome of men you have ever seen, his locks falling between his shoulders, his hair falling, his head dripping with water, and he was placing his hands on the shoulders of two men while he was circumambulating the House. So I said: Who is this?” They said: He is the Messiah, son of Mary. Then I saw behind him a man with curly hair, blind in his right eye, who most closely resembled Ibn Qatan among those I have seen, placing his hands on the shoulders of a man circumambulating the House. I said: Who is this? They said: The Antichrist. Narrated by Ubaydullah on the authority of Nafi’. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Makki, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Saad, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: No, by God, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say that Jesus was red, but he said: “While I was sleeping, I was circumambulating the Kaaba, and there was a red man with smooth hair, swaying between two men, with water dripping from his head - or his head was dripping with water - so I said: Who is this? They said: The son of Mary. So I went to turn around, and there was a red, big man, with curly hair, blind in his right eye, as if his eye was a floating grape. I said: Who is this? They said: The Antichrist, and the person who most closely resembles him is Ibn Qatan.” Al-Zuhri said: A man from Khuza’ah who died in the pre-Islamic era. All of these are the words of Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him. It was mentioned previously in the hadith of Abd Al-Rahman bin Adam on the authority of Abu Hurairah that Jesus, peace be upon him, will remain on earth for forty years after his descent, then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him. And in the hadith of Abdullah bin Umar in Muslim, it is said that he will remain for seven years, so it is possible - and God knows best - that what is meant is He stayed on earth for forty years, the total of his stay on it before he was raised and after he descended. He was raised when he was thirty-three years old, according to the Sahih. This was mentioned in a hadith describing the people of Paradise, that they are in the image of Adam, and the birth of Jesus was thirty-three years old. As for what Ibn Asakir narrated from some of them, that he was raised when he was one hundred and fifty years old, this is strange, strange and remote. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Jesus, son of Mary, in his history, from some of the predecessors, that he will be buried with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his room. And God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness over them. Qatada said: He will bear witness over them that he had conveyed the message from God to them and acknowledged the servitude of God Almighty. This is like the Almighty’s saying at the end of Surat al-Ma’idah 5:“And when God said, ‘O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, ‘Take me and my mother as gods besides God?’ He said, ‘Glory be to You! It is not for me to say that which I have no right to. If I had said it, You knew it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I said to them nothing but what You commanded me, ‘Worship God, my Lord and your Lord.’ And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them. But when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You should punish them, they are Your servants; but if You should forgive them, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
4:158: This is one of the sins they committed, which necessitated their being cursed, expelled, and distanced from guidance. It is their breaking of the covenants and agreements that were taken from them, and their disbelief in the signs of God, that is, His proofs and evidence, and the miracles that they witnessed at the hands of the prophets, peace be upon them. His statement: And their killing of the prophets without right is due to the abundance of their crimes and their audacity towards the prophets of God, as they killed a large group of prophets, peace be upon them. And their saying: Our hearts are covered. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, Qatadah, and others said: meaning in a cover. This is like the saying of the polytheists: And they said, ‘Our hearts are within coverings from that to which you invite us.’ (Al-Baqarah 2:100), and it was said that its meaning is that they claimed that their hearts were covered for knowledge, meaning that they were vessels for knowledge that contained and acquired it. Al-Kalbi narrated it on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. A similar statement was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. God Almighty said: Rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief. According to the first statement, it is as if they are apologizing to Him by saying that their hearts do not comprehend what He is saying, because they are covered and concealed. God said: Rather, they are sealed upon them because of their disbelief. According to the second statement, what they claimed was reversed from them in every way. We have already discussed something similar to this in Surat al-Baqarah 2:So they do not believe except a little, meaning their hearts were trained in disbelief, tyranny, and little faith. And because of their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning that they accused her of adultery. And likewise. Al-Suddi, Juwaybir, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others said: It is apparent from the verse that they accused her and her son of great sins, making her an adulteress and she became pregnant with her child from that. Some of them added: And she was menstruating, so upon them are the curses of God that continue until the Day of Resurrection. And their saying: We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of God means this one who claims this position for himself, we have killed him. This from them is from the perspective of mockery and ridicule, like the saying of the polytheists: O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad. And it was from the report of the Jews, upon them be the curses of God, His wrath, anger and punishment, that when God sent Jesus, son of Mary, with clear proofs and guidance, they envied him for what God the Most High had given him of prophethood and the dazzling miracles with which he would heal the blind and the lepers and bring the dead back to life by God’s permission, and he would fashion a bird from clay, then breathe into it, and it would become a bird whose flight could be seen by God the Almighty’s permission, in addition to other miracles with which God honored him and performed through his hands. Despite this, They denied him, opposed him, and sought to harm him with all they could, until the Prophet of God, Jesus, peace be upon him, did not live with them in one town, but rather he and his mother, peace be upon them, would frequently travel. But that did not convince them, so they sought the king of Damascus at that time, who was a polytheist who worshipped the stars, and his people were called the Greeks. They informed him that in Jerusalem there was a man who tempted and led people astray, and corrupted the king’s subjects. The king became angry at this and wrote to his deputy in Jerusalem to take precautions against the aforementioned man, to crucify him and put thorns on his head, and to stop his harm to the people. When the letter arrived, the governor of Jerusalem complied with that, and he and a group of Jews went to the house where Jesus, peace be upon him, was, and he was with a group of his companions, twelve or thirteen, and it was said seventeen people. That was on Friday after the afternoon on Saturday night, so they besieged him there. When he sensed them and that they would inevitably enter upon him or he would go out to them, he said to his companions: Which of you will cast my likeness upon him while he is my companion in Paradise? A young man from among them was appointed for this, but he seemed to think he was too young for this, so he repeated it a second and a third time, and all of that no one was appointed except that young man, so he said: You are he, and God cast upon him the likeness of Jesus until it was as if he were him, and a window was opened from the ceiling of the house, and Jesus, peace be upon him, fell asleep a year, and he was raised to heaven while he was like that, as God Almighty said: When God said, O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Me verse, so when he was raised, those people came out, and when they saw that young man, they thought he was Jesus, so they took him at night and crucified him, and put thorns on his head, and the Jews showed that they sought to crucify him, and they boasted about that and groups of Christians surrendered to them, that was due to their ignorance and lack of intelligence, except for those who were in the house with Christ, for they witnessed his being raised. As for the rest, they thought, as the Jews thought, that the one crucified was the Messiah, son of Mary, until they mentioned that Mary sat under that crucified one and cried, and it is said that he spoke to her, and God knows best, and all of this is from God’s testing of His servants, because of the great wisdom He has in that. God has made the matter clear, evident and evident, and made it manifest in the Great Qur’an, which He revealed to His noble Messenger, supported by miracles, clear proofs and evidence. The Most High said: And He is the most truthful of speakers and the Lord of the worlds, the Knower of secrets and consciences, the One who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth, the Knower of what was and what will be and what would not have been if it had been, how it would have been. And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear to them meaning they saw his resemblance and thought it was him. That is why He said: “And indeed, those who differ therein are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption” meaning by that those Jews who claimed that he killed him, and those ignorant Christians who handed him over to them, all of them in doubt about that and confusion and misguidance and madness. That is why He said: And they did not kill him for certain meaning they did not kill him, certain that it was him, but rather they doubted and imagined it. “Rather, God raised him up to Himself. And God is Exalted in Might” meaning His side is inviolable, and no one who seeks refuge at His door is wronged, Wise meaning in all that He decrees and decides of the matters that He created it, and He has the perfect wisdom, the conclusive argument, the great authority, and the ancient command. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God wanted to raise Jesus to heaven, he came out to his companions, and in the house were twelve men from the disciples, meaning he came out to them from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping with water, and he said: Among you is he who will disbelieve in me twelve times, after having believed in me. He said: Then he said: Which of you will be cast upon my likeness so that he will be killed in my place and be with me in my degree? Then a young man from the youngest of them stood up and said to him: Sit down. Then he repeated it to them. The young man stood up and said: Sit down. Then he repeated it to them. The young man stood up and said: I am. Then he said: It is you. Then the likeness of Jesus was cast upon him, and Jesus was raised from a window in the house to heaven. He said: The request came from the Jews, so they took the likeness and killed him and then crucified him. Some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after they had believed in him, and they split into three groups. One group said: God was with us as He willed, then He ascended to heaven. These are the Jacobites. One group said: The Son of God was with us as He willed, then God raised him to Himself. These are the Nestorians. One group said: The servant of God and His Messenger was with us as God willed, then God raised him to Himself. These are the Muslims. Then the two disbelieving women joined forces against the Muslim woman and killed her. Islam remained obliterated until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a sound chain of transmission back to Ibn Abbas. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah in a similar manner. More than one of the early Muslims mentioned it likewise, that he said to them: Which of you? He will be cast as my likeness and will be killed in my place, and he will be my companion in heaven. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Jesus came with seventeen of his disciples in a house and surrounded them. When they entered upon him, God Almighty made them all look like Jesus. They said to them: You have bewitched us so that Jesus may appear to us, or we will kill you all. Jesus said to his companions: Who among you will sell himself for Paradise today? One of them said: I will. He went out to them and said: I am Jesus and God made him look like Jesus. They took him, killed him, and crucified him. Then he appeared to them, and they thought that they had killed Jesus. The Christians thought the same that he was Jesus. God raised Jesus that day. This is a very strange context. Ibn Jarir said: It was narrated from Wahb something similar to this statement, which is what Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Ismail bin Abdul Karim told us, Abdul Samad bin Maqal told me that he heard Wahb say: When God informed Jesus, son of Mary, that he would leave this world, he was afraid of death and it was difficult for him, so he called the disciples and made food for them, and said: Bring me here tonight, for I have a need of you. So when they gathered around him at night, he had dinner for them and stood up to serve them. When they finished eating, he began to wash their hands, and perform ablution with his own hand, and wipe their hands with his clothes. They were astonished by that and hated it, so he said: Whoever rejects me tonight for anything I do, is not from me, and I am not from him. So they acknowledged him until he finished that, and he said: As for what I did with you tonight, in serving you food, and washing your hands with my own hand, let me be an example for you, for you see that I am the best of you, so do not be arrogant towards one another, and let some of you offer themselves to others as I offered myself to you. As for my need tonight, That I seek your help with, so that you call upon God for me, and strive in supplication that He delay my death. So when they set themselves up to supplicate, and wanted to strive hard, sleep overcame them until they were unable to supplicate. So he began to wake them up and say: Glory be to God, will you not be patient with me for one night, and help me in it? They said: By God, we do not know what is wrong with us. We used to spend a lot of time talking, but tonight we cannot stand to spend a lot of time talking, and we do not want to supplicate except that we are prevented from doing so. So he said: The shepherd goes and the sheep scatter, and he began to say words similar to this, eulogizing himself. Then he said: The truth is that one of you will disbelieve in me before the rooster crows three times, and one of you will sell me for a few dirhams and eat my price. So they went out and dispersed, and the Jews were looking for him. They took Simon, one of the disciples, and said: This is one of his companions. But he denied it and said: I am not his companion. So they left him. Then others took him, and he also denied it. Then he heard the sound of a rooster, so he wept and grieved him. When morning came, one of the disciples came to the Jews and said: What do you find for me if I guide you to the Messiah? So they offered him thirty dirhams, so he took them and guided them to him. Before that, he had been confused. So they took him and made sure of him and tied him with a rope. They led him and said to him: You used to raise the dead, rebuke the devil, and heal the insane. Will you not save yourself from this rope? And they spat on him, and threw thorns at him, until they brought him to the wood on which they wanted to crucify him, so God raised him up to Him, and they crucified what appeared to them, and he remained for seven days, then his mother and the woman whom Jesus, peace be upon him, had treated, and whom God had cured of madness, came crying where he was crucified, so Jesus came to them and said: Why are you crying? They said: On you, so he said: God has raised me up to Him, and nothing has befallen me except good, and this appeared to them, so order the disciples to meet me at such and such a place, so they met him at that place eleven, and they lost the one who sold him and the Jews had led him to him, so he asked him about his companions, and he said: He regretted what he had done, so he choked and killed himself, so he said: If he had repented, God would have accepted his repentance. Then he asked them about a boy who followed them called Yahya, and he said: He is with you, so go, for every man will come to speak the language of his people, so let him warn them and leave them, a very strange context. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: The name of the king of the Children of Israel who was sent to Jesus to kill him was a man from among them called Dawud. When they decided to do that to him, no servant of God was as terrified by death as I have been told, nor was he as distressed by it as he was, nor did he supplicate to God to remove it from him as he did, to the point that he would say, as they claim: O God, if you are removing this cup from one of your creation, then remove it from me. And his skin was bleeding from the distress of that, so he entered the entrance where they decided to enter upon him in order to kill him and his companions, who were thirteen, with Jesus, peace be upon him. When he was certain that they were going to enter upon him, he said to his companions from the disciples, and they were twelve men: Pharos, and James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and Andreas, and Philip, and the son of Jelma, and Mantha, and Thomas, and James the son of Hilkaia, and Thaddeus, and Cathanias, and Judas Zechariah Jota. Ibn Hamid said: Salamah said: Ibn Ishaq said: And among what was mentioned to me was a man named Sargis, and they were thirteen men besides Jesus, peace be upon him, whom the Christians denied, and that was because he was the one who appeared to the Jews in the place of Jesus. He said: I do not know if he was one of these twelve, so they denied him when they acknowledged to the Jews the crucifixion of Jesus and disbelieved in what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought of the report about him. If they were thirteen, then they entered the entrance when they entered, and they were fourteen with Jesus, and if they were twelve, then they entered the entrance and they were thirteen. Ibn Ishaq said: A man who had been a Christian and then converted to Islam told me that when Jesus received the message from God, I will raise you up to Me, he said: O group of disciples, which of you would like to be my companion in Paradise so that he may appear to the people in my image and they may kill him in my place? Sargis said: I will, O Spirit of God. He said: Sit in my place, so he sat in it, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised, so they entered upon him, and they took him and crucified him, and it was he whom they crucified, and he appeared to them to him, and their number when they entered with Jesus was known, and they saw them and counted their number, and when they entered upon him to take him, they found Jesus and his companions, as they saw, and they missed a man from the number, and he is the one about whom they differed, and they did not know Jesus, until they gave Judas Zachariah Jota thirty dirhams on the condition that he would guide them to him and introduce him to them, so he said to them: When you enter upon him, I will kiss him, and he is the one who came, so take him, so when they entered, and Jesus was raised and he saw Sargis in the form of Jesus, he did not doubt that it was him, so he leaned over him and kissed him, so they took him and crucified him. Then Judas Zachariah John regretted what he had done, so he strangled himself with a rope until he killed himself. He is cursed among the Christians, and he was one of his companions. Some Christians claim that he was Judas Zachariah John, and he was the one who was made to look like him to them, so they crucified him while he was saying: I am not your companion, I am the one who showed you him. And God knows which of them it was. Ibn Jarir said on the authority of Mujahid: They crucified a man who was made to look like Jesus, and God Almighty raised Jesus to heaven alive. Ibn Jarir chose that the likeness of Jesus was cast on all of his companions. And the Almighty said: “And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.” Ibn Jarir said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, meaning before the death of Jesus. This is directed to the fact that all of them will believe in him when he descends to kill the Antichrist, so all religions will become one, which is the pure religion of Islam, the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: before the death of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Al-Awfi said something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Abu Malik said regarding His statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: that is when Jesus descends, and before the death of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, there will not remain anyone from the People of the Scripture but will believe in him before his death. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, meaning the Jews in particular. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He means Al-Najashi and his companions, both of them were narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Abu Raja told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will surely believe in him before his death, he said: Before the death of Jesus. By God, he is alive in the sight of God, but when he descends, they will all believe in him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Othman Al-Laheqi told us, Juwairiyah bin Bashir told us, he said: I heard a man say to Al-Hasan, O Abu Saeed, the statement of God Almighty: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will surely believe in him before his death, he said: Before the death of Jesus, God raised Jesus to Himself and He will send him before the Day of Resurrection to a station in which the righteous and the wicked will believe. And this is what Qatada and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said, and more than one, and this statement is the truth, as we will explain later with conclusive evidence, God willing, and in Him is trust and upon Him is reliance. Ibn Jarir said: Others said: What is meant by that is, There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him in Jesus before the death of the owner of the Scripture. He mentioned that whoever directed that to him knew the truth from falsehood because everyone who is afflicted with death, his soul will not depart until the truth is distinguished from falsehood in his religion. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, he said: No Jew will die until he believes in Jesus. Al-Muthanna told me, Shibl told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, But that he will surely believe in him before his death every owner of the Scripture believes in Jesus before his death, before the death of the owner of the Scripture. Ibn Abbas said: If his neck were struck, his soul would not depart until he believes in Jesus. Ibn Hamid told us, Abu Numailah Yahya bin Wadh told us, Hussain bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A Jew will not die until he testifies that Jesus is the servant and messenger of God, even if he is hastened to do so with weapons. Ishaq bin Ibrahim and Habib bin al-Shaheed told me, Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. He said: It is in my father’s reading before their death. No Jew will ever die until he believes in Jesus. It was said to Ibn Abbas: What do you think if he falls from the top of a house? He said: He speaks about it while falling. It was said: What do you think if I behead one of them? He said: His tongue stutters with it. And Sufyan al-Thawri narrated the same from Khasif, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. He said: No Jew will die until he believes in Jesus, peace be upon him, and if he is struck with the sword he will speak about it. He said: And if he falls he will speak about it while he is falling. And Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated the same from Shu’bah, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. So all of these are authentic chains of transmission back to Ibn Abbas. And it was also authenticated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Muhammad ibn Sirin, and al-Dahhak and Juwaybir say the same. Al-Suddi said and narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he transmitted the reading of Abi bin Kaab: before their death. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: except that he will believe in him before his death, he said: None of them will die until he believes in Jesus before he dies. This may mean that al-Hasan meant what was mentioned above, and it may mean that he meant what these people meant. Ibn Jarir said, and others said: The meaning of this is that there is none from the People of the Book but that he will believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before the death of the owner of the Book. Mention of those who said that Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Hamid, he said: Ikrimah said: The Christian and the Jew will not die until they believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his statement: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. Then Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of these statements is the first statement, which is that no one from the People of the Scripture will remain after the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, except that he will believe in him before the death of Jesus, peace be upon him. There is no doubt that what Ibn Jarir said is correct, because the intended meaning of the context of the verse is to establish the invalidity of what the Jews claimed about the killing and crucifixion of Jesus, and the surrender of those ignorant Christians who surrendered to them, so God informed that it was not like that, but rather it appeared to them, so they killed the resemblance without realizing it, then He raised him to Himself, and that he remains alive, and that he will descend before the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by the successive hadiths that we will cite, God willing, soon, so he will kill the Messiah of misguidance, break the cross, kill the pig, and abolish the jizya, meaning he will not accept it. From any of the people of religions, but he does not accept anything but Islam or the sword, so this noble verse informed that all the people of the Book will believe in him at that time and not one of them will fail to believe in him, and for this reason He said: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will believe in him before his death meaning before the death of Jesus, peace be upon him, whom the Jews and those who agreed with them from the Christians claimed that he was killed and crucified and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them meaning because of their deeds that he witnessed from them before he was raised to heaven and after his descent to earth. As for those who interpreted this verse to mean that every person of the Book will not die until he believes in Jesus or Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon them, this is the reality, and that is because when everyone is dying, what he was ignorant of becomes clear to him, so he believes in him, but that faith will not be beneficial to him if he has seen the angel, as God Almighty said at the beginning of this surah And repentance is not for those who do evil until, when death approaches one of them, he says, “Indeed, I have repented now” the verse. And God the Almighty said: “And when they saw Our might, they said: We believe in God alone” 2:10. This indicates the weakness of what Ibn Jarir used as evidence to refute this statement, where he said: If this was what was meant by this verse, then everyone who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or in the Messiah from among those who disbelieved in them would be of their religion, and then his relatives from his religion would not inherit from him, because the Truthful One had informed him that he believed in him before his death. This is not good, since his belief does not necessarily mean that he becomes a Muslim. Do you not see the statement of Ibn Abbas: Even if he were to fall from a high place or be struck with a sword or be devoured by a wild beast, he would necessarily believe in Jesus? Faith in this case is not beneficial and does not remove its owner from his disbelief, for what we have presented. And God knows best. Whoever ponders carefully and looks closely, it will become clear to him that this is the reality, but this does not necessarily mean that this is what was meant by this verse. Rather, what was meant by it is what we mentioned of confirming the existence of Jesus, peace be upon him, and the continuation of his life in heaven, and that he will descend to earth before the Day of Resurrection to refute these and those from the Jews and Christians whose statements about him differed and clashed. And they were contradictory and opposite and devoid of the truth, so these Jews went too far, and these Christians went too far in belittling the Jews with what they accused him and his mother of of the great things, and the Christians praised him to the point that they claimed in him what he did not have, so they raised him in contrast to those from the position of prophethood to the position of divinity, exalted be He above what these and those say, greatly exalted, and He is transcendent and sanctified, there is no god but Him. Mentioning the hadiths that were reported about the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, to Earth from heaven at the end of time Before the Day of Resurrection, and that he calls for the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said in the Book of Mentioning the Prophets in his Sahih, which is accepted: The descent of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa`id bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the son of Mary will soon descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and wealth will overflow to the point that no one will accept it, and prostration will be better for them than the world and what is in it.” Then Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: “And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness.” Muslim narrated it likewise on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Halwani and Abd bin Hamid, both on the authority of Yaqub, on his authority. Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Al-Zuhri on his authority. And they narrated it on the authority of Al-Layth on the authority of Al-Zuhri on his authority, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Hafsah on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The son of Mary will soon descend among you as a just judge. He will kill the Antichrist, kill the pig, break the cross, abolish the jizyah, and wealth will be abundant. Prostration will be for God, Lord of the worlds, but only one.” Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death, the death of Jesus, son of Mary. Then Abu Hurairah repeated it three times. Another way On the authority of Abu Hurairah, Imam Ahmad said: Ruh bin Abi Hafsah told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hanzala bin Ali Al-Aslami, on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Jesus will enter the state of ihram at Faj Al-Rawha’ for Hajj or Umrah, or both of them together. Muslim narrated it in this way alone on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, and Yunus bin Yazid, all three of them on the authority of Al-Zuhri on this authority. Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Sufyan Ibn Husayn told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Jesus, son of Mary, will descend and kill the pig, and the cross will be erased, and prayers will be collected for him, and money will be given until it is no longer accepted, and the tax will be abolished, and he will descend to Ar-Rawha’ and perform Hajj or Umrah from there, or combine them.” He said: Abu Hurayrah recited: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will believe in him before his death, the verse, so Hanzala claimed that Abu Hurayrah said: He will believe in him before the death of Jesus, so I do not know whether all of this is a hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or something that Abu Hurayrah said, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Musa Muhammad Ibn Al-Muthanna, on the authority of Yazid Ibn Harun, on the authority of Sufyan Ibn Husayn, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on his authority. Another chain of transmission Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Nafi’, the freed slave of Abu Qatada Al-Ansari, that Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will you be when the Messiah, son of Mary, descends among you and your Imam is from among you? Aqeel and Al-Awza’i followed him, and Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Uthman ibn Umar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, both of them on the authority of Al-Zuhri with it. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Yunus, Al-Awza’i, and Ibn Dhi’b with it. Another way Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Qatada told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The prophets are brothers by bloodline, their mothers are different, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him: a square-built man, reddish and white, wearing two Egyptian garments, as if his head were dripping even if no wetness had touched him. He will break the cross, kill the pig, abolish the jizya, and call people to Islam. God will destroy all religions in his time except Islam, and God will destroy the Antichrist in his time. Then security will prevail on the earth until lions will graze with camels, leopards with cows, and wolves with sheep, and children will play with snakes that will not harm them. He will remain for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him.” Abu Dawud narrated it likewise on the authority of Hadiya ibn Khalid, on the authority of Hammam ibn Yahya. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir, and no one else mentioned this verse except him, on the authority of Bishr bin Muadh, on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, both of them on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Adam, who is the client of Umm Barthan, the owner of the water-carrier, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar, and he said: People will fight for the sake of Islam. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu al-Yaman, on the authority of Shu’ayb, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, and the prophets are paternal brothers, there is no prophet between me and him. Then Muhammad bin Sinan narrated it on the authority of Falih bin Sulayman, on the authority of Hilal bin Ali, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the closest of people to Jesus, son of Mary, in this world and the hereafter.
