Abu Sa`id said: By God, we did not see that man as anyone but Umar ibn al-Khattab, until he passed away. Then Al-Maharibi said: We returned to the hadith of Abu Rafi’ who said: Among his trials is that he will command the sky to rain and it rains, then he will command the earth to grow and it will grow. Among his trials is that he will pass by a tribe and they will deny him, so no grazing animal will remain except that it will perish. Among his trials is that he will pass by a tribe and they will believe him, then he will command the sky to rain and it will rain, and he will command the earth to grow and it will grow until their livestock return that day fatter than ever, with the largest and longest flanks and the most fertile udders, and nothing on earth will remain except that he will tread upon it and prevail over it, except Mecca and Medina, for he will not come to them from one of their passages except that the angels will meet him with drawn swords until he descends at the red mountain at the end of the salt marsh, then Medina will shake with its people three times, and no hypocrite, male or female, will remain except that he will go out to him, and the filth will be banished from it as the bellows banish the filth of iron, and that day will be called the Day of Deliverance. Umm Sharik bint Abi Al-Akr said: O Messenger of God, where will the Arabs be on that day? He said: “They will be few and most of them will be in Jerusalem on that day, and their imam will be a righteous man. While their imam has advanced to lead them in the dawn prayer, Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, will descend. That imam will walk backwards for Jesus, peace be upon him, to advance. Jesus will place his hand between his shoulders and say: ‘Advance and pray, for it has been established for you.’ So their imam will lead them in prayer. When he has finished, Jesus will say: ‘Open the door.’ So it will be opened, and behind him will be the Antichrist with seventy thousand Jews, all of them with a decorated sword and a shield. When the Antichrist looks at him, he will melt as salt melts in water and will run away. Jesus will say: ‘I have a blow against you that you have never dealt to me before.’ He will catch up with him at the eastern gate of Ludd and kill him. God will defeat the Jews, and nothing that God Almighty has created will remain in which a Jew could hide, except that God will make that thing speak, neither stone, nor tree, nor wall, nor animal - except the gharqadah, for it is one of their trees that does not speak - except that it will say: ‘O Muslim servant of God, this is a Jew, so come and kill him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘His days will be forty years, and the year is like half a twig.’” The year, and the year is like the month, and the month is like a Friday, and its last days are like a spark. One of you will be at the gate of the city and will not reach its other gate until the evening.” It was said to him: How do we pray, O Prophet of God, during those short days? He said: You can estimate the prayer as you estimate it during these long days, then pray. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then Jesus, son of Mary, will be in my nation a just judge and a fair leader. He will break the cross and slaughter the pig, and abolish the jizya, and abandon the charity. He will not seek to harm a sheep or a camel. Hatred and animosity will be lifted and the venom of every venomous creature will be removed until a newborn puts his hand into a snake and it will not harm him, and a newborn lion will flee and it will not lead her astray. The wolf will be among the sheep as if it were its dog. The earth will be filled with peace as it fills water, and the word will be one and none will be worshipped except God. War will lay down its burdens and the Quraysh will be stripped of their kingdom, and the earth will have the light of silver and its plants will grow as they did during the time of Adam until a group of people will gather to pick grapes and satisfy them, and a group of people will gather around a pomegranate and it will satisfy them.” The bull will be worth so-and-so in money, and the horse will be worth dirhams.” It was said: O Messenger of God, what makes a horse cheap? He said: It will never be ridden for war. It was said to him: What makes a bull expensive? He said: “It will plough the entire earth, and before the emergence of the Antichrist there will be three difficult years in which people will be afflicted with severe famine. God will command the sky in the first year to withhold a third of its rain, and command the earth to withhold a third of its vegetation. Then God will command the sky in the second year to withhold two-thirds of its rain, and command the earth to withhold two-thirds of its vegetation. Then God the Almighty will command the sky in the third year to withhold all of its rain, so that not a single drop will fall, and command the earth to withhold all of its vegetation, so that no hoofed animal will remain except that it will perish, except what God wills.” It was said: How will people live at that time? He said: Tahlil, Takbir, Tasbih, and Tahmid, and this will be done to them like food. Ibn Majah said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Tanafisi say: I heard Abd al-Rahman al-Maharibi say: This hadith should be given to the teacher so that he can teach it to the children in school. This hadith is very strange from this aspect, and some of it has supporting evidence from other hadiths, including what was narrated by Muslim, and the hadith of Nafi’ and Salim on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You will fight the Jews and kill them until a stone says: O Muslim, this is a Jew, so come and kill him.” And he has it on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Hour will not come until the Muslims fight the Jews and the Muslims kill them until a Jew hides behind a stone or a tree, and the stone or tree says: O Muslim, O servant of God, there is a Jew behind me, so come and kill him - except for the gharqad, for it is one of the trees of the Jews.” Let us mention the hadith of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an here because of its similarity to this hadith. Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Abu Khaithamah Zuhair bin Harb told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber told us, Yahya bin Jaber Al-Ta’i, the judge of Homs told me, Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair told me on the authority of his father Jubair bin Nufayr Al-Hadrami that he heard Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an Al-Kalabi H. Muhammad bin Mihran Al-Razi told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jaber told us on the authority of Yahya bin Jaber Al-Ta’i, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubair, on the authority of his father Jubair bin Nufayr, on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the Antichrist one morning, and he lowered and raised his voice until we thought he was in a group of palm trees. When we went to him, he could see that in our faces, so he said: What is the matter with you? We said: O Messenger of God, you mentioned the Antichrist one morning, so you lowered your voice and raised it until we thought he was among a group of palm trees. He said: "I fear nothing for you except the Antichrist. He will emerge while I am among you, then I will be his opponent on your behalf. But if he emerges while I am not among you, then every man will be his own opponent, and God will be my successor over every Muslim. He is a young, well-built man with a bulging eye. I liken him to Abd al-Uzza ibn Qatan. Whoever among you meets him, let him recite to him the opening verses of Surat al-Kahf. He will emerge from a gap between Syria and Iraq, and he will ravage right and left. O servants of God, be steadfast." We said: O Messenger of God, how long will he remain on earth? He said: Forty days, one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days. We said: O Messenger of God, and how quickly will he travel on earth? He said: “Like rain that the wind has turned back, so he comes to a people and calls them and they believe in him and respond to him. He orders the sky to rain, and the earth to produce vegetation, and their livestock return to them with the tallest peaks, the most abundant udders, and the most abundant flanks. Then he comes to the people and calls them and they respond to him, so he turns away from them and they become destitute and have nothing of their wealth in their hands. He passes by a ruin and says to it: Bring forth your treasures, and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees. Then he calls a man full of youth and strikes him with the sword and cuts him into two pieces, like a target shot. Then he calls him and he accepts and his face lights up and he laughs. While he is like this, God sends the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and he descends at the white minaret east of Damascus between two wells, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, it drips, and when he raises it, pearls flow from it. It is not permissible for an unbeliever to find the scent of his breath except that he dies, and his breath ends where his gaze ends, so he seeks it.” Until he catches up with him at the gate of Ludd, and kills him, then Jesus, peace be upon him, will come to a people whom God has protected from him, and he will wipe their faces and tell them of their degrees in Paradise. While he is like that, God Almighty will inspire Jesus: I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one can fight, so protect My servants to the mountain. God will send Gog and Magog, and they will swarm from every side. The first of them will pass by the Sea of Galilee and drink what is in it, and the last of them will pass by and say: There was once water here. The Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will attend until the head of a bull for one of them is better than a hundred dinars for one of you today. The Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will desire it, and God will send upon them the filth in their necks, and they will become like the death of a single soul. Then the Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will descend to the earth, and they will not find a space on the earth a span but that it will be filled with their stench and stench. The Prophet of God Jesus and his companions will desire God, and God will send birds like the necks of camels, and they will carry them and throw them wherever He wills. God, then God sends rain from which no house of mud or hair can withstand, and it washes the earth until it leaves it like a slate. Then it is said to the earth: Bring forth your fruit and return your blessing. On that day, a group will eat from the pomegranate and seek shade under its shell, and God will bless the Messengers until even a single camel will suffice the groups. While they are like that, God sends a pleasant wind that takes them under their armpits, and God takes the soul of every believer and every Muslim, and the worst of people will remain, fighting each other like donkeys, and the Hour will come upon them.” Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the People of Sunnah from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir with it. We will also mention it from the path of Ahmad when God the Almighty says in Surat al-Anbiya’: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose (al-Anbiya’: 11). Another hadith Muslim also said in his Sahih: Ubayd God ibn Muadh al-Anbari told us, my father told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Salim, who said: I heard Ya’qub ibn Asim ibn Urwah ibn Mas’ud al-Thaqafi say: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr, and a man came to him and said: What is this hadith that you are talking about, saying that the Hour will come at such and such a time? He said: Glory be to God, or there is no god but God, or a word like them, I intended not to tell anyone anything ever, but I said: You will see in a little while a great matter: He will burn the House and it will happen and it will happen, then he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Antichrist will emerge among my nation and will remain for forty, I do not know whether it will be a day or forty months or forty years, then God, the Most High, will send Jesus, son of Mary, who looks like Urwah ibn Mas`ud, and he will seek him out and kill him, then the people will remain for seven years with no enmity between two people, then God will send a cold wind from the direction of Ash-Sham, and no one will remain on the face of the earth in whose heart there is an atom’s weight of goodness - or faith - except that it will seize him, so that if one of you were to enter the heart of a mountain, it would enter it until it seizes him.” He said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “The worst of people will remain as light as birds and as dreamy as wild beasts, they will not recognize good and will not denounce evil, then Satan will appear to them and say: Will you not respond? They will say: What do you command us to do?” He will command them to worship idols, and they will have their livelihood and good living. Then the trumpet will be blown, and no one will hear it except that he will listen attentively and raise his head. He said: The first one to hear it will be a man filling the water tank of his camels. He said: He will be struck dumb and the people will be struck dumb. Then God will send - or he said - God will send down rain like dew - or he said the shade - of Nu'man the doubter - and the bodies of the people will grow from it. Then it will be blown again and they will be standing and looking. Then it will be said: O people, come to your Lord. Stop them, for they will be questioned. Then it will be said: Bring out the people of Hell. It will be said: From how many? It will be said: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. He said: That is a day when the children will turn gray, and that is a day when the shin will be uncovered. Then Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it in their interpretation together on the authority of Muhammad ibn Bashar, on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of Nu'man ibn Salim on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd God ibn Tha’labah al-Ansari, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Zayd al-Ansari, on the authority of Mujammi ibn Jariyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The son of Mary will kill the Antichrist at the gate of Ludd - or next to Ludd. Ahmad also narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah from the hadith of al-Layth and al-Awza’i, all three of them on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ubayd God ibn Tha’labah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of his uncle Mujammi ibn Jariyah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The son of Mary will kill the Antichrist at the gate of Ludd. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it on the authority of Qutaybah on the authority of al-Layth, and he said: This is a sound hadith. He said: There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, Nafi’ ibn Utbah, Abu Barzah, Hudhayfah ibn Asid, Abu Hurayrah, Kaysan, Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As, Jabir, Abu Umamah, Ibn Mas’ud, Abdullah ibn Amr, and Samurah. Ibn Jundub, Al-Nawwas Ibn Sam’an, Amr Ibn Awf, and Hudhayfah Ibn Al-Yaman, may God be pleased with them. What he meant by the narration of these is what mentions the Antichrist and Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, killing him. As for the hadiths that mention the Antichrist only, they are very many, and they are more than can be counted due to their prevalence and the frequency of their narration in the Sahihs, Hassans, Musnads, and other books. Another hadith - Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Furat, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked down upon us from Arafat while we were discussing the Hour, and he said: “The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, and the Antichrist, and three landslides: one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden and drive - or gather - the people, spending the night with them wherever they spend the night, and resting with them wherever they rest.” And Muslim and the people of the Sunnah narrated it in this way from the hadith of Furat al-Qazzaz. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’ on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, on the authority of Abu Sarihah, on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Asid al-Ghifari, with a chain of transmission ending with him, and God knows best. These are successive hadiths on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas’ud, Uthman bin Abi al-‘As, Abu Umamah, al-Nawwas bin Sam’an, Abdullah bin Amr bin al-‘As, Mujammi’ bin Jariyah, Abu Sarihah, and Hudhayfah bin Asid, may God be pleased with them. In them is evidence of the manner in which he will descend and his place, that he will be in the Levant, or rather in Damascus, near the eastern minaret, and that this will be when the dawn prayer is performed. In these times, in the year 741, a white minaret was built for the Umayyad Mosque from carved stones in place of the minaret that was destroyed due to the fire attributed to the actions of the Christians - upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection - and most of its construction was done with their money. It was strongly suspected that it was the one on which the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, would descend, and he would kill the pig, break the cross, and impose the jizya tax. It is not acceptable except for Islam, as mentioned in the two Sahihs. This is a statement from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and a confirmation, legislation, and justification for it in that time, when their ailments will be removed and their doubts will be removed from themselves. For this reason, they will all enter the religion of Islam, following Jesus, peace be upon him, and through his hands. For this reason, God Almighty said: There is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death 1:13. This verse is like His statement: And indeed, it is a sign of the Hour 1:13. It was read 1:13 with a fat-ha, meaning a sign and evidence of the approach of the Hour, because he will descend after the emergence of the Antichrist, and God will kill him at his hands. As it is proven in the Sahih that God did not create a disease without sending down a cure for it, and God will send Gog and Magog in his days, and God Almighty will destroy them through the blessing of his supplication. God Almighty said: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they stream forth from every mound, * And the true promise draws near 1:13. (Description of Jesus, peace be upon him) It was mentioned in the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “So when you see him, recognize him: a square-built man with a reddish-white complexion, wearing two white garments, as if his head were dripping even if no wetness had befallen him.” And in the hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an: “He will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus between two Mahroudahs, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowers his head, it drips, and when he raises it, something like pearls flows from it. It is not permissible for a disbeliever to smell the scent of his own breath except that he dies, and his breath ends where his glance ends.” Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the night of my ascension, I met Moses. He said: So I described him, and I thought he was a man. He said: A man with a swaying head, as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah. He said: And I met Jesus. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him and said: Squat, red, as if he had emerged from Dimas, meaning the bathhouse. And I saw Abraham, and I resembled his son to him. Hadith, and Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Mujahid from Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw Moses, Jesus and Abraham. As for Jesus, he was red, curly-haired and broad-chested. As for Moses, he was dark-skinned, large and straight-chested, as if he were from the Zutt men.” And he and Muslim narrated from Musa bin Uqbah from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the Antichrist one day among the people, and said: “God is not one-eyed. Beware, the Antichrist is blind in his right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape.” And Muslim narrated from him, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, “And God showed me at the Kaaba in a dream, and there was a dark man, the most handsome of men you have ever seen, his locks falling between his shoulders, his hair falling, his head dripping with water, and he was placing his hands on the shoulders of two men while he was circumambulating the House. So I said: Who is this?” They said: He is the Messiah, son of Mary. Then I saw behind him a man with curly hair, blind in his right eye, who most closely resembled Ibn Qatan among those I have seen, placing his hands on the shoulders of a man circumambulating the House. I said: Who is this? They said: The Antichrist. Narrated by Ubaydullah on the authority of Nafi’. Then Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Makki, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Saad, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of his father, who said: No, by God, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say that Jesus was red, but he said: “While I was sleeping, I was circumambulating the Kaaba, and there was a red man with smooth hair, swaying between two men, with water dripping from his head - or his head was dripping with water - so I said: Who is this? They said: The son of Mary. So I went to turn around, and there was a red, big man, with curly hair, blind in his right eye, as if his eye was a floating grape. I said: Who is this? They said: The Antichrist, and the person who most closely resembles him is Ibn Qatan.” Al-Zuhri said: A man from Khuza’ah who died in the pre-Islamic era. All of these are the words of Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him. It was mentioned previously in the hadith of Abd Al-Rahman bin Adam on the authority of Abu Hurairah that Jesus, peace be upon him, will remain on earth for forty years after his descent, then he will die and the Muslims will pray over him. And in the hadith of Abdullah bin Umar in Muslim, it is said that he will remain for seven years, so it is possible - and God knows best - that what is meant is He stayed on earth for forty years, the total of his stay on it before he was raised and after he descended. He was raised when he was thirty-three years old, according to the Sahih. This was mentioned in a hadith describing the people of Paradise, that they are in the image of Adam, and the birth of Jesus was thirty-three years old. As for what Ibn Asakir narrated from some of them, that he was raised when he was one hundred and fifty years old, this is strange, strange and remote. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim Ibn Asakir mentioned in the biography of Jesus, son of Mary, in his history, from some of the predecessors, that he will be buried with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his room. And God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness over them. Qatada said: He will bear witness over them that he had conveyed the message from God to them and acknowledged the servitude of God Almighty. This is like the Almighty’s saying at the end of Surat al-Ma’idah 5:“And when God said, ‘O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, ‘Take me and my mother as gods besides God?’ He said, ‘Glory be to You! It is not for me to say that which I have no right to. If I had said it, You knew it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I said to them nothing but what You commanded me, ‘Worship God, my Lord and your Lord.’ And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them. But when You took me up, You were the Observer over them, and You are Witness over all things. If You should punish them, they are Your servants; but if You should forgive them, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.”
4:160: God Almighty tells us that because of the injustice of the Jews and the great sins they committed, He forbade them good things that were permissible for them, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr, he said: Ibn Abbas read: good things that were permissible for them, and this prohibition may be predestined in the sense that God Almighty decreed that they interpreted their book, and distorted and changed things that were permissible for them, so they forbade them for themselves, as a form of strictness, constriction and extremism. It is possible that it is legal in the sense that God Almighty forbade them in the Torah things that were permissible for them before that, as God Almighty said: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed. We have already discussed the verse, and that what is meant is that all foods were permissible for them before the Torah was revealed except for what Israel had forbidden to himself of camel meat and milk. Then God Almighty forbade many things in the Torah. As He said in Surat al-An’am 6:“And We forbade the Jews every animal with claws, and of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat, except what adhered to their backs or the entrails or what was mixed with a bone. That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, and indeed, We are truthful.” That is, We forbade them that because they deserved it due to their transgression, tyranny, opposition to their Messenger, and disagreement with him. For this reason, He said: Then because of wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We forbade them [certain] good things which had been lawful to them, and because of their averting [people] from the way of God. That is, they turned people away and turned themselves away from following the truth, and this is a characteristic of theirs that they have been characterized by since ancient times and recently. For this reason, they were enemies of the Messengers and killed many of the Prophets, and they denied Jesus and Muhammad, may the peace and blessings of God be upon them. And His statement: And they took usury, although they were forbidden from it, meaning that God had forbidden them from usury, but they took it and deceived themselves with various tricks and types of doubts, and they ate people’s money unjustly. God the Almighty said: And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment, then God the Almighty said: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them, meaning those who are steadfast in religion and have a firm footing in beneficial knowledge. We have already discussed this in Surat Al Imran. And the believers is in apposition to those firmly rooted, and its predicate is believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Salam, Tha’laba ibn Sa’iyyah, Asad, Zayd ibn Sa’iyyah, and Asad ibn Ubayd, who entered Islam and believed in what God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with. And his saying: And those who establish prayer is like this in all the copies of the Imams, and likewise it is in the copy of Ubayy ibn Ka’b. Ibn Jarir mentioned that in the copy of Ibn Mas’ud it is and those who establish prayer. He said: The correct reading is for all of them. Then he responded to those who claimed that this was a mistake in the book, then he mentioned the differences of opinion among the people, so some of them said: It is in the accusative case for praise, as came in his saying: And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made a covenant, and those who are patient in poverty and hardship and at the time of battle. He said: This is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, as the poet said: Do not distance my people, who are the poison of the enemy and the scourge of the islands. Those who participate in every battle and are kind to the people Others said: It is in the accusative case in apposition to His statement: By what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, meaning and by those who establish prayer, as if he is saying: By establishing prayer, meaning they acknowledge its obligation and its being prescribed for them, or that what is meant by those who establish prayer are the angels, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, meaning they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and by the angels, and there is a view on this, and God knows best. His statement: and those who give zakat, may mean zakat on wealth, or it may mean zakat on souls, or it may mean both, and God knows best. and the believers in God and the Last Day, meaning they believe that there is no god but God, and they believe in resurrection after death, and the reward for deeds, both good and bad. His statement: those, is the report of what came before, We will give them a great reward, meaning Paradise.
4:161: God Almighty tells us that because of the injustice of the Jews and the great sins they committed, He forbade them good things that were permissible for them, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Maqri told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr, he said: Ibn Abbas read: good things that were permissible for them, and this prohibition may be predestined in the sense that God Almighty decreed that they interpreted their book, and distorted and changed things that were permissible for them, so they forbade them for themselves, as a form of strictness, constriction and extremism. It is possible that it is legal in the sense that God Almighty forbade them in the Torah things that were permissible for them before that, as God Almighty said: All food was lawful to the Children of Israel except what Israel had forbidden to himself before the Torah was revealed. We have already discussed the verse, and that what is meant is that all foods were permissible for them before the Torah was revealed except for what Israel had forbidden to himself of camel meat and milk. Then God Almighty forbade many things in the Torah. As He said in Surat al-An’am 6:“And We forbade the Jews every animal with claws, and of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat, except what adhered to their backs or the entrails or what was mixed with a bone. That is how We recompensed them for their transgression, and indeed, We are truthful.” That is, We forbade them that because they deserved it due to their transgression, tyranny, opposition to their Messenger, and disagreement with him. For this reason, He said: Then because of wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We forbade them [certain] good things which had been lawful to them, and because of their averting [people] from the way of God. That is, they turned people away and turned themselves away from following the truth, and this is a characteristic of theirs that they have been characterized by since ancient times and recently. For this reason, they were enemies of the Messengers and killed many of the Prophets, and they denied Jesus and Muhammad, may the peace and blessings of God be upon them. 4:163: Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Sakin and Adi bin Zaid said: O Muhammad, we do not know that God has sent down anything to any human being after Moses, so God sent down in that regard from their saying: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him to the end of the verses. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told us, Abdul Aziz told us, Abu Ma`shar told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, who said: God revealed, The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven until His saying, And their saying about Mary is a great slander. He said: When he recited it to them, meaning to the Jews, and informed them of their evil deeds, they denied everything that God had revealed and said: God has not revealed anything to any human being, nor to Moses nor to Jesus nor to any prophet. He said: So he untied his camel and said: Nor to anyone. Then God, the Almighty, revealed, And they did not estimate God with His true estimate when they said, God has not revealed anything to any human being. There is a consideration in what Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi said, for this verse in Surat al-An`am is Meccan, and this verse in Surat al-Nisa is Medinan, and it is a response to them when they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to bring down to them a book from the heaven. God, the Almighty, said, And they asked Moses for something greater than that. Then He mentioned their scandals and faults and what they were upon and what they are upon now of lying and slander. Then the Almighty mentioned that He revealed to His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He revealed to other prophets who came before, saying: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, until His saying: And We gave David the Psalms. The Psalms is the name of the book that God revealed to David, peace be upon him, and we will mention the biography of each one of these prophets, upon them be the best prayers and peace from God, when we tell their stories in Surat Al-Anbiya, God willing. In Him is the trust and upon Him is reliance. And His statement: And messengers We have mentioned to you before, and messengers We have not mentioned to you meaning before this verse, meaning in the Meccan surahs and others. And this is the naming of the prophets whose names God mentioned in the Qur’an, and they are: Adam, Idris, Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Shuaib, Moses, Aaron, Jonah, David, Solomon, Elijah, Elisha, Zachariah, John, and Jesus, and likewise Dhul-Kifl according to many of the commentators and their master Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: And messengers We have not related to you means other creations that were not mentioned in the Qur’an. There is a difference of opinion regarding the number of prophets and messengers. The well-known one is the long hadith of Abu Dharr, as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, may God have mercy on him, in his interpretation, where he said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Hasan and al-Husayn bin Abdullah bin Yazid told us, they said: Ibrahim bin Hisham bin Yahya al-Ghassani told us, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: O Messenger of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand. I said: O Messenger of God, how many messengers are there among them? He said: Three hundred and thirteen, a great multitude. I said: O Messenger of God, who was the first of them? He said: Adam. I said: O Messenger of God, a prophet and messenger? He said: Yes, God created him with His hand, then breathed into him from His spirit, then formed him into a tribe. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, four are Syrians: Adam, Seth, Noah, and Enoch, who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen, and four are Arabs: Hud, Salih, Shu’ayb, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr, and the first Prophet from the Children of Israel is Moses and the last of them is Jesus, and the first of the Prophets is Adam, and the last of them is your Prophet.” This hadith was narrated in full by Al-Hafiz Abu Hatim ibn Hibban Al-Busti in his book Al-Anwa’ wa Al-Taqasim, and he marked it as authentic. Abu Al-Faraj ibn Al-Jawzi disagreed with him and mentioned this hadith in his book Al-Mawdoo’at and accused Ibrahim ibn Hisham of it. There is no doubt that more than one of the imams of criticism and authentication spoke about it because of this hadith, and God knows best. This hadith was narrated from another chain of narration on the authority of another companion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Abu al-Mughira told us, Ma'an ibn Rafa'ah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: I said: O Prophet of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand, and the messengers from that are three hundred and fifteen, a large group. Ma'an ibn Rafa'ah al-Salami is weak, Ali ibn Yazid is weak, and al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman is also weak. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Abu Abdullah al-Jawhari al-Basri told us, Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabdhi told us on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand to the Children of Israel, and four thousand to the rest of the people." This is also a weak chain of narration, in which al-Rabdhi is weak, and his sheikh al-Raqashi is weaker than him, and God knows best. Abu Ya`la said: Abu al-Rabi` told us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-`Abdi told us, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among those who passed away from my brothers among the prophets were eight thousand prophets, then there was Jesus, son of Mary, then there was me. We have narrated it from Anas from another source, so al-Hafiz Abu `Abdullah al-Dhahabi told us, Abu al-Fadl ibn `Asakir told us, Imam Bakr al-Qasim ibn Abi Sa`id al-Saffar told us, Abu `Aisha bint Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn al-Saffar told us, al-Sharif Abu al-Sananik Hibat God ibn Abi al-Sahba` Muhammad ibn Haidar al-Qurashi told us, Imam al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq al-Asfarayini told us, he said: Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma`ili told us, Muhammad ibn `Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Ahmad ibn Tariq told us, Muslim ibn Khalid told us, Ziyad ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Safwan ibn Salim, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was sent after eight thousand prophets, four thousand of whom were from the Children of Israel. This is strange from this aspect, and its chain of transmission is acceptable. All of its men are known except for this Ahmad ibn Tariq, for I do not know him to be trustworthy or trustworthy, and God knows best. And the long hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari about the number of prophets, peace be upon them. Muhammad ibn Husayn al-Ajurri said: Abu Bakr Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Faryabi told us by dictation in the month of Rajab in the year two hundred and ninety-seven. Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani told us, my father told us, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting alone, so I sat next to him and said: O Messenger of God, you have commanded me to pray. He said: Prayer is the best thing, so do it often or do it little. I said: O Messenger of God, which deeds are best? He said: Belief in God and jihad in His cause. I said: O Messenger of God, which believers are best? He said: The best of them in character. I said: O Messenger of God, which Muslim is the most Muslim? He said: He from whose tongue and hand people are safe. I said: O Messenger of God, which migration is best? He said: He who abandons evil deeds. I said: O Messenger of God, which prayer is best? He said: Long supplication. I said: O Messenger of God, which fasting is best? He said: An obligatory duty that is sufficient, and with God it is many times greater. I said: O Messenger of God, which jihad is best? He said: He who hamstrings his horse and sheds its blood. I said: O Messenger of God, which slaves are best? He said: The most valuable and most precious to their owners. I said: O Messenger of God, which charity is best? He said: The effort of one who is poor and secretly gives to a poor person. I said: O Messenger of God, which verse revealed to you is the greatest? He said: The Throne Verse. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, the seven heavens with the Throne are like a ring thrown in a desert. The superiority of the Throne over the Throne is like the superiority of the desert over the ring.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many messengers are there? He said: Three hundred and thirteen, a great multitude, and good. I said: Who was the first of them? He said: Adam. I said: A messenger prophet? He said: Yes, God created him with His hand, and breathed into him from His spirit, and made him a tribe. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, four are Syrians: Adam, Seth, and Enoch, who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen, and Noah, and four are Arabs: Hud, Shu’ayb, and Salih, and your prophet Abu Dharr, and the first prophet of the Children of Israel was Moses and the last of them was Jesus, and the first of the messengers was Adam and the last of them was Muhammad.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many books did God send down? He said: “One hundred and four books. God sent down fifty pages to Seth, thirty pages to Enoch, ten pages to Abraham, and before that He sent down ten pages to Moses, and He sent down the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, what were the pages of Abraham? He said: "All of it, O king, the afflicted, the arrogant. I did not send you to gather the world together, but I sent you to respond to the supplication of the oppressed, for I will not respond to it even if it is from an unbeliever and there are similarities in it. And the wise person should have hours: an hour in which he communes with his Lord, an hour in which he holds himself to account, an hour in which he thinks about God's creation, and an hour in which he is alone for his need of food and drink. And the wise person should not be spiteful except for three reasons: provisions for the afterlife, or improvement of his livelihood, or pleasure in something that is not forbidden. And the wise person should be aware of his time, focused on his affairs, guarding his tongue, and whoever considers his speech as part of his deeds will speak little except in what concerns him." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, so what were the scrolls of Moses? He said: "They were all lessons. I am amazed at the one who is certain of death and yet rejoices. I am amazed at the one who is certain of destiny and yet suffers. I am amazed at the one who sees the world and its vicissitudes with its people and yet feels reassured by them. I am amazed at the one who is certain of the reckoning tomorrow and yet does not work." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, do we have in our hands anything of what was in the hands of Abraham and Moses, and what God revealed to you? He said: Yes, read, O Abu Dharr: "Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the life of this world, And the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, The scriptures of Abraham and Moses." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: I advise you to fear God, for it is the head of your affair. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, give me more. He said: You should recite the Qur'an and remember God, for it is a remembrance for you in the heavens and a light for you on the earth....." He said: "Beware of laughing too much, for it kills the heart and takes away the light of the face." I said: "O Messenger of God, tell me more." He said: "You should engage in jihad, for it is the monasticism of my nation." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "You should be silent except for good, for it drives away Satan and helps you in your religious affairs." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Look at those below you and do not look at those above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the favor of God upon you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Love the poor and sit with them, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the favor of God upon you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Maintain ties of kinship even if they sever ties with you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Speak the truth even if it is bitter." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Do not fear the blame of a blamer in God's cause." I said: "Tell me more." He said, “What you know about yourself keeps you away from people, and you do not find fault with them in what you love. It is enough of a defect for you to know about people what you do not know about yourself, or to find fault with them in what you love.” Then he struck my chest with his hand and said, O Abu Dharr, there is no intelligence like planning, no piety like restraint, and no lineage like good character. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ma’an bin Rafa’a, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah that Abu Dharr asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned the matter of prayer, fasting, and charity, and the virtue of the Throne Verse, and there is no power or strength except with God, and the best of martyrs, and the best of slaves, and the prophethood of Adam and that he was spoken to, and the number of prophets and messengers as mentioned above. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: I found in my father’s book written by him: Abdul Mut’ali bin Abdul Wahhab told me, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Umawi told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Abu Al-Wadak, who said: Abu Saeed said: Do the Khawarij believe in the Antichrist? He said: I said: No. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and no prophet was sent to be followed except that he warned his nation against him, and he made clear to me about him what he did not make clear to anyone else, and he is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed, and his right eye is one-eyed and bulging and cannot be hidden as if it were phlegm on a plastered wall, and his left eye is like a shining star, with him from every tongue, and with him is a green image of Paradise in which water flows, and a black image of Hell, smoking.” We have narrated it in the section in which there is the narration of Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili on the authority of Yahya ibn Ma’in: Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the seal of a thousand thousand prophets or more, and God did not send a prophet to his people except that he warned them against the Antichrist. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith, this is its wording with the addition of an alif, and it may have been inserted, and God knows best. The context of Imam Ahmad’s narration is more authentic and more deserving of authenticity, and the men in the chain of transmission of this hadith are not bad. This hadith was narrated by way of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Mujalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and there is not a prophet among them who did not warn his people of the Antichrist, and he has made clear to me what was not made clear to any of them, and he is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed.” His saying: And God spoke to Moses, speaking. This is an honor for Moses, peace be upon him, with this attribute, and that is why he is called: The Speaker. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sulayman Al-Maliki told us, Masih bin Hatim told us, Abdul-Jabbar bin Abdullah told us, he said: A man came to Abu Bakr bin Ayyash and said: I heard a man reciting And God spoke to Moses, speaking. Abu Bakr said: No one recited this except an unbeliever. I recited it according to Al-A’mash, and Al-A’mash recited it according to Yahya bin Waththab, and Yahya bin Waththab recited it according to Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami, and Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami recited it according to Ali bin Abi Talib, and Ali bin Abi Talib recited it according to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And God spoke to Moses, speaking. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, may God have mercy on him, became very angry with the one who recited it like this, because he distorted the wording and meaning of the Qur’an, and this was from the Mu’tazilah who deny that God spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, or spoke to any of His creation, as we narrated from some of the Mu’tazilah that he recited: Some of the sheikhs said: And God spoke to Moses directly. He said to him: O son of a whore, what do you say about the words of God the Almighty: And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him? Meaning that this does not allow for distortion or interpretation. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram told us, Muhammad ibn Marzouq told us, Hani’ ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja’far, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God spoke to Moses, he could see the crawling of ants on a rock in the dark night. It is authentic and was narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Hamid ibn Qays al-A’raj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the day that his Lord spoke to Moses, he was wearing a woolen cloak, a woolen cloak, woolen trousers, and sandals made of the hide of an unslaughtered donkey. Ibn Mardawayh said with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God spoke to Moses with one hundred thousand and forty thousand words in three days, all of them commandments. When Moses heard the speech of the humans, he hated them for what he heard of the speech of the Lord Almighty. This is also a weak chain of transmission, for Juwaybir is weaker, and Ad-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. As for the trace that Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and others narrated on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Isa Al-Raqashi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that he said: When God spoke to Moses on the Day of Mount Sinai, He spoke to him with a speech other than the one He spoke to him on the Day He called to Him. Moses said to Him: O Lord, is this Your speech that You spoke to me? He said: No, O Moses, I spoke to You with the strength of ten thousand tongues, and I have the strength of all tongues, and I am stronger than that. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel, they said: O Moses, describe to us the speech of the Most Merciful. He said: I cannot do it. They said: Then He made it appear to us. He said: Have you not heard the sound of thunderbolts? It is close to them but not to them. This is a weak chain of transmission, for this Al-Fadl Al-Raqashi is extremely weak. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Juz’ bin Jabir Al-Jathami, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: When God spoke to Moses in all languages, Moses said to Him: O Lord, is this Your speech? He said: No, and if I spoke to You with My speech, it would not be right. He said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that resembles Your speech? He said: No, and the most similar of My creation to My speech is the most similar of the thunderbolts you hear. This is attributed to Ka’b Al-Ahbar, and he is narrating from the previous books that contain the stories of the Children of Israel, and in them are the good and the bad. And His statement: Messengers, bringing good tidings and warnings, meaning they bring good tidings to those who obey God and follow His pleasure, and warn those who disobey His command and deny His messengers of punishment and torment. And His statement: “So that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise,” meaning that the Most High sent down His books and sent His messengers with good tidings and warnings, and explained what He loves and is pleased with from what He hates and rejects, so that no excuse would remain for the one who makes an excuse, as the Most High said: “And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, ‘Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger so we could have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced.’” And likewise His statement: And had not a disaster struck them for what their hands had put forth, the verse. It was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No one is more jealous than God, and for that reason He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden. No one loves praise more than God Almighty, and for that reason He has praised Himself. No one loves excuses more than God, and for that reason He sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners.” In another version: For that reason He sent His messengers and revealed His books.
4:164: Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Sakin and Adi bin Zaid said: O Muhammad, we do not know that God has sent down anything to any human being after Moses, so God sent down in that regard from their saying: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him to the end of the verses. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told us, Abdul Aziz told us, Abu Ma`shar told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, who said: God revealed, The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven until His saying, And their saying about Mary is a great slander. He said: When he recited it to them, meaning to the Jews, and informed them of their evil deeds, they denied everything that God had revealed and said: God has not revealed anything to any human being, nor to Moses nor to Jesus nor to any prophet. He said: So he untied his camel and said: Nor to anyone. Then God, the Almighty, revealed, And they did not estimate God with His true estimate when they said, God has not revealed anything to any human being. There is a consideration in what Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi said, for this verse in Surat al-An`am is Meccan, and this verse in Surat al-Nisa is Medinan, and it is a response to them when they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to bring down to them a book from the heaven. God, the Almighty, said, And they asked Moses for something greater than that. Then He mentioned their scandals and faults and what they were upon and what they are upon now of lying and slander. Then the Almighty mentioned that He revealed to His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He revealed to other prophets who came before, saying: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, until His saying: And We gave David the Psalms. The Psalms is the name of the book that God revealed to David, peace be upon him, and we will mention the biography of each one of these prophets, upon them be the best prayers and peace from God, when we tell their stories in Surat Al-Anbiya, God willing. In Him is the trust and upon Him is reliance. And His statement: And messengers We have mentioned to you before, and messengers We have not mentioned to you meaning before this verse, meaning in the Meccan surahs and others. And this is the naming of the prophets whose names God mentioned in the Qur’an, and they are: Adam, Idris, Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Shuaib, Moses, Aaron, Jonah, David, Solomon, Elijah, Elisha, Zachariah, John, and Jesus, and likewise Dhul-Kifl according to many of the commentators and their master Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: And messengers We have not related to you means other creations that were not mentioned in the Qur’an. There is a difference of opinion regarding the number of prophets and messengers. The well-known one is the long hadith of Abu Dharr, as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, may God have mercy on him, in his interpretation, where he said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Hasan and al-Husayn bin Abdullah bin Yazid told us, they said: Ibrahim bin Hisham bin Yahya al-Ghassani told us, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: O Messenger of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand. I said: O Messenger of God, how many messengers are there among them? He said: Three hundred and thirteen, a great multitude. I said: O Messenger of God, who was the first of them? He said: Adam. I said: O Messenger of God, a prophet and messenger? He said: Yes, God created him with His hand, then breathed into him from His spirit, then formed him into a tribe. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, four are Syrians: Adam, Seth, Noah, and Enoch, who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen, and four are Arabs: Hud, Salih, Shu’ayb, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr, and the first Prophet from the Children of Israel is Moses and the last of them is Jesus, and the first of the Prophets is Adam, and the last of them is your Prophet.” This hadith was narrated in full by Al-Hafiz Abu Hatim ibn Hibban Al-Busti in his book Al-Anwa’ wa Al-Taqasim, and he marked it as authentic. Abu Al-Faraj ibn Al-Jawzi disagreed with him and mentioned this hadith in his book Al-Mawdoo’at and accused Ibrahim ibn Hisham of it. There is no doubt that more than one of the imams of criticism and authentication spoke about it because of this hadith, and God knows best. This hadith was narrated from another chain of narration on the authority of another companion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Abu al-Mughira told us, Ma'an ibn Rafa'ah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: I said: O Prophet of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand, and the messengers from that are three hundred and fifteen, a large group. Ma'an ibn Rafa'ah al-Salami is weak, Ali ibn Yazid is weak, and al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman is also weak. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Abu Abdullah al-Jawhari al-Basri told us, Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabdhi told us on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand to the Children of Israel, and four thousand to the rest of the people." This is also a weak chain of narration, in which al-Rabdhi is weak, and his sheikh al-Raqashi is weaker than him, and God knows best. Abu Ya`la said: Abu al-Rabi` told us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-`Abdi told us, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among those who passed away from my brothers among the prophets were eight thousand prophets, then there was Jesus, son of Mary, then there was me. We have narrated it from Anas from another source, so al-Hafiz Abu `Abdullah al-Dhahabi told us, Abu al-Fadl ibn `Asakir told us, Imam Bakr al-Qasim ibn Abi Sa`id al-Saffar told us, Abu `Aisha bint Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn al-Saffar told us, al-Sharif Abu al-Sananik Hibat God ibn Abi al-Sahba` Muhammad ibn Haidar al-Qurashi told us, Imam al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq al-Asfarayini told us, he said: Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma`ili told us, Muhammad ibn `Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Ahmad ibn Tariq told us, Muslim ibn Khalid told us, Ziyad ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Safwan ibn Salim, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was sent after eight thousand prophets, four thousand of whom were from the Children of Israel. This is strange from this aspect, and its chain of transmission is acceptable. All of its men are known except for this Ahmad ibn Tariq, for I do not know him to be trustworthy or trustworthy, and God knows best. And the long hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari about the number of prophets, peace be upon them. Muhammad ibn Husayn al-Ajurri said: Abu Bakr Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Faryabi told us by dictation in the month of Rajab in the year two hundred and ninety-seven. Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani told us, my father told us, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting alone, so I sat next to him and said: O Messenger of God, you have commanded me to pray. He said: Prayer is the best thing, so do it often or do it little. I said: O Messenger of God, which deeds are best? He said: Belief in God and jihad in His cause. I said: O Messenger of God, which believers are best? He said: The best of them in character. I said: O Messenger of God, which Muslim is the most Muslim? He said: He from whose tongue and hand people are safe. I said: O Messenger of God, which migration is best? He said: He who abandons evil deeds. I said: O Messenger of God, which prayer is best? He said: Long supplication. I said: O Messenger of God, which fasting is best? He said: An obligatory duty that is sufficient, and with God it is many times greater. I said: O Messenger of God, which jihad is best? He said: He who hamstrings his horse and sheds its blood. I said: O Messenger of God, which slaves are best? He said: The most valuable and most precious to their owners. I said: O Messenger of God, which charity is best? He said: The effort of one who is poor and secretly gives to a poor person. I said: O Messenger of God, which verse revealed to you is the greatest? He said: The Throne Verse. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, the seven heavens with the Throne are like a ring thrown in a desert. The superiority of the Throne over the Throne is like the superiority of the desert over the ring.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many messengers are there? He said: Three hundred and thirteen, a great multitude, and good. I said: Who was the first of them? He said: Adam. I said: A messenger prophet? He said: Yes, God created him with His hand, and breathed into him from His spirit, and made him a tribe. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, four are Syrians: Adam, Seth, and Enoch, who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen, and Noah, and four are Arabs: Hud, Shu’ayb, and Salih, and your prophet Abu Dharr, and the first prophet of the Children of Israel was Moses and the last of them was Jesus, and the first of the messengers was Adam and the last of them was Muhammad.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many books did God send down? He said: “One hundred and four books. God sent down fifty pages to Seth, thirty pages to Enoch, ten pages to Abraham, and before that He sent down ten pages to Moses, and He sent down the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, what were the pages of Abraham? He said: "All of it, O king, the afflicted, the arrogant. I did not send you to gather the world together, but I sent you to respond to the supplication of the oppressed, for I will not respond to it even if it is from an unbeliever and there are similarities in it. And the wise person should have hours: an hour in which he communes with his Lord, an hour in which he holds himself to account, an hour in which he thinks about God's creation, and an hour in which he is alone for his need of food and drink. And the wise person should not be spiteful except for three reasons: provisions for the afterlife, or improvement of his livelihood, or pleasure in something that is not forbidden. And the wise person should be aware of his time, focused on his affairs, guarding his tongue, and whoever considers his speech as part of his deeds will speak little except in what concerns him." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, so what were the scrolls of Moses? He said: "They were all lessons. I am amazed at the one who is certain of death and yet rejoices. I am amazed at the one who is certain of destiny and yet suffers. I am amazed at the one who sees the world and its vicissitudes with its people and yet feels reassured by them. I am amazed at the one who is certain of the reckoning tomorrow and yet does not work." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, do we have in our hands anything of what was in the hands of Abraham and Moses, and what God revealed to you? He said: Yes, read, O Abu Dharr: "Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the life of this world, And the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, The scriptures of Abraham and Moses." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: I advise you to fear God, for it is the head of your affair. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, give me more. He said: You should recite the Qur'an and remember God, for it is a remembrance for you in the heavens and a light for you on the earth....." He said: "Beware of laughing too much, for it kills the heart and takes away the light of the face." I said: "O Messenger of God, tell me more." He said: "You should engage in jihad, for it is the monasticism of my nation." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "You should be silent except for good, for it drives away Satan and helps you in your religious affairs." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Look at those below you and do not look at those above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the favor of God upon you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Love the poor and sit with them, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the favor of God upon you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Maintain ties of kinship even if they sever ties with you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Speak the truth even if it is bitter." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Do not fear the blame of a blamer in God's cause." I said: "Tell me more." He said, “What you know about yourself keeps you away from people, and you do not find fault with them in what you love. It is enough of a defect for you to know about people what you do not know about yourself, or to find fault with them in what you love.” Then he struck my chest with his hand and said, O Abu Dharr, there is no intelligence like planning, no piety like restraint, and no lineage like good character. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ma’an bin Rafa’a, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah that Abu Dharr asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned the matter of prayer, fasting, and charity, and the virtue of the Throne Verse, and there is no power or strength except with God, and the best of martyrs, and the best of slaves, and the prophethood of Adam and that he was spoken to, and the number of prophets and messengers as mentioned above. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: I found in my father’s book written by him: Abdul Mut’ali bin Abdul Wahhab told me, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Umawi told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Abu Al-Wadak, who said: Abu Saeed said: Do the Khawarij believe in the Antichrist? He said: I said: No. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and no prophet was sent to be followed except that he warned his nation against him, and he made clear to me about him what he did not make clear to anyone else, and he is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed, and his right eye is one-eyed and bulging and cannot be hidden as if it were phlegm on a plastered wall, and his left eye is like a shining star, with him from every tongue, and with him is a green image of Paradise in which water flows, and a black image of Hell, smoking.” We have narrated it in the section in which there is the narration of Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili on the authority of Yahya ibn Ma’in: Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the seal of a thousand thousand prophets or more, and God did not send a prophet to his people except that he warned them against the Antichrist. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith, this is its wording with the addition of an alif, and it may have been inserted, and God knows best. The context of Imam Ahmad’s narration is more authentic and more deserving of authenticity, and the men in the chain of transmission of this hadith are not bad. This hadith was narrated by way of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Mujalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and there is not a prophet among them who did not warn his people of the Antichrist, and he has made clear to me what was not made clear to any of them, and he is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed.” His saying: And God spoke to Moses, speaking. This is an honor for Moses, peace be upon him, with this attribute, and that is why he is called: The Speaker. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sulayman Al-Maliki told us, Masih bin Hatim told us, Abdul-Jabbar bin Abdullah told us, he said: A man came to Abu Bakr bin Ayyash and said: I heard a man reciting And God spoke to Moses, speaking. Abu Bakr said: No one recited this except an unbeliever. I recited it according to Al-A’mash, and Al-A’mash recited it according to Yahya bin Waththab, and Yahya bin Waththab recited it according to Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami, and Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami recited it according to Ali bin Abi Talib, and Ali bin Abi Talib recited it according to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And God spoke to Moses, speaking.
