In Him is the trust and upon Him is reliance. And His statement: And messengers We have mentioned to you before, and messengers We have not mentioned to you meaning before this verse, meaning in the Meccan surahs and others. And this is the naming of the prophets whose names God mentioned in the Qur’an, and they are: Adam, Idris, Noah, Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Shuaib, Moses, Aaron, Jonah, David, Solomon, Elijah, Elisha, Zachariah, John, and Jesus, and likewise Dhul-Kifl according to many of the commentators and their master Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: And messengers We have not related to you means other creations that were not mentioned in the Qur’an. There is a difference of opinion regarding the number of prophets and messengers. The well-known one is the long hadith of Abu Dharr, as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh, may God have mercy on him, in his interpretation, where he said: Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, Ja’far bin Muhammad bin al-Hasan and al-Husayn bin Abdullah bin Yazid told us, they said: Ibrahim bin Hisham bin Yahya al-Ghassani told us, my father told me, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: O Messenger of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand. I said: O Messenger of God, how many messengers are there among them? He said: Three hundred and thirteen, a great multitude. I said: O Messenger of God, who was the first of them? He said: Adam. I said: O Messenger of God, a prophet and messenger? He said: Yes, God created him with His hand, then breathed into him from His spirit, then formed him into a tribe. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, four are Syrians: Adam, Seth, Noah, and Enoch, who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen, and four are Arabs: Hud, Salih, Shu’ayb, and your Prophet, O Abu Dharr, and the first Prophet from the Children of Israel is Moses and the last of them is Jesus, and the first of the Prophets is Adam, and the last of them is your Prophet.” This hadith was narrated in full by Al-Hafiz Abu Hatim ibn Hibban Al-Busti in his book Al-Anwa’ wa Al-Taqasim, and he marked it as authentic. Abu Al-Faraj ibn Al-Jawzi disagreed with him and mentioned this hadith in his book Al-Mawdoo’at and accused Ibrahim ibn Hisham of it. There is no doubt that more than one of the imams of criticism and authentication spoke about it because of this hadith, and God knows best. This hadith was narrated from another chain of narration on the authority of another companion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Abu al-Mughira told us, Ma'an ibn Rafa'ah told us on the authority of Ali ibn Yazid, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: I said: O Prophet of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand, and the messengers from that are three hundred and fifteen, a large group. Ma'an ibn Rafa'ah al-Salami is weak, Ali ibn Yazid is weak, and al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman is also weak. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq Abu Abdullah al-Jawhari al-Basri told us, Makki ibn Ibrahim told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabdhi told us on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand to the Children of Israel, and four thousand to the rest of the people." This is also a weak chain of narration, in which al-Rabdhi is weak, and his sheikh al-Raqashi is weaker than him, and God knows best. Abu Ya`la said: Abu al-Rabi` told us, Muhammad ibn Thabit al-`Abdi told us, Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among those who passed away from my brothers among the prophets were eight thousand prophets, then there was Jesus, son of Mary, then there was me. We have narrated it from Anas from another source, so al-Hafiz Abu `Abdullah al-Dhahabi told us, Abu al-Fadl ibn `Asakir told us, Imam Bakr al-Qasim ibn Abi Sa`id al-Saffar told us, Abu `Aisha bint Ahmad ibn Mansur ibn al-Saffar told us, al-Sharif Abu al-Sananik Hibat God ibn Abi al-Sahba` Muhammad ibn Haidar al-Qurashi told us, Imam al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq al-Asfarayini told us, he said: Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma`ili told us, Muhammad ibn `Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Ahmad ibn Tariq told us, Muslim ibn Khalid told us, Ziyad ibn Sa`d told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Safwan ibn Salim, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was sent after eight thousand prophets, four thousand of whom were from the Children of Israel. This is strange from this aspect, and its chain of transmission is acceptable. All of its men are known except for this Ahmad ibn Tariq, for I do not know him to be trustworthy or trustworthy, and God knows best. And the long hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari about the number of prophets, peace be upon them. Muhammad ibn Husayn al-Ajurri said: Abu Bakr Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Faryabi told us by dictation in the month of Rajab in the year two hundred and ninety-seven. Ibrahim ibn Hisham ibn Yahya al-Ghassani told us, my father told us, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I entered the mosque, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting alone, so I sat next to him and said: O Messenger of God, you have commanded me to pray. He said: Prayer is the best thing, so do it often or do it little. I said: O Messenger of God, which deeds are best? He said: Belief in God and jihad in His cause. I said: O Messenger of God, which believers are best? He said: The best of them in character. I said: O Messenger of God, which Muslim is the most Muslim? He said: He from whose tongue and hand people are safe. I said: O Messenger of God, which migration is best? He said: He who abandons evil deeds. I said: O Messenger of God, which prayer is best? He said: Long supplication. I said: O Messenger of God, which fasting is best? He said: An obligatory duty that is sufficient, and with God it is many times greater. I said: O Messenger of God, which jihad is best? He said: He who hamstrings his horse and sheds its blood. I said: O Messenger of God, which slaves are best? He said: The most valuable and most precious to their owners. I said: O Messenger of God, which charity is best? He said: The effort of one who is poor and secretly gives to a poor person. I said: O Messenger of God, which verse revealed to you is the greatest? He said: The Throne Verse. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, the seven heavens with the Throne are like a ring thrown in a desert. The superiority of the Throne over the Throne is like the superiority of the desert over the ring.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many prophets are there? He said: One hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many messengers are there? He said: Three hundred and thirteen, a great multitude, and good. I said: Who was the first of them? He said: Adam. I said: A messenger prophet? He said: Yes, God created him with His hand, and breathed into him from His spirit, and made him a tribe. Then he said: “O Abu Dharr, four are Syrians: Adam, Seth, and Enoch, who is Idris, and he was the first to write with a pen, and Noah, and four are Arabs: Hud, Shu’ayb, and Salih, and your prophet Abu Dharr, and the first prophet of the Children of Israel was Moses and the last of them was Jesus, and the first of the messengers was Adam and the last of them was Muhammad.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how many books did God send down? He said: “One hundred and four books. God sent down fifty pages to Seth, thirty pages to Enoch, ten pages to Abraham, and before that He sent down ten pages to Moses, and He sent down the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion.” He said: I said: O Messenger of God, what were the pages of Abraham? He said: "All of it, O king, the afflicted, the arrogant. I did not send you to gather the world together, but I sent you to respond to the supplication of the oppressed, for I will not respond to it even if it is from an unbeliever and there are similarities in it. And the wise person should have hours: an hour in which he communes with his Lord, an hour in which he holds himself to account, an hour in which he thinks about God's creation, and an hour in which he is alone for his need of food and drink. And the wise person should not be spiteful except for three reasons: provisions for the afterlife, or improvement of his livelihood, or pleasure in something that is not forbidden. And the wise person should be aware of his time, focused on his affairs, guarding his tongue, and whoever considers his speech as part of his deeds will speak little except in what concerns him." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, so what were the scrolls of Moses? He said: "They were all lessons. I am amazed at the one who is certain of death and yet rejoices. I am amazed at the one who is certain of destiny and yet suffers. I am amazed at the one who sees the world and its vicissitudes with its people and yet feels reassured by them. I am amazed at the one who is certain of the reckoning tomorrow and yet does not work." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, do we have in our hands anything of what was in the hands of Abraham and Moses, and what God revealed to you? He said: Yes, read, O Abu Dharr: "Indeed he has succeeded who purifies himself, And remembers the name of his Lord and prays. Rather, you prefer the life of this world, And the Hereafter is better and more lasting. Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, The scriptures of Abraham and Moses." He said: I said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: I advise you to fear God, for it is the head of your affair. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, give me more. He said: You should recite the Qur'an and remember God, for it is a remembrance for you in the heavens and a light for you on the earth....." He said: "Beware of laughing too much, for it kills the heart and takes away the light of the face." I said: "O Messenger of God, tell me more." He said: "You should engage in jihad, for it is the monasticism of my nation." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "You should be silent except for good, for it drives away Satan and helps you in your religious affairs." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Look at those below you and do not look at those above you, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the favor of God upon you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Love the poor and sit with them, for that is more likely to keep you from belittling the favor of God upon you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Maintain ties of kinship even if they sever ties with you." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Speak the truth even if it is bitter." I said: "Tell me more." He said: "Do not fear the blame of a blamer in God's cause." I said: "Tell me more." He said, “What you know about yourself keeps you away from people, and you do not find fault with them in what you love. It is enough of a defect for you to know about people what you do not know about yourself, or to find fault with them in what you love.” Then he struck my chest with his hand and said, O Abu Dharr, there is no intelligence like planning, no piety like restraint, and no lineage like good character. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ma’an bin Rafa’a, on the authority of Ali bin Yazid, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah that Abu Dharr asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned the matter of prayer, fasting, and charity, and the virtue of the Throne Verse, and there is no power or strength except with God, and the best of martyrs, and the best of slaves, and the prophethood of Adam and that he was spoken to, and the number of prophets and messengers as mentioned above. Abdullah bin Al-Imam Ahmad said: I found in my father’s book written by him: Abdul Mut’ali bin Abdul Wahhab told me, Yahya bin Saeed Al-Umawi told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Abu Al-Wadak, who said: Abu Saeed said: Do the Khawarij believe in the Antichrist? He said: I said: No. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and no prophet was sent to be followed except that he warned his nation against him, and he made clear to me about him what he did not make clear to anyone else, and he is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed, and his right eye is one-eyed and bulging and cannot be hidden as if it were phlegm on a plastered wall, and his left eye is like a shining star, with him from every tongue, and with him is a green image of Paradise in which water flows, and a black image of Hell, smoking.” We have narrated it in the section in which there is the narration of Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili on the authority of Yahya ibn Ma’in: Marwan ibn Mu’awiyah told us, Mujalid told us on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the seal of a thousand thousand prophets or more, and God did not send a prophet to his people except that he warned them against the Antichrist. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith, this is its wording with the addition of an alif, and it may have been inserted, and God knows best. The context of Imam Ahmad’s narration is more authentic and more deserving of authenticity, and the men in the chain of transmission of this hadith are not bad. This hadith was narrated by way of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Mujalid told us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the seal of a thousand prophets or more, and there is not a prophet among them who did not warn his people of the Antichrist, and he has made clear to me what was not made clear to any of them, and he is one-eyed, and your Lord is not one-eyed.” His saying: And God spoke to Moses, speaking. This is an honor for Moses, peace be upon him, with this attribute, and that is why he is called: The Speaker. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sulayman Al-Maliki told us, Masih bin Hatim told us, Abdul-Jabbar bin Abdullah told us, he said: A man came to Abu Bakr bin Ayyash and said: I heard a man reciting And God spoke to Moses, speaking. Abu Bakr said: No one recited this except an unbeliever. I recited it according to Al-A’mash, and Al-A’mash recited it according to Yahya bin Waththab, and Yahya bin Waththab recited it according to Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami, and Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami recited it according to Ali bin Abi Talib, and Ali bin Abi Talib recited it according to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And God spoke to Moses, speaking. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, may God have mercy on him, became very angry with the one who recited it like this, because he distorted the wording and meaning of the Qur’an, and this was from the Mu’tazilah who deny that God spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, or spoke to any of His creation, as we narrated from some of the Mu’tazilah that he recited: Some of the sheikhs said: And God spoke to Moses directly. He said to him: O son of a whore, what do you say about the words of God the Almighty: And when Moses came to Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him? Meaning that this does not allow for distortion or interpretation. Ibn Mardawayh said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim told us, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Bahram told us, Muhammad ibn Marzouq told us, Hani’ ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi Ja’far, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Yahya ibn Waththab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God spoke to Moses, he could see the crawling of ants on a rock in the dark night. It is authentic and was narrated by al-Hakim in his Mustadrak and Ibn Mardawayh from the hadith of Hamid ibn Qays al-A’raj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the day that his Lord spoke to Moses, he was wearing a woolen cloak, a woolen cloak, woolen trousers, and sandals made of the hide of an unslaughtered donkey. Ibn Mardawayh said with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God spoke to Moses with one hundred thousand and forty thousand words in three days, all of them commandments. When Moses heard the speech of the humans, he hated them for what he heard of the speech of the Lord Almighty. This is also a weak chain of transmission, for Juwaybir is weaker, and Ad-Dahhak did not meet Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. As for the trace that Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and others narrated on the authority of Al-Fadl bin Isa Al-Raqashi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that he said: When God spoke to Moses on the Day of Mount Sinai, He spoke to him with a speech other than the one He spoke to him on the Day He called to Him. Moses said to Him: O Lord, is this Your speech that You spoke to me? He said: No, O Moses, I spoke to You with the strength of ten thousand tongues, and I have the strength of all tongues, and I am stronger than that. When Moses returned to the Children of Israel, they said: O Moses, describe to us the speech of the Most Merciful. He said: I cannot do it. They said: Then He made it appear to us. He said: Have you not heard the sound of thunderbolts? It is close to them but not to them. This is a weak chain of transmission, for this Al-Fadl Al-Raqashi is extremely weak. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Juz’ bin Jabir Al-Jathami, on the authority of Ka’b, who said: When God spoke to Moses in all languages, Moses said to Him: O Lord, is this Your speech? He said: No, and if I spoke to You with My speech, it would not be right. He said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that resembles Your speech? He said: No, and the most similar of My creation to My speech is the most similar of the thunderbolts you hear. This is attributed to Ka’b Al-Ahbar, and he is narrating from the previous books that contain the stories of the Children of Israel, and in them are the good and the bad. And His statement: Messengers, bringing good tidings and warnings, meaning they bring good tidings to those who obey God and follow His pleasure, and warn those who disobey His command and deny His messengers of punishment and torment. And His statement: “So that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise,” meaning that the Most High sent down His books and sent His messengers with good tidings and warnings, and explained what He loves and is pleased with from what He hates and rejects, so that no excuse would remain for the one who makes an excuse, as the Most High said: “And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, ‘Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger so we could have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced.’” And likewise His statement: And had not a disaster struck them for what their hands had put forth, the verse. It was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No one is more jealous than God, and for that reason He has forbidden indecencies, both apparent and hidden. No one loves praise more than God Almighty, and for that reason He has praised Himself. No one loves excuses more than God, and for that reason He sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners.” In another version: For that reason He sent His messengers and revealed His books.
4:166: Since the Almighty's statement: Indeed, We have revealed to you to the end of the context, includes proof of his prophethood, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a response to those who denied his prophethood from among the polytheists and the People of the Book, God Almighty said: But God bears witness to what has been revealed to you meaning, even if those who disbelieved in it, who lied to you and opposed you, God bears witness to you that you are His Messenger to whom He revealed the Book, which is the Great Qur'an, Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is sent down by One Who is Wise and Praiseworthy. For this reason, He said: He sent it down with His knowledge meaning in His knowledge that He wanted to inform the servants of the clear proofs, guidance, and criterion, and what God loves and is pleased with, and what He hates and rejects, and what it contains of knowledge of the unseen, of the past and the future, and what it contains of mentioning His sacred attributes that no sent prophet or close angel knows except that God informs him of them, as God Almighty said: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills and He said: And they do not encompass Him in knowledge. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Al-Hasan bin Sahl Al-Jaafari and Khazz bin Al-Mubarak told us, they said: Imran bin Uyaynah told us, Ata bin Al-Saib told us, he said: Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami taught me the Qur’an, and when one of us recited the Qur’an to him, he would say: You have taken the knowledge of God, and no one today is better than you except through deeds, then he would recite His statement: He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and sufficient is God as a witness. His statement: And the angels bear witness means the truth of what came to you and was revealed to you and sent down to you along with God’s testimony to that, and sufficient is God as a witness. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to them: By God, I know that you know that I am the Messenger of God. They said: We do not know that. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you. He sent it down with His knowledge.” And His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God have certainly strayed far astray means that they disbelieved in themselves, so they did not follow the truth, and they sought to avert people from following it and emulating it. They have departed from the truth and strayed from it, and have gone far and vastly away from it. Then the Almighty informed about His judgment on the disbelievers in His verses, His Book, and His Messenger, who are unjust to themselves by doing so and by averting people from His way, committing His sins, and violating His prohibitions, that He will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path meaning a path to goodness, except the path of Hell and this is an isolated exception, therein to abide forever the verse. Then the Almighty said: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you meaning that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, has come to you with guidance, the religion of truth, and a clear explanation from God Almighty, so believe in what he has brought you and follow him, and it will be better for you. Then He said: And if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, meaning He is independent of you and your faith, and He is not harmed by your disbelief, as God Almighty said: “And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy,” and He said here: And God is Knowing, meaning of who among you deserves guidance, so He guides him, and who among you deserves misguidance, so He misguides him, Wise, meaning in His words, actions, law, and destiny.

Muhammad bin Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Muhammad, on the authority of Ikrimah or Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to them: By God, I know that you know that I am the Messenger of God. They said: We do not know that. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “But God bears witness to what He has revealed to you. He sent it down with His knowledge.” And His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God have certainly strayed far astray means that they disbelieved in themselves, so they did not follow the truth, and they sought to avert people from following it and emulating it. They have departed from the truth and strayed from it, and have gone far and vastly away from it. Then the Almighty informed about His judgment on the disbelievers in His verses, His Book, and His Messenger, who are unjust to themselves by doing so and by averting people from His way, committing His sins, and violating His prohibitions, that He will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path meaning a path to goodness, except the path of Hell and this is an isolated exception, therein to abide forever the verse. Then the Almighty said: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you meaning that Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, has come to you with guidance, the religion of truth, and a clear explanation from God Almighty, so believe in what he has brought you and follow him, and it will be better for you. Then He said: And if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, meaning He is independent of you and your faith, and He is not harmed by your disbelief, as God Almighty said: “And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy,” and He said here: And God is Knowing, meaning of who among you deserves guidance, so He guides him, and who among you deserves misguidance, so He misguides him, Wise, meaning in His words, actions, law, and destiny.

For this reason, He said: He sent it down with His knowledge meaning in His knowledge that He wanted to inform the servants of the clear proofs, guidance, and criterion, and what God loves and is pleased with, and what He hates and rejects, and what it contains of knowledge of the unseen, of the past and the future, and what it contains of mentioning His sacred attributes that no sent prophet or close angel knows except that God informs him of them, as God Almighty said: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills and He said: And they do not encompass Him in knowledge. 4:171: God the Almighty forbids the People of the Book from exaggeration and flattery, and this is common among Christians, as they went too far in the case of Jesus until they raised him above the status that God gave him, so they removed him from the realm of prophethood, until they took him as a god besides God, worshipping him as they worship Him. Rather, they went to extremes in their followers and partisans who claimed to be of his religion, so they claimed infallibility for them, and followed them in everything they said, whether it was true or false, misguidance or guidance, correct or false. For this reason God the Almighty said: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God (al-An'am 11:1). Imam Ahmad said: Hisham told us that Al-Zuhri claimed on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Mas'ud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Umar, that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Do not flatter me as the Christians flattered Jesus, son of Mary. I am only a servant, so say: The servant of God and His Messenger." Then he and Ali ibn al-Madini narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, in the same way, and its wording is: I am only a slave, so say the slave of God and His Messenger. Ali ibn al-Madini said: This is a hadith with a sound chain of transmission, and thus al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of al-Hamidi, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of al-Zuhri, with the same wording: I am only a slave, so say the slave of God and His Messenger. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Banani, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that a man said: O Muhammad, O our master and son of our master, and the best of us and the son of the best of us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, stick to what you say and do not let Satan lead you astray. I am Muhammad bin Abdullah, the servant of God and His Messenger. By God, I do not like you to raise me above the status that God Almighty has given me.” This is unique in its transmission from this source. And the Almighty said: And do not say about God except the truth meaning do not fabricate against Him and make a wife or a son for Him. God, the Almighty, is far above that, and He is transcendent, holy and unique in His leadership, pride and greatness. There is no god but Him, and no lord but Him. That is why He said: The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was only a messenger of God and His word which He cast into Mary and a spirit from Him. That is, he is only a servant of God’s servants and a creation of His creation. He said to him: Be, and he was. He is a messenger of His messengers and His word which He cast into Mary, that is, He created him with the word with which Gabriel, peace be upon him, was sent to Mary, so he breathed into her from His spirit with the permission of his Lord, the Almighty, and so Jesus was with His permission, the Almighty, and that breath which He breathed was in the pocket of her garment, so it descended until it entered her vagina like the sperm of a father and mother. All are created by God, the Almighty, and that is why it was said of Jesus: He is the word of God and a spirit from Him, because he did not have a father from whom he was born, but rather he arose from the word with which He said to him: Be, and he was. And the spirit with which He sent Gabriel said about it: “The Messiah, the son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; many were the messengers that passed away before him. His mother was a woman of truth. They both used to eat food.” And God Almighty said: “The likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was.” And God Almighty said: And she who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit and made her and her son a sign for the worlds. And God Almighty said: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity to the end of the surah. And God Almighty said, informing about the Messiah: He is no more than a servant upon whom We bestowed favor verse. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, And His Word which He cast into Mary and a spirit from Him is His saying: Be and it was. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan al-Wasiti told us: I heard Shadh bin Yahya say about the statement of God, And His Word which He cast into Mary and a spirit from Him, he said: The Word did not become Jesus, but rather Jesus became through the Word. This is better than what Ibn Jarir claimed in his statement, He cast it into Mary, meaning He informed her of it, as he claimed in his statement, When the angels said, ‘O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a Word from Him,’ meaning He informs you of a Word from Him, and He makes that like the statement of God, And you did not expect that the Book would be revealed to you except as a mercy from your Lord. Rather, the correct statement is that it is the Word that Gabriel brought to Mary, so he breathed into her by God’s permission and Jesus, peace be upon him, became. Al-Bukhari said: Sadaqah bin Al-Fadl told us, Al-Walid told us, Al-Awza’i told us, Umair bin Hani’ told us, Junada bin Abi Umayya told us, on the authority of Ubadah bin Al-Samit, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever bears witness that there is no god but God, alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that Jesus is the servant of God and His Messenger and His Word which He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise is true and Hell is true, God will admit him into Paradise regardless of his deeds.” Al-Waleed said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir told me on the authority of Umair ibn Hani’ on the authority of Junada, who added, From the eight gates of Paradise, he enters from whichever one he wishes. Muslim narrated it in the same way on the authority of Dawud ibn Rashid on the authority of al-Waleed on the authority of Ibn Jabir, and from another chain of transmission on the authority of al-Awza’i on his authority. So his saying in the verse and the hadith, and a spirit from Him, is like his saying, And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him, meaning from His creation and from Him. And from is not for partiality as the Christians say, upon them be the successive curses of God. Rather, it is for the beginning of the goal as in the other verse. Mujahid said in his saying, and a spirit from Him, meaning and a messenger from Him. And others said: and love from Him. The first is more apparent, which is that it is created from a created spirit, and the spirit was attributed to God in a way of honor, just as the she-camel and the House were attributed to God in His saying, This is the she-camel of God, and in His saying, And purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, and as was narrated in the authentic hadith, Then enter upon my Lord in His Abode, He attributed it to Him in an honorary addition. This is It's all one thing and one style. And His saying: So believe in God and His Messenger means believe that God is One, Unique, without a son or a wife, and know and be certain that Jesus is the servant and messenger of God, and for this reason the Almighty said: And do not say, ‘Three’ meaning do not make Jesus and his mother partners with God, God is far above that, and this verse is like the one in Surat Al-Ma’idah where the Almighty says: Indeed they have disbelieved who say, ‘God is the third of three.’ And there is no god except one God, and as He said at the end of the mentioned surah: And when God said, ‘O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, ‘Take me as a god,’ and He said at the beginning of it: Indeed they have disbelieved who say, ‘God is the Messiah, son of Mary,’ the verse. So the Christians, may God’s curses be upon them, because of their ignorance, have no control, and their disbelief has no limit, rather their sayings and their misguidance are widespread, some of them believe him to be a god, some of them believe him to be a partner, and some of them believe him to be a son, and they are many sects with different opinions and inconsistent sayings. Some theologians said well when they said: If ten Christians gathered together, they would separate into eleven opinions. One of their famous scholars, Saeed bin Batrik, mentioned that he left Alexandria around the year 400 AH, that they had gathered in the great council in which they had concluded the great trust that they had, which was only a small, petty betrayal, and that was during the days of Constantine, the builder of the famous city, and that they had disagreed about it in a way that was not controlled or limited, so they were more than two thousand bishops, so they were many parties, fifty of them on a statement, twenty on a statement, a hundred on a statement, seventy on a statement, and more and less. When he saw a group of them that had exceeded three hundred by eighteen people, and they had agreed on a statement, the king took it and supported it and confirmed it, and he was a clever philosopher, and he eliminated all other statements, and the plot of those three hundred and eighteen was organized, and churches were built for them, and they established books and laws for them, and they created in them the trust that they teach the young boys to believe in it and baptize them on it, and the followers of these are the royalists. Then they met in a second council, and the Jacobites took place among them, then a third council, and the Nestorians took place among them, and all of these groups affirmed the three hypostases in Christ and differed in how that was done, and in the divinity and humanity, according to their claim, did they unite, or did they not unite, or mixed, or were dissolved in it in three articles, and each of them disbelieves in the other group, and we disbelieve in the three, and for this reason the Almighty said: Stop, it is better for you meaning it is better for you God is only one God, exalted is He above having a son meaning He is exalted and sanctified far above that, To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs meaning everyone is His kingdom and His creation, and everything in them is His servants and they are under His management and control, and He is Disposer of affairs over everything, so how could He have a wife and a son from them, as He said in the other verse: “Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son?” The verse, and the Almighty said: “And they say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son.’ You have certainly done a thing monstrously. The heavens almost burst from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse.” This is because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is none in the heavens and earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them precisely. And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.”
4:172: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Hisham told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata', on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement, He will not disdain means he will not be arrogant. Qatada said: The Messiah will not be ashamed to be a slave of God, nor will the angels brought near. Some of those who preferred the angels over humans used this verse as evidence when he said, nor the angels brought near. There is no evidence for that, because he only connected the angels to the Messiah, because disdain means abstention, and the angels are more capable of that than the Messiah, so that is why he said, nor the angels brought near. And it does not follow from their being stronger and more capable of abstention that they are better. It was said: They were mentioned because they took gods with God, as Christ did. So God Almighty informed us that they are servants of His servants and creations of His creation, as God Almighty said: And they say, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants. (Surat al-Baqarah 2:170), and for this reason He said: And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them all together to Himself. That is, He will gather them to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and He will judge between them with His just judgment in which He is not unjust or unfair. That is, He said: But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their reward in full and increase them from His bounty. That is, He will give them rewards according to the extent of their righteous deeds, and He will increase them from His bounty, kindness, vast mercy, and grace. Ibn Mardawayh narrated on the authority of Baqiyyah on the authority of Ismail ibn Abdullah al-Kindi, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. He said: Their rewards. He will admit them to Paradise. “And He will increase them from His favor. He said: Intercession for those who deserve Hellfire, for those who did good to them in their worldly life. This is an unproven chain of transmission. If it is narrated from Ibn Mas’ud as a continuation of the hadith, then it is good. As for those who disdain and are arrogant, meaning they refrain from obeying God and worshipping Him and are arrogant about that. He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper, like His statement: Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] humiliated, meaning humiliated, contemptible, and abject, just as they were refusing and arrogant.

4:174: The Almighty says, addressing all people and informing them that a great proof has come to them from Him, which is the conclusive evidence for the excuse and the argument that removes doubt. For this reason He said: And We have sent down to you a clear light, meaning a clear light on the truth. Ibn Jurayj and others said: It is the Qur’an. But as for those who believed in God and held fast to Him, meaning they combined the two stations of worship and reliance on God in all their affairs. Ibn Jurayj said: They believed in God and held fast to the Qur’an. Narrated by Ibn Jarir: Then He will admit them to His mercy and bounty. That is, He will have mercy on them and admit them to Paradise, and He will increase their reward, multiply their rewards, and raise their ranks out of His bounty and kindness to them. And guide them to Himself on a straight path. That is, a clear, straight, straight path, with no crookedness or deviation. This is the description of the believers in this world and the hereafter. In this world, they are on the path of righteousness and safety in all beliefs and actions, and in the hereafter, they are on the straight path of God that leads to the gardens of Paradise. In the hadith of Al-Harith Al-A’war, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The Qur’an is the straight path of God and the strong rope of God. The hadith was presented in full at the beginning of the interpretation. All praise and thanks be to God.

4:176: Al-Bukhari said: Sulayman bin Harb told us, Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard Al-Bara’ say: The last surah to be revealed was Bara’ah, and the last verses to be revealed were: They ask you for a fatwa. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir ibn `Abdullah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me while I was sick and out of my mind. He performed ablution and then poured water over me, or he said: They poured it over him, and I regained my senses. I said: No one inherits from me except those who are not related to me, so how about the inheritance? Then God revealed the verse of inheritance. They included it in the two Sahihs on the authority of Shu`bah, and the group narrated it on the authority of Sufyan ibn `Uyaynah on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, and in some wordings, then the verse of inheritance was revealed: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to me,” the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn `Abdullah ibn Yazid told us, Sufyan told us, and Abu al-Zubayr said: He means Jabir, it was revealed regarding “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are not related to me,” and it seems that the meaning of the statement - and God knows best - is that they ask you about those who are not related to me, “Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning them,” so the aforementioned indicates what is abandoned. We have already discussed Kalalah and its derivation, and that it is taken from the crown that surrounds the head from its sides. For this reason, most scholars have interpreted it as someone who dies without having a son or a father. Some people say that Kalalah is someone who has no son, as indicated by this verse: If a man dies and leaves no son. The ruling on Kalalah was unclear to the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him, as it was proven from him in the two Sahihs that he said: There are three things that I wish the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) had entrusted to us with a covenant that we could adhere to: the grandfather, Kalalah, and a chapter on usury. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ma`dan ibn Abi Talhah, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: I did not ask the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about anything more than I asked him about Kalalah until he stabbed me in the chest with his finger and said: The verse of summer at the end of Surat al-Nisa is sufficient for you. This is how he narrated it in an abbreviated form, and Muslim narrated it in a longer form than this. Another path Imam Ahmad said: Abu Naim told us, Malik, meaning Ibn Mughul, told us, saying: I heard Al-Fadl Ibn Amr, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Omar, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Kalalah, and he said: The verse of summer is sufficient for you, so he said: For me to have asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it is more beloved to me than for me to have red camels. This is a good chain of transmission, except that there is a break in it between Ibrahim and Omar, as he did not meet him. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about Kalalah. He said: The verse of summer is sufficient for you. This is a good chain of transmission. It was narrated by Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash. It seems that what is meant by the verse of summer is that it was revealed in the summer season, and God knows best. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, guided him to understand it, for it is sufficient, he forgot to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about its meaning. That is why he said: For me to have asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it is more beloved to me than to have red camels. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Jarir Ash-Shaibani told us on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, who said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Kalalah, and he said: Has God not made that clear? Then they ask you for a legal opinion was revealed. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that Abu Bakr As-Siddiq said in his sermon: “Behold, the verse that was revealed at the beginning of Surat An-Nisa’ concerning the inheritance shares, God revealed it regarding the child and the parent, and the second verse, He revealed it regarding the husband and the wife and the brothers from the mother’s side, and the verse with which he concluded Surat An-Nisa’, He revealed it regarding the brothers and sisters from the father and the mother, and the verse with which he concluded Surat Al-Anfal, He revealed it regarding the relatives, some of them are closer to others in the Book of God than the relatives of the agnates.” Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Mention the speech on its meaning And to God is the help sought and upon Him is reliance. The Almighty said: If a man perishes meaning he dies. God the Almighty said: Everything will perish except His Face everything will perish and nothing will remain except God the Almighty, as He said: Everything on it will perish, but the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain. His statement: He has no children is held by those who believe that the absence of a father is not a condition of kalalah, but rather the absence of a child is sufficient for the existence of kalalah. This is a narration on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, narrated by Ibn Jarir on his authority with a sound chain of transmission to him. However, what is referred to is the opinion of the majority and the ruling of al-Siddiq, that he is the one who has no children and no father. This is indicated by his statement: And he has a sister, for her is half of what he left. If there was a father with her, she would not inherit anything because he excludes her by consensus. This indicates that he is the one who has no children according to the text of the Qur’an and no father according to the text upon reflection as well, because the sister is not entitled to half with the father, and she does not have any inheritance at all. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ narrated to us, Abu Bakr bin Abdullah narrated to us, on the authority of Makhul, Atiyah, Hamza and Rashid, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, that he was asked about a husband and a sister from the father and mother, so he gave the husband half and the sister half, so he was spoken to about that and he said: I was present with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ruled on that. Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source, and Ibn Jarir and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they used to say about the deceased who left behind a daughter and a sister, that the sister has nothing, based on his saying: If a man dies and has no children and has a sister, then she has half of what he left behind. He said: So if he left behind a daughter, then he has left behind a son, so the sister has nothing. The majority disagreed with them and said in this matter that the daughter has half by fixed share, and the sister has the other half by agnatic kinship, based on evidence other than this verse, and this verse stipulated that she should be given a fixed share in this case. As for her inheritance by agnatic kinship, when al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Sulayman on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of al-Aswad, he said: Muadh bin Jabal ruled among us during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that half goes to the daughter and half goes to the sister, then Sulayman said: He ruled. In us, and it was not mentioned during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In Sahih al-Bukhari also, on the authority of Hazil bin Shurahbil, he said: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari was asked about a daughter, a son’s daughter, and a sister. He said: For the daughter is half, and for the sister is half. And he went to Ibn Mas’ud, so he would follow me. So he asked Ibn Mas’ud and informed him of what Abu Musa had said. He said: Then you have gone astray, and I am not among those who are guided. I rule in it as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled: half for the daughter, and for the son’s daughter is a sixth to complete two-thirds, and what remains is for the sister. So we went to Abu Musa and informed him of what Ibn Mas’ud had said. He said: Do not ask me as long as this scholar is among you. And his saying: And he inherits her if she has no children means that the brother inherits all of her money if she dies as a distant relative, and she has no children, that is, no father, because if she had a father, the brother would not inherit anything. If we assume that there is someone with a share, his share is given to him, such as a husband or a brother from the mother, and the rest is given to the brother, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give the shares to those entitled to them, and whatever is left behind is for the closest male relative. And his saying: If there are two sisters, then for them are two-thirds of what he left means that if the one who dies as a distant relative has two sisters, then two-thirds are given to them, and so is what is more than two sisters in their ruling. From here the group took the ruling of two daughters, just as the ruling of sisters from the daughters was derived in his saying: If there are more than two women, then for them are two-thirds of what he left. And His statement: And if there are brothers, both men and women, the male shall have twice the share of the female. This is the ruling for agnates, whether sons or sons, or brothers, if their males and females are together, the male shall be given twice the share of the female. And His statement, God makes clear to you, means He imposes upon you His obligations, defines His limits, and explains His laws to you. And His statement, lest you go astray, means lest you go astray from the truth after the explanation. And God is Knowing of all things, meaning He is All-Knowing of the consequences of matters, their interests, and what is good in them for His servants, and what each of the relatives deserves according to his closeness to the deceased. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ya`qub told me, Ibn `Ulayyah told me, Ibn `Awn told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: They were on a journey, and the head of Hudhayfah’s camel was at the rear of the Messenger of God’s camel, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the head of `Umar’s camel was at the rear of Hudhayfah’s camel. He said: Then the verse “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion concerning those who are left behind as a result of kinship.” was revealed. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met Hudhayfah, and Hudhayfah met `Umar. Later, `Umar asked Hudhayfah about her, and he said: By God, you are foolish if you thought that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met her. So I met her as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met her. By God, I will never tell you anything more about her. `Umar used to say: O God, if you made her clear to him, then she was not made clear to me. This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it. He also narrated it on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Yahya on the authority of `Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, in a similar manner, and it is disconnected between Ibn Sirin and Hudhayfah. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Amr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Yusuf bin Hammad Al-Maani and Muhammad bin Marzouq told us: Abdul-A’la bin Abdul-A’la told us, Hisham bin Hassan told us on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Hudhayqah, on the authority of his father, who said: The verse of Kalala was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on a journey. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped and saw Hudhayfah and the head of Hudhayfah’s she-camel at the back of the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, mount, so he met it with him. Hudhayfah looked and saw Umar, may God be pleased with him, so he met it with him. When Umar was in the caliphate, Umar looked into Kalala, so he called Hudhayfah and asked him about it. Hudhayfah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met it with me, so I met it with you as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met me. By God, I am truthful, and by God, I will never tell you anything more. Then Al-Bazzar said: We do not know anyone who narrated this hadith except Hudhayfah, and we do not know of any chain of transmission from Hudhayfah other than this chain of transmission, and no one narrated it from Hisham except Abd Al-A’la, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in the same way from the hadith of Abd Al-A’la. Uthman bin Abi Shaybah said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that Umar asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, how the kalalah are inherited. He said: Then God revealed, They ask you verse, he said: It was as if Umar did not understand, so he said to Hafsa: If you see a good mood from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then ask him about it, so she saw a good mood from him and asked him about it, and he said: Your father mentioned this to you, but I do not think your father knows it, he said: So Umar used to say: I do not think I know it. The Messenger of God said what he said. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, then he narrated it through the chain of transmission of Ibn Uyaynah, and on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Tawus, that Umar ordered Hafsah to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about kalalah, so he dictated it to her on one shoulder, and he said: Who ordered you to do this, Umar? I do not think he will establish it, or is the verse of summer not sufficient for him? And the verse of summer in An-Nisa’ And if a man or woman leaves a kalalah, or a woman, so when they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the verse that is the conclusion of An-Nisa’ was revealed, so Umar threw the shoulder, that is what he said in this hadith, and it is mursal. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kuraib told us, Uthman told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, who said: Umar took a shoulder and gathered the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and then said: I will pass judgment on the issue of the kalalah in a manner that women will talk about in their chambers. Then a snake came out of the house and they dispersed. He said: If God, the Almighty, had willed to complete this matter, He would have completed it. This is a sound chain of transmission. Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah Al-Naysaburi said: Ali bin Muhammad bin Uqbah Al-Shaibani told us in Kufa, Al-Haytham bin Khalid told us, Abu Nu'aym told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, I heard Muhammad bin Talhah bin Yazid bin Rukanah narrating on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, who said: It would be dearer to me to have asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about three things: Who will be the caliph after him? And about a people who said: We acknowledge the zakat on our wealth but we do not pay it to you. Is it permissible to fight them? And about the kalalah. Then he said: Its chain of transmission is sound according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it. Then he narrated with this chain of transmission to Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of Umar, who said: Three things that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have been dearer to me than the world and what is in it: the caliphate, the kalalah, and usury. Then he said: It is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, although they did not include it. And with this chain of transmission to Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, he said: I heard Sulayman al-Ahwal narrating on the authority of Tawus, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: I was the last person to see Umar, so I heard him say: The statement is what you said. I said: What did you say? He said: I said: The kalalah is the one who has no children. Then he said: It is authentic according to their conditions, although they did not include it. And thus Ibn Mardawayh narrated it on the authority of Zama’ah ibn Salih, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, and Sulayman al-Ahwal on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: I was the last person to see Umar ibn al-Khattab, he said: I and Abu Bakr differed regarding the kalalah, and the statement is what I said. He said: It was mentioned that Umar shared between the brothers on the mother’s and father’s side and between the brothers on the mother’s side in one-third if they were together, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, disagreed with him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Muhammad ibn Hamid al-Amri told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, that Umar wrote a letter about the grandfather and the agnates, and he kept asking God for guidance, saying: O God, if you know good in it, then carry it out. Then when he was stabbed, he called for a letter and it was erased, and no one knew what he had written in it. He said: I had written a letter about the grandfather and the agnates, and I was asking God for guidance about it, so I decided to leave you as you were. Ibn Jarir said: It was narrated on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, that he said: I am ashamed to contradict Abu Bakr in it, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, used to say: It is everything except the child and the parent. This is what Abu Bakr said, and the majority of the Companions, the Followers, and the Imams in ancient and modern times agreed upon it. It is the doctrine of the Four Imams and the Seven Jurists, and the opinion of the scholars of all the regions. It is what the Qur’an indicates, as God guided us to, that He made that clear and explained in His saying: “God makes it clear to you, lest you go astray. And God is Knowing of all things.” And God knows best.
